papers.title: A rigid commensurate host and a defect that switches: vacancies in the frustrated alternating spin-(1, 1/2) Heisenberg chain
papers.abstract: The alternating spin-$(1,\tfrac12)$ Heisenberg chain with a frustrating next-nearest-neighbor coupling $J_2$ loses its Lieb--Mattis moment through a discontinuous transition to a singlet whose nature was left open. Using an SU(2)-symmetric density-matrix renormalization group, in which the total spin is a quantum-number label, we identify that phase and follow a single vacancy through it. The total spin collapses directly from $S=L/4$ to $S=0$, with no partially polarized window. The singlet phase is critical: its singlet--triplet gap closes as $1/L$, its entanglement entropy grows logarithmically with a central charge $c\simeq1.8$, and its modulation wavevector, extrapolated from $L=80$ to $200$, is commensurate at $3π/4$ and independent of $J_2$ to $5\times10^{-5}$. Removing the central $S=1$ site switches the ground state of the doped chain from a triplet to a singlet at $J_2^{\ast}=0.3068(3)$, where the host shows no feature; the triplet is not bound to the vacancy but spread over one of the two segments it leaves. The transmission of correlations through the vacancy saturates at a finite value below $J_2^{\ast}$, $T(\infty)=0.102(15)$ and $0.036(9)$ at $J_2=0.28$ and $0.30$, and the cut-chain law $T\propto L^{-1}$ is excluded on both sides. We also show that the longitudinal correlator is not an observable in a triplet sector.

papers.title: Neural Computation Runs on Dissipative Structures Under Cyclic Calibration: A Systems Perspective on Sleep
papers.abstract: Biological function operates far from thermodynamic equilibrium, sustained by metastable structures that continuously cycle through synthesis, function execution, and degradation--consuming energy and exporting entropy in the process. Neural computation exemplifies this dissipative organization, relying on low-entropy structures engaged in dynamic processes that define key information transfer and processing parameters such as gain, threshold, and integration time. This perspective proposes that sleep serves as a systemic recalibration phase required to reset crucial signaling parameters that drift during dissipative processing. During wakefulness, neural activity progressively consumes and disrupts the organization of the very substrate from which it emerges, leading to parameter drift and reduced computational precision. Sleep maintains computational accuracy across activity cycles by recalibrating function-structure coupling--that is, by counterbalancing entropic drift. Rather than explaining the experimentally observed sleep need through homeostatic regulation of unknown physiological variables, this perspective reframes it as an emergent property of neural computation under thermodynamic constraints.

papers.title: From Adults to Children: Benchmarking Foundation Models for Chest X-Ray Classification under Domain Shift
papers.abstract: Foundation models have shown significant potential across diverse fields and have been applied to medical imaging, but their robustness across patient populations remains unclear. In this work, we investigate foundation models' ability to generalize from adult to pediatric chest X-ray classification. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first benchmark to compare multiple foundation models under a common adult-to-pediatric evaluation setting while also analyzing the effect of adaptation depth. We harmonize VinDr-CXR and PediCXR into a five-label classification task and evaluate six foundation models and two CNN baselines. All models are adapted using adult data only and tested in both the in-domain and pediatric domains using linear probing, partial fine-tuning, and full fine-tuning. The benchmark reveals a clear and consistent trend: all models suffer a substantial performance degradation when transferred from adult to pediatric data, with drops exceeding 10 percentage points. While Macro-AUROC values reach approximately 92% on the adult test set, performance decreases to around 78% on the pediatric domain. Another important finding is that increasing the depth of adaptation improves pediatric performance on average, although the effect varies across models. Moreover, strong in-domain performance does not necessarily indicate greater robustness to domain shift.

papers.title: Descending Everest, Part I: Oracle Complexity of Convex Optimization under $(L_0,L_1)$-Smoothness
papers.abstract: For convex $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth functions, the curvature may grow together with the gradient norm. Therefore, even when $\|x^0-x^*\|\le R$, the gradient and the optimality gap at the starting point may be exponentially large in $L_1R$, and the bound $\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}$, known for the accelerated method on functions with Lipschitz gradient, no longer describes the complexity of the problem. We determine the oracle complexity of this class for arbitrary deterministic first-order methods: for $L_0R^2/\varepsilon\ge1$, the optimal number of oracle calls $N$ satisfies $1+N=\widetildeΘ(\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}+L_1R)$. The upper bound reads $O(\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}+(1+L_1R)\log(2+L_1R))$: the method first passes through the large-gradient regime in $O(1+L_1R)$ iterations with an inexact line search, and then the standard accelerated method with a constant stepsize takes over. The lower bound is obtained by means of chains and the orthogonal invariance principle on functions conjugate to strongly convex functions on a polytope. If the initial optimality gap is at most $4\varepsilon$, the optimal bound becomes $1+N=\widetildeΘ(\sqrt{L_0R^2/\varepsilon}+(L_1R)^{2/3})$.

papers.title: A simultaneous variant of the Hall-Paige theorem and applications
papers.abstract: For $k\geq 1$ , we say that a finite group $G$ satisfies property $\mathcal P_k$ if, for every $β_1,\ldots,β_k\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)$, there exists a bijection $f$ of $G$ such that each map $g\mapsto β_i(g)f(g)$ is a bijection. For $k=1$ this is equivalent to the classical Hall--Paige complete mapping property. We prove that if $p$ is the smallest prime divisor of $|G|$, then $G$ satisfies $\mathcal P_k$ for every $k<p-1$ and we show that this bound is sharp. For finite abelian $p$-groups, the bijection $f$ may moreover be chosen to be an automorphism, and for noncyclic homocyclic $p$-groups this remains true for $k=p-1$. Finally, we interpret $\mathcal P_k$ in terms of common transversals and common orthogonal mates of Latin squares generated from automorphisms and the Cayley table of a finite group $G$.

papers.title: A Response to the Reply Presented in "A Fair Comparison of Sliding-Mode and Immersion-and-Invariance Observers"
papers.abstract: In response to the reply presented in [Muñoz-Vázquez and Sánchez-Torres(2026)], this technical report extends the experimental evaluation of position-feedback velocity observers and adaptive tracking controllers for a pendular system with nonlinear friction reported in [Cervantes-Pérez et al.(2026)]. The immersion and invariance (I&I) adaptive control scheme proposed in [Romero et al.(2025)], whose gains are tuned according to the guidelines presented in [Ortega et al.(2025)], is compared with a control scheme employing the adaptive modi?ed super-twisting observer of [Dávila et al.(2006)], whose observer gains are selected according to the guidelines proposed in [Muñoz-Vázquez and Sánchez-Torres(2026)]. Although these "tuning guidelines" attenuate chattering in certain scenarios, the experimental results reported here show that they do not eliminate it in general.

papers.title: Theory of Dispersion and Exchange Interactions Subjected to Surface Roughness in Application to Signal Transmission through a Nanoswitch
papers.abstract: We present the theoretical description of a resistive nanoswitch designated for a change-over between the two operation modes by calculating the electri elastic, dispersion (van der Waals and Casimir), and also exchange repulsive forces in its configuration with an account of surface roughness. The dispersion forces are described by means of the Lifshitz theory and, at the shortest separations between the interacting bodies, where this theory is inapplicable, by the method of additive summation of the interatomic potentials corrected for the role of the effects of nonadditivity. The exchange repulsion is also found by a summation of the interatomic potentials and using the proximity force approximation. It is shown that the nanoswitch possesses the equilibrium closest separation between a cantilever tip and a ground plate calculated as a function of the actuation voltage and operates in a cyclic manner with no pull-in when this voltage is switched on and off. We have found the tunnel current between a cantilever tip and a plate and investigated distortions appearing in the signal transmitted through a nanoswitch. According to our results, the amplitude distortions arising in the low-frequency information signal can be made sufficiently small by increasing a difference between the amplitudes of the carrier and information signals. Possible applications of the obtained results are discussed.

papers.title: A number field extension of Ramanujan's identity and its integral representation via the generalized Riemann $Ξ$-function
papers.abstract: On pages 219--220 of Ramanujan's Lost Notebook appears an intriguing modular transformation whose integral representation is expressed in terms of the Riemann $Ξ$-function. In this paper, we establish a number field analogue of this identity. We also obtain an integral representation for the transformation formula associated with the functional equation of the higher power of the Dedekind zeta function recently studied by the present author and Maji. Interestingly, we recover Hardy's integral representation of the well-known Jacobi theta relation involving the Riemann $Ξ$-function. We further obtain a number-field analogue of the extended Ramanujan--Koshliakov formula established by Dixit.

papers.title: AI Consilium: a Benchmark of LLM Clinical Multidisciplinary Second Opinions
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate differential diagnoses for complex cases, but a useful second opinion must also be factually grounded, clinically coherent, actionable, and safe. We developed a multidimensional benchmark using 300 diagnostically resolved NEJM--MedQA cases: 110 for physician reference ratings and Judge calibration and 190 for held-out evaluation. Eight single-model pipelines generated independent role-specific opinions and interactive-consilium reports under free-form and structured clinical-reasoning conditions. A physician-calibrated LLM Judge evaluated 3,040 final reports and the corresponding structured primary-role outputs. Model identity separated report quality more strongly than response format. Structured final reports had higher overall mean scores in seven of eight model pipelines, with their clearest advantage in management (2.740 vs. 2.436). Compared with the structured pre-consilium primary-role opinion, the complete structured synthesis had higher pooled scores across all five shared criteria, with the largest increases in problem prioritization, factual grounding, and reasoning coherence. GPT-5.6-Sol led every evaluated component and reached consensus in the fewest review rounds. These findings show that the benchmark can distinguish model capability, the contribution of multidisciplinary synthesis, criterion-specific effects of response structure, deliberation dynamics, and inference requirements within one common-case evaluation.

authors.name: Ivan I. Panin
authors.institution: St. Petersburg Department of Steklov Institute of Mathematics

authors.name: Mikhail Yu. Valkov
authors.institution: Ministry of Health of the Russian Federation

papers.title: Realization Divergence in Multi-Provider Quantum Computing: A Pre-Registered Study of What Survives Measurement
papers.abstract: Quantum programs pass through compilers, transpilers and vendor services before execution. However, the distance between what was written and what runs is rarely measured. We call this distance realization divergence: the observable difference in how an identical source circuit is realized and behaves across quantum software stacks. We report a hardware study across three vendors and four devices, combining pre-registered predictions with explicitly identified exploratory analyses and amendments. In a compilation experiment with assigned placement policies, embedding radius correlates with two-qubit overhead at Spearman 0.805, against 0.492 for circuit size. Under a fixed lowest-index policy, an eight-qubit Bernstein-Vazirani circuit exhibits greater execution divergence than a twelve-qubit circuit on IQM Emerald. The opposite ordering occurs on IQM Garnet. Both comparisons replicate across two repetitions with disjoint confidence intervals. These results support a placement-dependent explanation, without isolating individual hardware noise mechanisms. The same ordering inversion is absent on the all-to-all IonQ control. On Rigetti Cepheus, a follow-up using topology-aware native placement found no consistent advantage in correct-answer probability for either submission track, but did not establish equivalence between the tracks. Structural comparisons depend on metric weighting, placement and device generation. Provider interfaces also limit observability: Rigetti's supported-operation list remained unchanged across a device generation that replaced the native entangler. We classify silent interface failures in composed toolchains and identify checks at toolchain boundaries, connecting valid cross-provider comparisons with concrete software-quality practices.

papers.title: Feasibility Ceilings Before Learning: Sizing and Timing Bounds for Drone-Mesh Interception
papers.abstract: A mesh of interceptors defending a fixed site must spread over the predicted arrival point of an approaching object. This is a recurring task in multi-agent robotics: N agents, each covering a disc of radius r, spread over a probability density so that a point drawn from it falls within some agent's disc. We give closed forms for the quantities that bound performance before any policy is chosen, and validate each by Monte Carlo. The uncertainty of a point predicted by extrapolating a noisy linear track follows from least-squares variance propagation plus a delta-method term for the uncertain arrival time, agreeing with simulation to within 1.8%. The coverage probability of a packed mesh admits a closed form accurate to 0.007 absolute, with a volumetric analogue. A naive area ratio misses a ceiling: while agents stay at least 2r apart, no mesh exceeds 90.69% coverage in the plane or 74.05% in a volume. This ceiling belongs to the separation constraint, not to the problem - permitting overlap substitutes Kershner's thinnest-covering density and removes it, the better regime above a crossover at p=0.80. Hexagonal packing is optimal among five arrangements; the centroidal-Voronoi configuration coverage control supplies reaches only half its coverage at small budgets. The Gaussian assumption is conservative under heavy tails and anisotropy but fragile under bias: a one-sigma aim-point offset costs 14 points of coverage. A repositioning team must also choose a commit time, and the admissible window can be empty. Against the applicable ceiling, analytic placement attains 85% of what the configuration permits while centralised PPO averages 15% over three trainer seeds, with a paired bootstrap against a null policy containing zero at every seed. We argue such ceilings should be computed before any learning experiment and quoted alongside every result.

authors.name: Dmytro Babarytskyi
authors.institution: Kharkiv National University of Radio Electronics

papers.title: Stimulated capture of axion dark matter around primordial black holes
papers.abstract: We study the stimulated capture of axion and axion-like particles around primordial black holes, mediated by quartic self-interactions. We identify the parametric regions where Bose-enhanced growth overcomes cosmological dilution and derive analytic criteria for efficient formation and long-term survival of the hydrogenic ground-state cloud, confronting them with current bounds on axion-photon couplings. We discuss observational implications of these PBH+cloud systems, including resonant axion-to-photon conversion in neutron star magnetospheres and finite-size microlensing distortions. In the former case, the resonance condition selects a conversion shell outside the neutron star surface, and we show that the large axion occupation number of the cloud can compensate for the small conversion probability. The resulting transient line flux densities can exceed nominal VLA and ALMA sensitivities in regions where the Galactic encounter rate is observationally relevant. Independently, when the cloud size becomes comparable to or larger than the Einstein radius, finite-size effects can modify the standard point-lens microlensing light curve.

authors.name: Nuno P. Branco
authors.institution: Centro de Física da Universidade de Coimbra

authors.name: João G. Rosa
authors.institution: Centro de Física da Universidade de Coimbra

papers.title: Logical isomorphism and logical limit laws for small permutation classes and regular languages
papers.abstract: In this paper we show that for each small permutation class $\mathcal{F}$ there exists a regular language $L_\mathcal{F}$ such that the monadic second-order TOTO logic on $\mathcal{F}$ is isomorphic to classical monadic second-order logic on $L_\mathcal{F}$. Thanks to the fact that regular languages are closed under monadic second-order restrictions this shows that many subsets of $\mathcal{F}$ have a well-behaved structure. In particular, this allows us to show that random permutations from any small permutation class satisfies convergence laws for both first-order logic and monadic second-order logic. In the latter case, the law is modular. Our proofs introduce a way of using the automaton description of regular languages to prove properties of generating functions which may be of independent interest. Potential applications include first-order limit laws for random words in some regular languages.

papers.title: MedToolFault and MedGuard: evaluating and improving clinical agent reliability
papers.abstract: Clinical agents must retrieve patient-specific evidence and correctly update records despite unreliable tool responses. We introduce MedToolFault, a fault-injection benchmark linking six tool-failure classes to answer correctness, required state changes and forbidden mutations in public clinical-agent tasks. We also introduce MedGuard, a tool-layer method that verifies read evidence and attributes ambiguous writes through public interfaces. Across 127,861 formal episode evaluations, we assess fault recovery, mechanism controls, task expansion, constrained tool budgets and external question answering. Across nine model configurations, unguarded agents fail in 32.2-67.8% of fault-injected evaluations on tasks each configuration solves without faults. MedGuard improves paired safe success by 13.7-46.6 percentage points on these tasks.

authors.name: Sicheng Zhou
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

authors.name: Yifan Wu
authors.institution: Hefei CAS Ion Medical and Technical Devices (China)

papers.title: Multiscale Generalized Sparse Plane Wave Decomposition in the Spherical Harmonic Domain
papers.abstract: Sparse plane wave decomposition (SPWD) is a physics-driven model-based approach for analyzing sound fields that is suitable for real-time operation. SPWD is used in different contexts such as direction of arrival (DOA) estimation and sound field separation. SPWD employs spherical Dirichlet kernels to decompose sound fields represented as steered response maps into a finite number of plane waves using sparse recovery techniques. This article proposes a multiscale generalized sparse plane wave decomposition approach that uses an optimal spherical kernel and a multiscale sparse decomposition method to improve recovery performance. The utility of the proposed approach is shown by comparisons with the original SPWD approach via extensive numerical simulations.

papers.title: Minimizing Age of Incorrect Information in Pull-Based Remote Estimation of a Markov Source
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider a discrete-time pull-based remote estimation system involving an information source and a remote monitor where the information source is a finite-state irreducible discrete-time Markov chain (DTMC) process. In this system, the remote monitor sends a pull request towards the source which responds by sampling its process so as to transmit the sampled values towards the monitor through a delay channel, encapsulated in information packets. We consider i) zero delay (ZD) and ii) unit delay (UD) channels, where the packet transmission times are zero and one slot, respectively. For remote estimation, we use the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimator, and for quantifying its performance, we use the mean age of incorrect information (MAoII) which is a recently proposed freshness and mismatch metric that penalizes an incorrect estimation along with its duration. Our goal is to obtain pull policies so as to minimize MAoII under a long-run sampling rate constraint. For the ZD model, we propose a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP) formulation of the problem, which allows us to find the optimum observation-dependent pull policy. On the other hand, the UD channel prevents the monitor from possessing perfect information on the actual AoII process at any given time, and the SMDP formulation of the ZD channel cannot readily be used for the UD model. For the system with the UD channel, we first provide a numerical algorithm to calculate the MAoII and the average sampling rate for a given observation-dependent pull policy. For the optimization of the underlying remote estimation system, we use the joint distribution of the age and source processes to be obtained from the history of all observations, termed as belief. Subsequently, we propose a belief-dependent policy obtained via the belief-MDP formulation and a constrained deep reinforcement learning (CDRL) algorithm.

papers.title: Capital Costs Protect the Network: Mining Gap Dynamics in Proof-of-Work Blockchains Under a Stochastic Mempool
papers.abstract: Proof-of-Work blockchains increasingly rely on transaction fees to keep miners engaged as block subsidies decline. An immediate outcome of this is that miners may sit idle at the start of a round until enough high-fee transactions accumulate in order to make mining worthwhile. This idle period is known as the mining gap. We model the high-fee transaction backlog as a Lindley-type recursion under a two-tier fee market and use its stationary distribution to characterize the mining gap. Under Bitcoin's difficulty-adjustment mechanism, the expected gap grows strictly with the hashpower active on the network and consumes the entire round as that hashpower grows without bound. A free-entry condition determines a unique long-run equilibrium hashpower. Capital cost caps the equilibrium hashpower and prevents the mining gap from occupying the entire round. We further characterize how the block subsidy, transaction fees, and operating cost shape the equilibrium hashpower and the mining gap.

papers.title: Interior Regularity for Stable Solutions of Semilinear Elliptic Equations with Sign-Changing Nonlinearities
papers.abstract: We investigate interior regularity for stable solutions of the semilinear elliptic equation $-Δu=f(u)$ in an open set $Ω\subseteq \mathbb R^n$, where $f$ is locally Lipschitz and may change sign. We establish sharp interior Hölder estimates for stable classical solutions in every dimension $n\le 9$, thereby fully resolving a question raised by Cabré concerning interior regularity without the nonnegativity assumption on $f$. For $n\le 5$, we also give a short alternative proof of the corresponding Hölder regularity result due to Peng, Zhang, and Zhou. We further establish higher-integrability estimates for the gradient and $L^1$ bounds for the Hessian in all dimensions. For $n\ge 10$, we obtain BMO and Morrey estimates, extending related results previously established for nonnegative nonlinearities. When $f$ is convex, we extend the interior regularity estimates to stable weak solutions through an approximation theorem. As applications, we prove Liouville-type theorems for entire stable solutions of equations with sign-changing nonlinearities across all dimensions.

papers.title: Edge ideals of gapfree graphs with matching number $3$
papers.abstract: We prove that if $G$ is a gapfree graph with matching number $3$, then every power $I(G)^q$, $q\geq2$, of its edge ideal has linear quotients, and hence a linear resolution. Our approach combines graph reductions based on clique domination of gapfree graphs and matching number with operations preserving linear quotients. We reduce the problem to $26$ non-co-chordal graphs on at most seven vertices. A new preservation theorem for gapfree edge addition, together with known results on duplication and gapfree expansion, handles all but one of these graphs. For the remaining graph on seven vertices, we construct a linear quotients ordering for the square and extend it recursively to every higher power.

papers.title: FlashAttention with Statistics: Low-Overhead Attention Features for Compact Hallucination Detectors
papers.abstract: Large language models can produce fluent answers that the supplied context does not support. A compact frozen proxy model can detect such answers by reading the context and another model's response, even from a proprietary generator. Attention-based detectors use summary statistics of the proxy's attention weights, but standard pipelines materialize the attention matrix, whose memory grows quadratically with sequence length. We compute these statistics without materializing attention, by accumulation in the FlashAttention pass, sparse lookups after it, or a second tiled pass over the scores, and classify them by this path into nearly free and costlier ones. On an H100, the statistics of five published detectors add 16% to the latency of a Qwen3-8B forward at 2K tokens, falling to 1.4% at 35K, and store 22.5 KiB per response token. On three benchmarks, probes trained on frozen Qwen3 proxies of 0.6B to 8B parameters prove strong detectors: a 4B proxy outperforms the strongest of nine zero-shot 4-9B LLM judges in F1 on two of the three, the proxies match or outperform specialized grounding checkers of up to 7B parameters, probing each proxy beats prompting it as a judge, and adding attention features significantly improves F1 in half of the 12 benchmark-proxy pairs, never significantly lowering it.

papers.title: Stability analysis of the steady solution for incompressible lid-driven cavity flow
papers.abstract: Steady solutions at high Reynolds numbers are computed using an iterative method that linearizes the nonlinear convective terms. This linearization reduces the original nonlinear boundary-value problem to a sequence of linear problems, one solved at each iteration, thereby improving the numerical robustness of the algorithm and enabling convergence over a wide range of governing parameters. The stability of steady incompressible fluid flows is studied within the framework of a linear problem for perturbations. The original steady velocity and pressure fields are subjected to small perturbations, after which the equations are linearized with respect to the perturbations. The resulting linear problem allows one to analyze the evolution of small perturbations and to establish whether the steady solutions under consideration are stable with respect to infinitesimal perturbations. In this work, the computational implementation is based on spatial discretization by the finite element method on triangular meshes. The stability of the obtained solutions is analyzed by solving a generalized algebraic eigenvalue problem formed after discretization of the linear problem for perturbations. The presence of eigenvalues with positive real part indicates instability, whereas their absence indicates stability. Calculations were performed on a sequence of refined meshes at various Reynolds numbers for the flow in a square cavity.

papers.title: The asymptotic surjective number and F-surjective signature
papers.abstract: We study two invariants measuring the asymptotic abundance of surjections between modules. We prove that Hashimoto's asymptotic surjective number is attained over local rings, hence it is a rational number. We also prove that its associated function is constructible in families and on spectra; on the latter, it is moreover lower semicontinuous on the support of the target. We establish the existence of the F-surjective signature, a common generalization of F-signature and dual F-signature, and prove that it is superadditive in its source and varies lower semicontinuously across the spectrum under mild assumptions. As applications, we obtain new rationality results for dual F-signature and prove a transformation inequality under finite maps, with consequences for quotient singularities and reduction mod p.

papers.title: Commuting Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols on the Fock space
papers.abstract: We give a counterexample to a characterization of commuting Toeplitz operators due to Bauer, Choe, and Koo [JFA, 268 (2015), 3017--3060]. We prove a corrected characterization for Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols of exponential type on the Fock space in one complex variable.

authors.name: Youqi Liu
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Transference theory for the trilinear restriction estimate and an application to the quadratic NLS in 3D
papers.abstract: In this article we develop a theory for effectively transferring trilinear restriction estimates for the Schrödinger equation to functions in a more general resolution space adapted to the Schrödinger equation. As an application we provide a global theory for the quadratic NLS in three spatial dimensions in the critical Sobolev space $\dot{H}^{-\frac{1}{2}}$.

authors.name: Vitor Borges
authors.institution: National Institute of Health Dr. Ricardo Jorge

papers.title: Unimodular Zeros of Selmer's Harmonic Trinomials
papers.abstract: Let $n>k$ be positive integers and let $\varepsilon,δ\in\{-1,1\}$. In this note, we classify the unimodular zeros of the harmonic trinomial $H_{\varepsilon,δ}:\mathbb{C}\to \mathbb{C}$ given by \[ H_{\varepsilon,δ}(z)=z^n+\varepsilon\overline z^{\,k}+δ, \] where $\overline{z}$ is the complex conjugate of $z\in \mathbb{C}$. Let $g:=\gcd(n,k)$ be the greatest common divisor of $n$ and $k$, and set $n_0:=n/g$ and $k_0:=k/g$. For each choice of $\varepsilon,δ\in \{-1,1\}$, we give a necessary and sufficient congruence involving $n_0$ and $k_0$ to guarantee that $H_{\varepsilon,δ}$ has unimodular zeros. More precisely, if the corresponding congruence holds, then $H_{\varepsilon,δ}$ has exactly $2g$ unimodular zeros, which are given explicitly; otherwise, it has no unimodular zeros. The proof uses a reduction to a trinomial equation and elementary divisibility arguments.

papers.title: Surjective maps preserving quasi-nilpotence of products of operators
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space and let $\mathcal B(X)$ the full algebra of all bounded linear operator on $X$. In this paper, we give a complete characterization of surjective maps $φ:\mathcal B(X)\to\mathcal B(X)$ satisfying \[ r(AB)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad r(φ(A)φ(B))=0 \qquad(A,B\in\mathcal B(X)). \] Without assuming additivity, injectivity, or continuity, we show that there exists a function $γ: B(X)\mapsto \C \setminus\{0\}$ such that the map $φ$ takes one of the following forms: 1. there exists a bounded linear or conjugate-linear, invertible operator $S:X\to X$ such that : \label{eq:direct} φ(A)=γ(A)SAS^{-1},\qquad \text{ for all } \quad A\in B(X), 2. the space $X$ is reflexive and there exists a bounded linear or conjugate-linear, invertible operator $S:X^*\to X$ such that \label{eq:dual} φ(A)=γ(A)SA^*S^{-1},\qquad \text{ for all } \quad A\in B(X).

papers.title: The best Ulam constant of the n-th order linear differential operator with constant coefficients
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Banach space over the field $\mathbb{K} \in \{\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{C}\}$, and let $L:\mathcal{C}^{n}(\mathbb{R},X)\to\mathcal{C}(\mathbb{R},X)$ be the $n$-th order linear differential operator defined by $Ly := y^{(n)} + a_1 y^{(n-1)} + \cdots + a_n y$, where $a_1,\ldots,a_n \in \mathbb{K}$ are fixed scalars and $n$ is a fixed positive integer. It is well known that $L$ is Ulam stable if and only if its characteristic equation has no roots on the imaginary axis. In this paper, we determine the best Ulam constant of $L$ under this condition, for an arbitrary order $n$ and without any restriction on the multiplicities of the roots of the characteristic equation. This improves and completes several known Ulam stability results for this operator and provides the best estimate possible for the error between approximate and exact solutions of the equation $Ly=f$, where $f\in\mathcal{C}(\mathbb{R},X)$. Moreover, as an auxiliary result, we give an explicit formula for the general solution of this equation.

papers.title: A nonstandard fractional Jacobi pseudospectral method for weakly regular right-sided Caputo terminal problems
papers.abstract: Right-sided fractional differential equations arising in terminal value problems present substantial analytical and numerical challenges due to their intrinsic nonlocal structure and the presence of weak algebraic-type singularities near the terminal point. These singular behaviors significantly degrade the performance of classical finite-difference, finite-element, and standard spectral methods, which typically rely on smoothness assumptions that break down in the fractional setting. In this work, we develop a comprehensive fractional pseudospectral framework specifically designed for nonlinear right-sided Caputo terminal value systems. The proposed method employs a versatile family of nonstandard fractional Jacobi basis functions whose endpoint-weighted structure naturally reflects the asymptotic behavior of right-sided fractional operators. This construction enables the accurate approximation of solutions with limited regularity near the terminal point, without requiring smoothing transformations or mesh grading. We establish the existence and uniqueness of the discrete numerical solution and derive rigorous convergence estimates that faithfully capture the inherent singularity structure of the problem. A series of numerical experiments validates the theoretical developments and demonstrates that the proposed approach delivers high-order accuracy and superior resolution of terminal-layer behavior compared with traditional spectral techniques. The resulting framework provides an efficient and reliable computational tool for challenging nonlinear fractional terminal value systems characterized by weak solution regularity.

authors.name: Mahmoud A. Zaky
authors.institution: École Marocaine des Sciences de l'Ingénieur

papers.title: Stochastic Latent Twins: Learning Stochastic Solution Operators
papers.abstract: Scientific prediction under uncertainty requires more than a single future state: it requires the distribution of possible outcomes. We show that this distribution-valued evolution can be learned directly as a stochastic solution operator between arbitrary source and target times. We introduce Stochastic Latent Twins, which represent the physical state through a deterministic encoder-decoder while placing stochasticity entirely in a probability-valued latent evolution map. This separation makes the stochastic transition law independent of the state representation and enables direct probabilistic prediction without recursive time stepping. We establish an end-to-end Wasserstein approximation theory that separates representation and latent-transition errors, derive stability guarantees, and develop a distributional theory of physics conformity with latent-to-physical transfer bounds and conformity by construction. The resulting framework can be learned directly from observed transitions and supports forward prediction, backward conditional evolution, one-shot generation, and physics-conforming stochastic dynamics within the same formulation. Numerical experiments ranging from linear and non-Gaussian SDEs to stochastic Lorenz dynamics, generative modeling, a stochastic Hamiltonian system, and a two-dimensional stochastic Burgers equation verify the theory, expose the distinct roles of state representation and transition-family expressivity, compare favorably with recent stochastic and one-step generative methods, and demonstrate exact physical conservation by construction. More broadly, Stochastic Latent Twins provide a step toward scientific surrogates that represent not only the evolution of a system, but also its uncertainty and physical structure, opening new opportunities across uncertainty quantification, data assimilation, inverse problems, control, and digital twins.

papers.title: Quantile-Guided Diffusion for Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: Quantile forecasts summarize uncertainty at each future time step, while diffusion forecasters represent it through sampled future trajectories. We study how predicted quantiles can serve as distributional controls for diffusion forecasting. Specifically, we investigate how the mechanism of quantile integration affects its effectiveness in guiding a pretrained diffusion forecaster. We find that residual control throughout the denoising network yields the most consistent improvements. We instantiate this approach as Control-TS, which learns a quantile-control pathway while keeping the pretrained backbone frozen. Across eight benchmarks, Control-TS consistently improves the backbone's CRPS, achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art forecasting models, and retains its gains in capacity-matched comparisons. Further analyses examine how these gains depend on quantile granularity, predictor choice, and forecast quality. Finally, we introduce the Conditional Linear Predictive Score (CLPS), which complements distributional metrics by evaluating the downstream forecasting utility of generated futures. Together, these findings support predicted quantiles as an effective interface between explicit uncertainty estimates and diffusion-based trajectory generation.

papers.title: Causal Analysis of Robot Foundation Models Enables Efficiency Gains
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are a promising approach to general purpose robot manipulation. While the internal computation of vision-language models, which compose the backbone of VLAs, has been studied extensively, less is known about how their perceptual and semantic representations are transformed into action in VLA models. We study this question mechanistically in three frontier VLA models ($π_{0.5}$, MolmoAct2, and MolmoBot) by analyzing the causal pathways through which the input image and the instruction shape actions. Across the three models, activation patching shows that causally relevant information influences the action expert (AE) through a narrow band of mid-to-late cross-attention layers, which we term the action-conditioning interface. The content of this information changes with token and layer within the model. Early-to-mid layer representations of the target noun token determine which object is selected, whereas mid-to-late layers carry the spatial information in text tokens that redirects the movement when patched. Where spatial information is stored in prompt tokens various based on the architecture. In MolmoAct2 the model forms task-conditioned representations at the text positions that follow the instruction, whereas $π_{0.5}$ additionally stores this information at image token positions. We show that these findings can be translated directly into improving model efficiency. We find that restricting MolmoBot's action expert conditioning to only 3 out of 36 layers reduces inference FLOPs by up to $33\%$ while maintaining comparable task success with the default model across 3,000 evaluation episodes ($46.7\%$ vs. $46.9\%$), and the same principle carries over to real-robot deployment of $π_{0.5}$.

authors.name: Andrew Lee
authors.institution: University of Iowa Hospitals and Clinics

papers.title: Quantitative Volume Estimate on Singular Sets of One-phase Free Boundary Problems in Ricci Limit Spaces
papers.abstract: We study limit solutions of the one-phase free boundary problem on noncollapsed Ricci limit spaces. We introduce a quantitative stratification $\mathcal{S}^k_{\varepsilon,r}$ of the singular set of the free boundary that simultaneously captures the approximate splitting of the ambient space and the approximate homogeneity and translational invariance of the solution. We also introduce a new truncated parabolic Weiss quantity that provides quantitative homogeneity via pinching across scales. Although this quantity may not be uniformly bounded across all small scales, it effectively shows that, among the first $j$ scales in a fixed decreasing geometric progression, at most $C\sqrt{j}$ scales fail to exhibit quantitative homogeneity. Such slow growth in $j$ enables us to adapt the covering argument of Cheeger and Naber [arXiv:1103.1819] to show, for every $η>0$, a $Cr^{n-k-η}$ upper bound for the volume of the $r$-tubular neighborhood of the $k$-th quantitative singular stratum, $\mathcal{S}^k_{\varepsilon,r}$. The same tubular-neighborhood estimate holds for the effective stratum $\mathcal S_\varepsilon^k$, and in particular we get the Minkowski dimension bound $\dim_{\mathcal M} \mathcal S_\varepsilon^k \le k$, from which the previously known sharp bound $\dim_{\mathcal H} \mathrm{Sing} \le n-3$ in Chan, Zhang, and Zhu [arXiv:2112.06962] follows. As another corollary, we prove that the free boundary admits a Hölder manifold structure away from a set of Minkowski dimension at most $n-3$.

papers.title: Local Extrema and Infinite Derivatives of the Delange Function of Base 3
papers.abstract: The Delange function of base $3$ is the continuous function $T(x)=\sum_{j\ge0}3^{-j}τ(3^jx)$ of Takagi type, where $τ(x)=2\min\{\mathrm{dist}(x,\mathbb{Z}),1/3\}$. Multiplied by $3^n$, its values at the points $m/3^n$ are the smallest numbers $ξ_n(m)=2(nm-S_3(m))$ of edges leaving a set of $m$ vertices in the ternary Hamming cube $Q_n^3$, where $S_3(m)=\sum_{j<m}s_3(j)$ and $s_3$ is the ternary digit sum. Both facts are known. We show that the local minima of $T$ are exactly the ternary rationals $m/3^n$, and that the local maxima are exactly the points $(m+1/2)/3^n+k$ with integers $k$, $m$, $n$ such that $n\ge0$, $0\le m<3^n$ and $s_3(m)=n$. We also characterize, in terms of the ternary digits $ξ_1,ξ_2,\ldots$ of $x$, when $T$ has an infinite derivative at $x$ from one or both sides. At a ternary rational the right derivative is $+\infty$ and the left derivative is $-\infty$. At every other point, the right derivative is $+\infty$ exactly when $\sum_{j\le n}(1-ξ_j)\to+\infty$. The condition for the left derivative to be $+\infty$ is stronger and also involves the lengths of the maximal strings of zeros among the digits. For the value $-\infty$ the two sides are exchanged and the roles of zeros and twos are swapped. In particular, $T$ has an infinite derivative at every rational point that is not a ternary rational and whose period has different numbers of zeros and twos. We also determine the maximum of $ξ_n(m)$ over every block of sizes $a3^k\le m\le(a+1)3^k$, describe by the ternary digits of $h$ the sizes $h$ for which the $h$-extra edge connectivity of $Q_n^3$ equals $ξ_n(h)$, and compute the Fourier coefficients of $T$ and its variation at each level. Finally, we determine the level set at height $3/4$, which has dimension $\log2/\log9$, and show that no level set has a larger upper box dimension and that $\{x\in[0,1]:T(x)=y\}$ is finite for almost every $y$.

papers.title: Convexity, the spectrum of free Laplacians and geometric consequences: a free KLS bound
papers.abstract: We establish a compactness theorem for the resolvent of free Laplacians. More precisely, let $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ be a self-adjoint tuple admitting Lipschitz conjugate variables in the sense of Dabrowski (2014). Under the non-commutative curvature--dimension condition $CD(c,\infty)$ with $c>0$, introduced in our previous work (2026), we prove that the free Laplacian $Δ:=\partial^*\bar\partial$ is proper, that is, has compact resolvent. Our argument is non-perturbative and uses a spectral variant of the free Bochner method based on Dabrowski's almost-commutation formulas. A further stochastic argument gives a normal unital trace-preserving embedding of $M=W^*(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ into $L(\mathbb F_2)$. Together, the compactness and embedding theorems gives several operator-algebraic consequences, including the Haagerup approximation property, the CMAP, and strong solidity. We also obtain proper proximality and bi-exactness. We finally obtain several geometric consequences. We prove a free analogue of Klartag's improved log--Lichnerowicz inequality (2023), together with rigidity in the equality case. More surprisingly, under $CD(0,\infty)$, we prove a dimension-free Kannan--Lovász--Simonovits (KLS) bound in the free setting. As a consequence, we obtain a free thin-shell estimate for isotropic tuples. We conclude with further questions on spectral comparison with the canonical semicircular model.

papers.title: WaveLLM: Wavelet-Domain LLM Entropy Modeling for Lossless Image Compression
papers.abstract: Lossless image compression fundamentally relies on accurate entropy modeling, driving a recent shift toward large language model (LLM)-based methods. However, existing approaches mainly emphasize the modeling capacity of LLMs while directly serializing images into pixel or residual sequences, leaving heterogeneous signal patterns entangled within a single prediction stream. In this paper, we argue that effective entropy modeling depends not only on model capacity, but also on the predictability of the input representation. Motivated by this insight, we propose WaveLLM, a wavelet-domain LLM-based entropy model for lossless image compression. By decomposing an image into multi-level wavelet subbands, WaveLLM converts a heterogeneous prediction problem into a set of more structured and statistically homogeneous subproblems that are more amenable to autoregressive probability estimation. To bridge numerical coding symbols with the LLM's native text token space, we introduce a dedicated numerical interface featuring value embeddings and a coefficient prediction head. Furthermore, a task-adaptive prompting strategy is designed to enable a single shared model to adapt to diverse subbands within a unified framework. Built on Llama-3.2-3B with LoRA adaptation, WaveLLM achieves 2.51, 2.24, and 2.27 bpsp on Kodak, CLIC Pro, and DIV2K, respectively, outperforming the PixelCNN-based codec using the same wavelet transform by 0.43, 0.36, and 0.46 bpsp, and surpassing recent LLM-based lossless compressors on all three benchmarks.

papers.title: SCOPE: Semantic Bounded Credit Optimization for Prompt Engineering in Text-to-image Generation
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables language models to improve text-to-image (T2I) generation by rewriting prompts for a frozen image generator. Existing methods typically apply a single signal derived from the image to individual subword tokens, although objects, counts, attributes, and relations form coherent semantic spans. We propose SCOPE, an objective based on Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) that aligns update weighting with this structure. The rewriter jointly generates an enhanced prompt and its semantic partition. SCOPE pools shifts in policy log probabilities within each span to derive a shared coefficient for its token losses while retaining a single advantage for each completion. It requires neither separate span rewards nor additional image renders. Across Qwen-Image, SD3, and FLUX.1-dev, SCOPE achieves average relative gains over vanilla GRPO of 9.48% on GeneVal and 7.62% on T2I-CompBench. Ablation studies show that both semantic boundaries and pooling within spans contribute to these gains, supporting semantic structure as a practical inductive bias for prompt engineering with RL.

papers.title: ChronoSheaf: Joint Spatio-Temporal Spectral Filtering on Cellular Sheaves
papers.abstract: Sheaf neural networks generalize graph neural networks by assigning each edge a learned linear restriction map that specifies how the local representations of adjacent nodes relate to one another, thereby mitigating oversmoothing. Existing sheaf architectures, however, define the sheaf Laplacian as an instantaneous spatial operator and therefore cannot explicitly model how signals evolve over time on a graph. We first introduce a spectral sheaf Laplacian, defined jointly over space and time, such that a single operator regulates signal propagation across both the spatial graph and the temporal domain. Directly extending this operator's receptive field in space or time would require increasingly complex sheaf structures. Instead, we propose a spectral filter that expands the effective receptive field along both dimensions without enlarging the underlying sheaf. Building on this operator, we introduce ChronoSheaf, a spatio-temporal sheaf network with two key components. First, Transitional Restriction Maps (TRM) decompose each node's restriction map into a spatial term and two temporal frames that independently control its relation to neighboring nodes at the preceding and following timestep, enabling asymmetric temporal influence. Second, the Dual Spectral Filter (DSF) applies a single bounded-degree polynomial filter with an adaptively estimated spectral radius to the joint spatio-temporal sheaf operator. We validate ChronoSheaf on a diverse set of spatio-temporal forecasting benchmarks, where it outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/ChronoSheaf-1D7D/.

authors.name: Zahra Ahmadi
authors.institution: Islamic Azad University, Science and Research Branch

papers.title: Tolerant Testers for Subgraph-Freeness
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the problem of tolerantly testing the property of being $H$-free (which also implies distance approximation from being $H$-free). In the general-graphs model, we show that tolerant $K_k$-freeness testing can be achieved with query complexity that is polynomial in the arboricity of the input graph $G$, $arb(G)$, and independent of the size of $G$ (for graphs in which the average degree is $Ω(1))$. Specifically for triangles, our algorithm distinguishes graphs which are $ε$-close to being triangle-free from graphs that are $3ε(1+η)$-far from being triangle-free with expected query complexity which is $\tilde{O}(arb^3(G))$ (for constant $η$ and $ε$). For general $k$-cliques our algorithm distinguishes graphs which are $ε$-close to being $K_k$-free from graphs which are ${k \choose 2}ε(1+η)$-far from being $K_k$-free with expected query complexity which is polynomial in $k$, $1/ε$, $1/η$ and $arb(G)$. We then generalize our result and provide a similar result for any motif $H$ which is $2$-connected and has radius $1$. This includes for example the wheel graph. Finally, we show that our tester can be applied to the bounded-degree model for tolerantly testing $H$-freeness for any motif $H$. The query complexity of the algorithm is polynomial in the degree bound, $d$, improving the previous state-of-the-art by Marko and Ron (TALG 2009) that obtained quasi-polynomial query complexity in $d$.

papers.title: Minkowski Functionals of CII Line Intensity Maps: Probing Astrophysics and Primordial Features
papers.abstract: Line intensity mapping aims to measure the total cumulative light of spectral lines from galaxies, without resolving individual sources. In this work, we investigate mock intensity maps of ionized carbon CII using Minkowski functionals, which capture the morphological properties of the maps. We generate semi-numerical simulations of CII intensity maps at $z\approx 6$ and $7.6$, adopting an astrophysical model that relates CII line luminosity to the mass of the host dark matter halos. We find that Minkowski functionals can provide tight constraints on the astrophysical model parameters in the presence of noise characteristics expected from the upcoming CCAT survey. We further investigate the prospects of probing a bump-like feature superimposed on the standard single power-law primordial power spectrum. Using a Fisher matrix formalism, we demonstrate that the effects of this primordial feature can be disentangled from those of the astrophysical model parameters. Combining measurements across multiple smoothing scales as well as redshifts can further improve the constraints and enhance the prospects for detecting such primordial features.

papers.title: Spectral comparison on Specht modules and mixing of the interchange process
papers.abstract: We characterize the cases in which the minimal eigenvalues of interchange-process Laplacians on two Specht modules can be compared up to a positive multiplicative constant, independent of the edge rates. In the comparable cases, we establish an inverse-polynomial lower bound for this constant. We conjecture that the constant can always be taken to be 2/3. We apply these ideas to the mixing times of the interchange and exclusion processes. Using the comparison method of Hermon, Kozma and Salez, we prove that our conjecture implies a conjecture of Oliveira on the mixing time of the interchange process. We also obtain unconditional mixing-time bounds for both processes.

papers.title: Multimodal AI Detection for Math-Heavy Scientific Text
papers.abstract: As large language models become increasingly capable of generating, and assisting with, scientific writing, there is a need for greater transparency and disclosure around the use of AI in research. Consequently, a veritable subfield of research and a number of commercial services aim to flag AI-generated content automatically. However, existing detectors which rely only on text extracted from PDFs fail to benefit from the rich visual information contained in the formatting of math-heavy scientific content. To study this, we select human-written proof and prose passages from pre-2022 arXiv LaTeX sources and re-generate them using 15 modern LLMs within the context of the same paper. This leaves us with coupled human and AI outputs in three different representations: the LaTeX source, a rendered image of the PDF, and the text extracted from the PDF. We find that the accuracy of the state-of-the-art Pangram 4 drops significantly as the mathematical content in a passage increases, especially when evaluated on text as opposed to LaTeX. However, this is not an inherent limitation of detecting AI-generated math: finetuning Qwen-3.5-27B based detectors on this domain recovers the gap, with LaTeX inputs performing significantly better than text since they preserve more formatting information. Since LaTeX sources are rarely available in practice, we also train SnapJudge: an image-based detector operating on screenshots of both prose and proofs from papers. At 0.1% false positive rate, SnapJudge achieves a detection rate of 92% on proofs and 93% on prose generated by frontier models, substantially outperforming both Pangram 4 and our text-based detector. We release our data, models and code at https://nlplab.cs.duke.edu/snapjudge.

papers.title: Vibrational Dressing of Collective Molecular Polaritons: A Scalable Green's-Function Theory
papers.abstract: We develop a scalable Green's-function theory of vibrationally dressed molecular-polariton absorption in the Holstein--Tavis--Cummings model. Within the self-consistent Born approximation (SCBA), the ground-state linear response of $N$ identical molecules coupled to one cavity mode follows from a $2\times2$ cavity--bright matrix, while scattering through the $N-1$ dark states remains in the molecular self-energy. The number of self-consistent equations is independent of $N$, allowing large ensembles to be treated without explicitly resolving the dark manifold. Benchmarks against hierarchical equations of motion show that the theory captures collective linewidth narrowing and an $N$-dependent minimum in the lower-polariton linewidth as its exciton fraction varies, beyond a Hopfield-weighted linewidth estimate. Comparisons with exact diagonalization for discrete local vibrations show weaker vibronic progressions and better overall SCBA agreement as $N$ increases at fixed single-molecule coupling. The resulting framework connects microscopic vibrational scattering to collective absorption spectra without introducing fitted polariton linewidths.

authors.name: Michael Galperin
authors.institution: United States National Library of Medicine

papers.title: Statistical Characterization of Erratic and Chaotic Processes through Their Extrema I. Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We propose a general statistical framework for characterizing erratic functions through the statistics of their extrema, with the aim of identifying statistical signatures associated with chaotic processes. It is based on analyzing the extrema points of erratic functions associated with these processes. One is instructed to determine the probability distribution functions ( PDF)s of the locations of the extrema points, the spacings between the locations, in particular the nearest neighbors, and the ratios between adjacent spacings. We then fit these PDFs with PDFs known to relate to chaotic behavior like of random matrix theory. The extrema considered establish a cloud of points in general in $D$ dimensions for erratic function of several variables. For certain systems one finds also extrema curves. We further determine the ``thermodynamic" description of the erratic functions by computing the Shannon or differential entropy and by equating the PDFs to the Gibbs one. With this map we determine the ``energy function" and for certain cases also the ``temperature". We analyze three benchmark spacing PDFs: the Bernoulli shift map, the Poisson and the Gaussian beta ensemble and several others. We want to emphasize that the map to thermodynamics can be applied to variety of chaotic processes including non-physics ones. We distinguish marginal spacing distributions from joint distributions of consecutive spacings. The latter probe correlations and statistical organization that are invisible in one-spacing PDFs and may provide stronger signatures for distinguishing structured chaotic-like behavior from uncorrelated irregularity.

papers.title: Acoustic Illusion of a Rigid Object for a Moving Emitter via Equivalent Surface Control
papers.abstract: We report a three-dimensional acoustic illusion of a rigid object illuminated by an emitter moving along an arbitrary trajectory. The object is absent: control sources are arranged around its location, the closed surface they define being termed the equivalent surface. Driven by the field the object would have scattered onto this surface, the sources radiate, by the Kirchhoff--Helmholtz representation, that same field beyond it. The control signals follow in closed form from a time-dependent physical optics formulation that we derive for a moving emitter, in which the motion enters analytically through the acoustic travel times, so that the scattering problem need not be re-solved at each emitter position, nor the propagation domain discretized. For objects too large to enclose, the signals are mapped onto an internal surface, an option whose advantages and penalties are discussed. Numerical simulations validate the method in both configurations.

papers.title: Automorphisms of twisted Chevalley groups of type ${}^2E_6$ over local rings
papers.abstract: We classify abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full twisted Chevalley groups of type ${}^2E_6$ over commutative local rings with involution and $2$ invertible, for both isogeny types. Every automorphism is standard, with no invertibility assumption on $3$. In the adjoint case, it has a unique expression as a composition of conjugation by an element of the full twisted group and a ring automorphism commuting with the involution. For the simply connected form, the full group equals its elementary subgroup, and the factors are strictly inner, diagonal, and ring automorphisms. The main step replaces a linear change of basis by a group element. Invariant alternating tensors determine the transported Chevalley bracket. We correct this bracket over a faithfully flat local extension and descend the resulting conjugating element by uniqueness. Root-subgroup relations then recover the coefficient automorphism.

papers.title: Dynamical phase transition for a logarithm observable in chaotic systems
papers.abstract: We consider the full distribution $P_N(A)$ of the dynamical observable $A = - \sum_{i=1}^N \ln x_i$ where $x_1, \dots, x_N$ is a sequence generated by a chaotic map $f(x)$ via $x_{n+1} = f(x_n)$. We study the particular cases where $f(x)$ is the doubling, tent or logistic map, and focus on the limit $N \gg 1$. Typical fluctuations of $A$ are Gaussian with mean $\left\langle A\right\rangle$ and variance which are both of order $\sim N$. We find that the left tail of the distribution ($A < \left\langle A\right\rangle$) scales as $P_{N}(A) \sim e^{-NI(A/N)}$, and calculate the rate function $I(a)$ which depends on the map $f(x)$. Interestingly, we find that the right tail of the distribution ($A > \left\langle A\right\rangle$) follows an anomalous scaling: $P_{N}(A) \sim e^{-N^{1/3} F((A-\left\langle A\right\rangle) / N^{2/3})}$. The large-deviation function $F(y)$ has a universal form for the three maps, differing only in the scaling constants. At a critical value $y=y_c$, it exhibits a corner singularity which has the character of a condensation transition. The transition separates between a subcritical phase $0< y<y_c$ in which the fluctuations are Gaussian and arise homogeneously from all of the $x_i$'s, and a supercritical phase $y>y_c$ in which a small fraction of the $x_i$'s give a macroscopic contribution to the fluctuation. Despite this anomalous behavior of the right tail, we find that the cumulants of the distribution $P_N(A)$ grow linearly with $N$ at large $N$, and calculate the associated coefficients.

papers.title: Geometric Hashing in MPC with Applications to Clustering and Stochastic Embeddings
papers.abstract: In this paper we study consistent hashing (a.k.a. sparse partitions) for doubling metrics in the Massively Parallel Computation (MPC) model. A $(Γ,Λ)$-hash with diameter bound $Δ$ partitions a metric space into clusters of diameter at most $Δ$ such that every ball of radius $Δ/Γ$ intersects at most $Λ$ clusters in expectation. Consistent hashing has emerged as a central tool in geometric MPC algorithms. However, so far it has been solely used in Euclidean spaces, where it can be pre-computed. On the other hand, in cases where the metric space is received as input and unknown in advance, no previous parallel construction was known. We present the first fully scalable MPC algorithm over machines with local space $n^σ$, that given an $n$-point metric space with doubling dimension $d\leq O(σ\log n)$, samples a randomized $(Γ,2^{O(d/Γ)})$-hash in $O(d/σ^3)$ rounds. There is a dichotomy: if the doubling dimension is $d=Ω(σ\cdot\log n)$, a polynomial number of rounds is required to compute such a hash. We conclude by showing that this MPC primitive yields $O(d/σ^3)$-round fully scalable MPC algorithms for a broad class of fundamental geometric problems in doubling metrics, including stochastic tree embeddings with $O(\log n)$ expected distortion, constant factor approximation for facility location, bicriteria $(O(ε^{-2}),1+ε)$-approximation for $k$-median and $k$-means.

authors.name: Hyeonjun Shin
authors.institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Cross-Prompt Inference Mitigates Rare-Class Suppression in Imbalanced VLM Finetuning
papers.abstract: When a vision-language model is finetuned on class-imbalanced data, rare-class recall can fall well below the model's own zero-shot performance. In this regime, we uncover a surprising matched-prompt penalty whereby the standard choice of reusing the descriptive finetuning prompt at inference can yield lower rare-class recall than using a different descriptive prompt. We call this inference-time strategy cross-prompt inference. We evaluate diverse VLMs across six datasets and find that cross-prompt inference consistently recovers rare-class recall, with varying trade-offs in frequent-class recall. The effect reflects a train-eval prompt interaction rather than prompt quality alone, and does not arise with non-descriptive prompt changes. It is strongest when imbalance and visual confusability produce substantial rare-class suppression, and is weak or absent when such suppression does not occur. Using Tuning Contribution (TuCo), which decomposes a model's computation into pretrained and finetuning parts, we find that cross-prompt inference reduces reliance on finetuning-induced computation and shifts the model toward its pretrained component. Reducing that finetuning contribution also substantially reduces the cross-prompt advantage. These results show that rare-class knowledge suppressed by imbalanced finetuning can remain accessible under a different inference prompt.

papers.title: Automorphisms of triality groups over local rings
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative local ring with $2,3\in R^\times$, and let $ρ\in\Aut(R)$ satisfy $ρ^3=\id$. We classify abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full triality groups in the adjoint and simply connected forms of type $D_4$. Every automorphism is uniquely determined by an adjoint group element and a ring automorphism preserving the trace $T=\id+ρ+ρ^2$; conversely, every such pair defines an automorphism. A square-zero example shows that trace-preserving coefficient automorphisms need not normalize $\langleρ\rangle$ when $ρ$ is nontrivial on $R$ but trivial on its residue field. We also prove a relative rigidity theorem for homomorphisms from elementary triality groups over arbitrary coefficient rings to local targets with $2$ and $3$ invertible, assuming that an adjoint conjugation makes the parameter-one root images standard modulo the maximal ideal. Conversely, every unital trace-preserving ring homomorphism into such a local coefficient ring induces the corresponding homomorphism of elementary groups.

papers.title: VoroTypes: automated enumeration of Voronoi cell topologies for structural identification of complex crystals in atomistic simulations
papers.abstract: VoroTypes enumerates, for an arbitrary crystal structure, the complete family of Voronoi cell topologies that can arise under small generic perturbations of atomic positions, and exports it as a topological filter for the VoroTop framework. This extends per-atom structural identification in molecular dynamics simulations, previously limited to a handful of simple reference structures, to complex crystals such as Frank--Kasper and Laves phases, with per-sublattice resolution. The package takes a standard crystallographic description (a CIF or POSCAR file) as input, applies exact symmetry reduction and validity pruning to accelerate the enumeration, and produces filters that load directly into the standalone VoroTop program or into OVITO. A library of pre-computed filters covers over a thousand structures from the Materials Project.

papers.title: On the Subadditivity of Mutual f-Information
papers.abstract: We address an open problem raised by Polyanskiy and Wu in their textbook concerning the subadditivity of mutual \(f\)-information. We study two notions of generalized mutual information: mutual \(f\)-information, defined by \(\widetilde{I}_f(X;Y)=D_f(p_{XY}\|p_Xp_Y)\), and variational \((G,f)\)-information, obtained by minimizing an average of transformed \(f\)-divergences. For the first notion, we derive a sufficient condition on \(g(x)=x^2f''(x)\) that guarantees subadditivity under conditionally independent observations. This condition yields explicit families beyond the previously known examples generated by \(x\log x\) and \((x-1)\log x\). Our proof relies on the concavity of a generalized variance functional. For the variational notion, we extend existing sufficient conditions beyond the transforms \(G(x)\in\{x,\log(1+x),-\log(1-x)\}\). Using a comparison inequality for \(G^{-1}(G(A)+G(B))\), we obtain differential criteria for concave and convex transforms. Explicit constructions illustrate the resulting classes of subadditive information measures.

papers.title: On the Sampling of Certain Dirichlet and Prime Sums at Gram Points and their Viscosity
papers.abstract: Consider the Dirichlet polynomial and its prime-indexed sub-sum \[ \begin{array}{ccc} E(t) := \sum_{k\le \left[ \sqrt{ \frac{t}{2π} } \right]} \frac{e^{it\log k}}{\sqrt{k}}, & ; & E_1(t) := \sum_{\substack{p\le \left[ \sqrt{\frac{t}{2π}} \right]\\ p\ {\rm prime}}} \frac{e^{it\log p}}{\sqrt p}. \end{array} \] In this work we investigate the statistical and arithmetic properties of the sets \[ \mathcal{C}_N := \left\{ E(g_n):1\le n\le N \right\}, \qquad \mathcal{P}_N := \left\{ E_1(g_n):1\le n\le N \right\}, \] obtained by sampling these sums at the Gram points \(g_n\) of the Hardy \(Z\)-function. We refer to \(\mathcal{C}_N\) and \(\mathcal{P}_N\) as the full and prime \(N\)-th Gram clouds, respectively. The motivation is that the approximate functional equation expresses both \(Z(g_n)\) and \(Z'(g_n)\) through different projections of the same oscillatory phase configuration, suggesting that the geometry of these sampled sums may retain information about the local behavior of nearby zeros. Numerically, we find that Gram-point sampling produces highly non-generic geometric structures: good and isolated bad Gram points occupy markedly different regions of the clouds, the prime cloud of isolated bad points splits into two anisotropic lobes, and the position along the principal direction of the folded prime cloud is strongly correlated with the viscosity of the Hardy $Z$-function \( μ(g_n)=\left|\frac{Z'(g_n)}{Z(g_n)}\right|, \) with smallest-viscosity points concentrating near distinguished extremal regions of the lobes.

papers.title: Mixed modified-gravity--modified-inertia MOND theories
papers.abstract: It is plausible that in a more fundamental theory of MOND both gravity and inertia will differ from their Newtonian versions. Such theories, if they embody the basic tenets of MOND, will share its primary predictions with existing theories, which modify either gravity or inertia. But they are expected to differ in their structure and in their secondary predictions. Here, I discuss families of nonrelativistic MOND theories that modify both the kinetic and the gravitational actions of Newtonian dynamics. Each family is spanned by one parameter $0\leη\le 1$, which is the scaling dimension of the deep-MOND limit of all terms in the action. Pure modified gravity ($η=0$) and pure modified inertia ($η=1$) are the end cases in each family. I speak of families, since the modified action terms themselves are not strictly specified, but are treated in rather general terms. These theories are artificial in that they are not based on a single unifying idea that dictates the modification of the two components. But they are still useful in pinpointing some idiosyncracies of such theories. For example, neither of the two modified terms, by itself, leads to MOND phenomenology; only their combined effect does. I show how the two combine to make some of the primary MOND predictions, such as asymptotic flatness of rotation curves, the mass-asymptotic-speed relation, and the deep-MOND, virial, mass-velocity-dispersion ($M-σ$) relation. Another idiosyncracy of such theories is the emergence of different interpolating functions in the kinetic equations of motion and in the gravitational field equations, each relevant under different circumstances, and neither of which have the standard deep-MOND limit. Such examples alert us to the wide range of theories that can lead to MOND phenomenology.

papers.title: When Rotation Bounds Nothing: Streaming Image Classifiers to Field Nodes Under Physical Capture
papers.abstract: Field nodes run image classifiers locally, exposing a first-class asset, the trained model, to theft. Trusted-execution enclaves, collaborative-inference splits, and encrypted storage assume the device owner is the adversary from deployment. Here the operator owns the node, and an adversary seizing it reads only what cold-boot capture finds resident. One answer stores nothing: a chunkable multi-exit model streams into volatile memory, rotating to bound residency. We characterise the capture envelope on real LTE traces across two victims of one architecture, against passive and adaptive adversaries. Neither survives a capable adversary; recovery cost alone differs. Against a from-scratch victim the uncaptured stages must be learned: the adaptive adversary gains most at shallow seizures, ends the CIFAR-10 envelope at every rotation, and stays rotation-bounded on CIFAR100, from 42.6% of usable seizures at 5 s to 86.8% at 30 s. Against the same architecture sliced from a public pretrained backbone, the adversary downloads those stages, recovering at least 90% of maximum accuracy at all depths, taking usable CIFAR-100 seizures from 0.0% to 97.3% at 5 s, given the victim's full labelled training set. Delivery-side secrecy raises a seizure's price; a public copy of the withheld stages erases it.

papers.title: Barrier Log-Concavity of Large Forests
papers.abstract: We prove that the independence sequence of every sufficiently large forest is strictly barrier log-concave: whenever $i_{k+1}>i_k$, one has $i_k^2>i_{k-1}i_{k+1}$. Consequently, every common downward coefficient tilt is unimodal, with one order threshold valid simultaneously for all $0<t\le1$. As an application, we prove that every sufficiently large well-covered tree has a strictly log-concave independence polynomial. More generally, the latter conclusion holds for well-covered forests with sufficiently large matching number. Every sufficiently large forest with a palindromic independence polynomial is also strictly log-concave, with its modes at the central ranks. The proof establishes local coefficient-curvature estimates uniformly over forests of unbounded maximum degree and over activities tending to zero. Combined with the fixed-density theorem of Fang, Lu, Nevo, Yao, and Zheng, these estimates complete the strict log-concavity interval down to rank one through $\lfloor17α/25\rfloor$; the terminal fraction is inherited. The classical decreasing tail then yields the barrier property. A cumulative-coefficient corona theorem transfers barrier log-concavity of the base forest to full strict log-concavity of its leaf corona.

papers.title: Long-Horizon Investment with Delayed Information in a Mean-Reverting Market
papers.abstract: We study long-term investment in an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck diffusion model with exponential utility. We solve the finite-horizon problem explicitly and show that information delay qualitatively alters long-horizon behavior. Under full information, the certainty equivalent generated by mean reversion grows quadratically with the investment horizon. With any fixed positive delay, it grows only linearly, at an asymptotic rate that we compute explicitly. We derive an explicit causal representation of the optimal delayed portfolio and show that projecting the full-information strategy onto delayed information can fail dramatically: the resulting exponential loss becomes infinite for sufficiently long horizons. Numerical examples illustrate the economic impact of information delay.

papers.title: Skew fields of non-commutative meromorphic functions affiliated to finite operator algebras
papers.abstract: We embed skew fields of meromorphic functions in several non-commuting variables into the topological $*-$algebra of closed linear operators affiliated to a finite von Neumann algebra, $\mathfrak{M}$, with faithful, normal tracial state, $τ$. Namely, let $\mathscr{O} _d (r)$, $r \in (0, +\infty]$, denote the rings of formal power series in $d \in \mathbb{N}$ non-commuting variables with "radius of convergence" at least $r$ and let $Ξ\in \mathfrak{M} ^{1\times d}$ be a tuple of row-norm $<r$ with the property that there exist no non-zero trace-class operators $T_1, \cdots, T_d \in \mathscr{B} (L^2 (\mathfrak{M}, τ))$ obeying $\sum _j [T_j , Ξ_j] =0$. Then the unital homomorphism $\mathscr{O} _d (r) \rightarrow \mathfrak{M}$ defined by the evaluation, $\mathfrak{z} _j \mapsto Ξ_j$, extends to an embedding of the universal skew field of fractions of $\mathscr{O} _d (r)$ into the $*-$algebra of closed operators affiliated to $\mathfrak{M}$. In their $L^2-$homology theory of von Neumann algebras, Connes and Shlyakhtenko defined a certain quantity, $0 \leq Δ(Ξ) \leq d$, as the Murray-von Neumann co-dimension of the Hilbert module generated by all $d-$tuples of finite rank operators obeying the above commutator condition with $Ξ\in \mathfrak{M} ^{1\times d}$. As demonstrated by Mai, Speicher and Yin, this $Δ$ measures, in a certain precise sense, the algebraic independence of the components of $Ξ$. Connes-Shlyakhtenko proved that $Δ$ is an upper bound for Voiculescu's non-microstates free entropy dimension, $δ^* (Ξ)$, and remark that it is of interest to determine whether these two quantities are equal. Using non-commutative function theory, we show that this is generally not the case, by constructing a triple of self-adjoint operators, $Ξ= (Ξ_1,Ξ_2,Ξ_3)$, for which this inequality is strict, $δ^*(Ξ) < Δ(Ξ)$.

papers.title: Efficient Agnostic Learning of Univariate Densities Under Local Differential Privacy
papers.abstract: We propose a general framework for non-interactive locally differentially private (LDP) learning of structured univariate distributions that can be approximated by piece-wise polynomials. This gives the first sample-efficient LDP learners for several distribution classes, including mixtures of log-concave distributions, such as Gaussian mixture models (GMMs). These learners also provide agnostic guarantees and are computationally efficient. We also prove a lower bound for learning GMMs under LDP, improving on the standard pure-DP packing lower bounds of Bun et al. [BKSW19]. To obtain our general learning framework, we develop an efficient non-interactive LDP algorithm for synthetic data generation over large domains, which may be of independent interest. We then use it together with a deterministic adaptation of the non-private piecewise polynomial learner of Acharya et al. [ADLS17].

papers.title: Constrained Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning in Imagination
