papers.title: KBS: A Korean Benchmark Suite for Foundation Model Evaluation
papers.abstract: We present a Korean Benchmark Suite (KBS) comprising Ko-ARC, Ko-GSM8K, Ko-EQ-Bench, Ko-WinoGrande, Ko-LAMBADA, and Ko-IFEval, covering six capabilities across 9,396 items. The suite combines review, localization, direct Korean construction, and redesign for Korean, avoiding a translation-only approach to benchmark adaptation. We evaluate Korean-developed models, multilingual open models, and closed API models under protocols that account for model access, prompt format, and scoring differences. Results show that Korean benchmark scores depend on task construction, scoring rules, prompting, and model post-training. These findings suggest that Korean evaluation should report both final scores and the settings used to obtain them.

authors.name: Sungmok Jung
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: HyCo: Hybrid Drafting for Cost-Efficient Mobile-Cloud Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Device-cloud speculative decoding reduces server computation, but growing a deep draft tree with a small language model (SLM) requires repeated passes on a mobile neural processing unit (NPU). We present HyCo, which runs the server model's native multi-token prediction (MTP) head on the device to build a deep chain and uses one SLM pass to add alternative branches. The server returns the hidden state, input embedding, and key-value entries needed by the head instead of executing its sequential steps. Quantization, a restricted vocabulary, and a 1K-token window fit both drafters to the NPU. An ε-threshold rule additionally relaxes exact preservation of the verifier's sampling distribution. In single-client runs with a Galaxy S26 Ultra over LTE/5G, HyCo reduces server GPU time per output token relative to server-side MTP self-speculation by 38.6% on Spec-Bench and 29.2% on 32K-token summarization. With the same acceptance rule, three runs of each system on Spec-Bench show 9.0 percentage points more saving and 1.9x delivery speed than an SLM-only drafter. HyCo differs from Cloud+MTP by +0.2 judge-score points (paired 95% CI: -0.9 to +1.3); exploratory translation favors SpecEdge-ε. Without relaxation, HyCo exact saves 27.7% and 11.9% on the two datasets.

authors.name: Sangjun Park
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Believed but Not Said: Measuring Hidden Belief Collapse in Multi-Agent LLM Discussions
papers.abstract: LLM systems increasingly rely on groups of agents that discuss, critique, and check one another, assuming that peers will catch individual errors. We test this assumption against a minimal adversary. In a ten-agent factual discussion, one or three adversarial agents repeatedly assert a plausible false answer. After each round we probe each benign agent's private answer through a separate call whose response is hidden from its peers, and we separately label its public stance toward the claim. Across six models and three factual-QA datasets, groups remain stable without an attacker: only 0.6% of benign agents finish with the false answer. A single adversarial agent increases this rate to 44.8% and three to 60.5%. Studies of conformity typically report public agreement without private change; we find the reverse. With three adversarial agents present, benign agents hold the false answer in 51.6% of exposed turns but publicly endorse it in only 19.7%. Much of the influence therefore remains invisible in the discussion, and the false answers persist when agents are asked for their own views. Agents that retain the true answer often fail to defend it; once adopted, the false answer spreads among benign agents, and baseline knowledge does not predict robustness.

authors.name: Wei-Chieh Huang
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: A complete classification of perfect state transfer in Grover walks on abelian Cayley graphs
papers.abstract: We completely classify connected Cayley graphs over finite abelian groups that exhibit perfect state transfer in Grover walks. First, we show that a Cayley graph over any finite group exhibiting perfect state transfer has valency $1$, $2$, or $4$. For valency $4$, we prove that an abelian Cayley graph $\operatorname{Cay}(Γ,S)$ exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if $S=\{a,-a,a+h,-a+h\}$, where $h$ has order $2$, and $4\nmid |Γ|/2$. Combining this characterization with the valency-one and valency-two cases, we explicitly determine all pairs $(Γ,S)$ for which $\operatorname{Cay}(Γ,S)$ exhibits perfect state transfer. Our results extend the classification of circulant graphs of valency at most four obtained by Kubota and Yoshino [Circulant graphs with valency up to 4 that admit perfect state transfer in Grover walks, \emph{J. Comb. Theory Ser. A.}, 216 (2025) 106064] to Cayley graphs over arbitrary finite abelian groups and to all valencies.

papers.title: CF-NODE: Counterfactual Spatial Node Intervention for Test-Time Adaptation Under Domain Shift, Evaluated Across Five Diabetic Retinopathy Datasets
papers.abstract: Automated fundus-based diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading can substantially expand screening capacity, but source-trained models degrade sharply across different cameras, clinics, and patient populations. Existing test-time adaptation methods depend on entropy minimization or target information accumulated from image batches and streams. These mechanisms can reinforce confidently incorrect predictions and break down when clinical images arrive independently. We introduce CF-NODE, a novel counterfactual test-time adaptation framework for cross- domain DR grading. Instead of trusting prediction confidence or estimating a target distribution, CF-NODE asks how each prediction responds under a controlled intervention on the evidence supporting it. CF-NODE ranks internal spatial nodes using model-derived attention, feature magnitude, and node-set similarity, progressively attenuates the highest-ranked nodes, and uses the stability of the resulting expected-grade response to apply a bounded calibration of the predicted grade distribution. The framework is fully frozen and adapts every image independently using only geometric views and a fixed source-derived prior, requiring no target-derived information or model updates. We evaluate CF-NODE on five external DR datasets under repeated-seed evaluation against TENT, EATA, SAR, and T3A. CF-NODE outperforms all four methods with statistically significant improvements over the second-best method, improves AUC on every target domain, and attains the highest average AUC and macro-F1, delivering stronger grade discrimination together with more balanced recognition across DR severity levels. These results demonstrate that counterfactual intervention sensitivity provides consistent and deployment-ready domain robustness for single-image clinical inference.

papers.title: An Eventown Result for Multisets
papers.abstract: We study an extension of the Eventown problem of sets to multisets on $[n] = \{1,2,...,n\}$. A multiset is called $m$-bounded if each element has multiplicity at most $m$. The intersection of two multisets is defined as the multiset in which each element has multiplicity equal to the minimum of its multiplicities in the two original multisets. A family of $m$-bounded multisets is called an Eventown family if every member and the intersection of every pair of distinct members has even cardinality, with cardinalities counted with multiplicities. We determine the maximum size $E_m(n)$ of such a family for every $m$ and $n$. We show that $ E_{2q}(n)=(q+1)^n, $ and $ E_{2q+1}(n)=(q+1)^{n-2k}\bigl((q+1)^2+1\bigr)^k,$ where $k=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. In particular, the case $m=1$ recovers the classical Eventown theorem for sets. We also characterize all extremal families for $m\ge2$. For even $m$, the unique extremal family consists of all multisets in which every element has even multiplicity. For odd $m\ge3$, every extremal family has a product structure arising from two explicit families on pairs of coordinates, together with an additional coordinate restricted to even multiplicities when $n$ is odd. Consequently, there are exactly $k+1$ extremal types up to permutations of the ground set.

authors.name: Abisek Dewan
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Kolkata

papers.title: Hydrostatic Equilibrium Constraints on the Fuzzy Dark Matter Mass from Dwarf Spheroidals: Method, Systematics, and Robustness
papers.abstract: We present the analysis of a non-parametric estimator of the fuzzy (wave) dark matter (FDM) boson mass based on local hydrostatic equilibrium: the classical gravitational acceleration must be balanced by the gradient of the quantum potential of the Schrödinger-Poisson-Madelung system. We apply this condition, without assuming a soliton or any other parametric profile, to the non-parametric density and enclosed mass posteriors from pyGravSphere of the nine Milky Way dwarf spheroidal (dSph) galaxies. For each posterior realization we solve, in a least squares sense over a fixed radial window, for the boson mass that best balances the two terms, which yields a posterior distribution of mass for each galaxy. The per galaxy medians span $m\sim(0.8$-$4.6)\times10^{-20}\,\mathrm{eV}$, with Draco and Ursa Minor the lightest and Carina and Sextans the heaviest. A weighted mass estimate gives $m=(1.3\pm3.5)\times10^{-20}$ eV, dominated by Draco and Ursa Minor. We characterize the systematics in detail.

authors.name: Koushik Dutta
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Kolkata

papers.title: Zhang twists for semigroups and groupoids, with applications to Steinberg algebras
papers.abstract: Zhang twists provide a powerful mechanism for deforming graded algebras, while preserving their graded module categories. We extend this theory by introducing Zhang twists for graded semigroups and graded ample groupoids. We show that the twisting construction preserves a broad class of semigroup structures, and that two graded monoids are twists of each other if and only if their categories of graded sets are pointedly equivalent. We show that Zhang twists are compatible with noncommutative Stone duality: twists on graded-Boolean inverse semigroups are in correspondence with those on the associated graded ample groupoids. Moreover, in the setting of Steinberg algebras we prove that twisting the groupoid gives the same result as twisting the corresponding algebra. These results provide a unified framework linking graded semigroups, inverse semigroup duality, ample groupoids, and graded algebras, while extending the scope of Zhang twists to settings arising from symbolic dynamics, graph algebras, and Steinberg algebras.

papers.title: Automatic Sentence Completion Using Bengali Audio Speech with a Transformer-Based Early Speech Recognition System
papers.abstract: Dementia severely impairs communication abilities and turns everyday conversations into challenging experiences. Individuals affected by dementia frequently struggle to express their thoughts or complete sentences, making it difficult for family members and caregivers to understand their needs. This study proposes a novel approach to assist dementia patients by developing an integrated system that detects signs of dementia through Bangla speech and text analysis and provides sentence auto-completion support during conversations. To achieve this, recorded voices from individuals with and without dementia were analysed, and key acoustic features were extracted to capture vocal patterns associated with cognitive decline. A transformer-based model was employed to transcribe voice signals into text for linguistic analysis. In the classification task, several Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) models were evaluated using both acoustic and textual representations, and the LSTM model architectures demonstrated strong capabilities for modelling contextual patterns in speech and language data. For the sentence auto-completion task, a sequential learning model based on a Bidirectional LSTM (Bi-LSTM) network with an attention mechanism was developed to sequentially complete partially expressed Bangla sentences during conversation. This research bridges the gap in dementia analysis in an underrepresented language and implements a sentence auto-completion framework for cognitive disorders.

authors.name: Sharun Akter Khushbu
authors.institution: North Carolina Agricultural and Technical State University

papers.title: Can LLMs Tell Stories Out of Order? A Corpus and Benchmark for Nonlinear Narrative Generation
papers.abstract: Every story has two orders: the order in which its events happen and the order in which they are told. A story is nonlinear when the two differ. We introduce a benchmark of 83 published works that measures whether language models can tell nonlinear stories. For each work, we annotate one list of events in both orders, together with a story graph of causal dependencies, character knowledge, and the questions the telling raises and resolves. Given events in chronological order, all 19 models tell them, on average, more chronologically than the published works do; asked for a specific structure, they land within the human range about half the time. We then compare a model's stories of the same events under different conditions, using both an automated judge and 71 human readers. Both prefer the chronological story a model writes by default to the nonlinear one it writes on request, which readers find harder to follow in 81% of decisive judgments. Readers also prefer stories written from the story graph to stories constrained to the published telling order (72% of decisive judgments), a difference the judge does not detect. Our results suggest that following an instruction to reorder a story is not yet the same as telling it well out of order.

authors.name: Md. Tariquzzaman
authors.institution: Jashore University of Science and Technology

papers.title: CF-Splat: Closed-Form Triangle Splatting with Mesh Priors
papers.abstract: Splatting-based radiance-field representations have recently gained popularity in robotic perception, enabling high-quality novel-view synthesis (NVS) through explicit scene primitives. However, existing splatting methods typically rely on iterative nonlinear optimization that jointly optimizes millions of coupled primitive parameters, resulting in substantial computation time, peak GPU memory consumption, and susceptibility to local minima. In this paper, we propose CF-Splat, a novel closed-form triangle-splatting framework for efficient scene appearance estimation over a known mesh either pre-existing or provided by upstream mapping or reconstruction pipelines. Our key insight is that, by properly formulating the problem over the given mesh geometry and calibrated cameras, the rendered pixel colors can be expressed linearly with respect to the per-vertex spherical harmonics (SH) coefficients, allowing multi-view scene appearance estimation to be formulated as a global linear least-squares (LLS) problem without the need of iterative nonlinear optimization. To guarantee a well-posed solution under uneven multi-view observation coverage, we introduce adaptive SH regularization that constrains insufficiently supported high-order SH coefficients and yields a unique global minimizer. To ensure the scalability to large-scale scenes, we develop a triangle-structured matrix-free preconditioned conjugate-gradient solver that avoids explicitly constructing the large sparse normal system while producing the same LLS solution. Experiments on diverse real-world datasets demonstrate that CF-Splat achieves competitive or superior NVS quality compared with state-of-the-art splatting methods. While, CF-Splat requires approximately 27.5-378.0 times less computation time and 1.8 times lower peak GPU memory on average than 3DGS across scenes of different scales on a consumer-grade laptop.

papers.title: Two-element factors and finite bases for additively idempotent semirings
papers.abstract: For every additively idempotent semiring $S$ in the constant-free signature, $S$ is finitely based if and only if $S\times E$ is finitely based when $E=M_2$ or $T_2$. For each $E\in\{L_2,R_2,D_2,N_2\}$, both implications fail even for finite $S$: we give a finite finitely based semiring whose product with $E$ is nonfinitely based and a finite nonfinitely based semiring whose product with $E$ is finitely based.

papers.title: The linear positive torsor presentation and arithmetic purity of strong approximation
papers.abstract: In this article, we define a notion for varieties called linear positive torsor presentation. For varieties with a linear positive torsor presentation over number fields, we establish the arithmetic purity of strong approximation with the Brauer--Manin obstruction off the empty set. As a consequence, we recover arithmetic purity for smooth toric variety with no non-constant global section. Moreover, we classify the chain connected class for rational points on such varieties over any field of characteristic zero.

papers.title: IWOO: Wave Optics Optimizer Improved with Hybrid Strategies for Numerical Optimization and Engineering Applications
papers.abstract: The Wave Optics Optimizer (WOO) incorporates optical diffraction and interference into numerical optimization and has shown competitive performance in benchmarks and engineering applications. However, it can converge slowly, become trapped in local optima, and lose search effectiveness in later iterations. This paper proposes an Improved Wave Optics Optimizer (IWOO) that integrates four complementary strategies. First, a good point set and opposition-based learning are combined in GPS--OBL initialization to improve population quality and diversity. Second, an E-DM nonlinear perturbation mechanism is embedded in temporary triangle-based search to develop the TriEDM multi-path strategy and enhance search capability. Third, Correlation-Guided Groupwise Orthogonal Learning (CGOL) leverages relationships among decision variables to improve search efficiency while reducing computational overhead. Fourth, an adaptive stagnation-aware Runge--Kutta correction is introduced to mitigate premature convergence. IWOO is evaluated on the IEEE CEC2019, CEC2022, and CEC2017 benchmark suites against representative and high-performing optimizers, with ablation studies assessing the contribution of each strategy. Within the representative algorithm group, IWOO achieves Friedman ranks of 1.8000, 1.5833, and 1.4483 on CEC2019, CEC2022, and CEC2017, respectively. Tests on six constrained engineering optimization problems further demonstrate its competitive accuracy, stability, and practical applicability.

papers.title: The Impact of High-Mass Clusters on the Binary Black Hole Merger Rate over Cosmic Time
papers.abstract: We present a cosmological calculation of the binary black hole merger rate from dense star clusters, using a $\texttt{Cluster Monte Carlo}$ ($\texttt{CMC}$) model grid spanning the full observed parameter space of cluster mass, metallicity, and virial radius. For the first time, we incorporate $N=10^{7}$-particle $\texttt{CMC}$ models into this calculation, including a new solar-metallicity model, extending the $\texttt{CMC Cluster Catalog}$ to the most massive clusters observed in the local Universe. Using an analytic cluster formation model which convolves the cluster formation rate with delay-time distributions from our model suite, we find that the local cluster BBH merger rate is dominated by low-mass ($M_1 \lesssim 20\,M_\odot$) mergers originating from recently formed, high-metallicity clusters. While high-mass clusters are the primary sites of hierarchical (second-generation and higher) mergers, their contribution to the overall merger rate is suppressed by the exponential cutoff of the cluster initial mass function. The hierarchical merger rate is therefore highly sensitive to the exact value of the Schechter mass, $M_S$, suggesting that gravitational wave constraints on the hierarchical merger fraction can independently constrain the high-mass end of the cluster initial mass function. Our cluster formation model reproduces the observed present-day GC number density without fine tuning, and we find $M_S = 10^7\,M_\odot$ provides the best match to the observed Virgo GC mass distribution. For this value, $27\%$ of local dynamical mergers are hierarchical, compared to $18\%$ for the canonical value of $M_S = 10^{6.26}\,M_\odot$. Our merger weights, which we make publicly available, can be used for direct comparison with LVK distributions and other formation models.

papers.title: Building and calibrating a 3Di subgrid flood model for Hanoi, without a surveyed terrain model, drainage data, or rain gauges
papers.abstract: Urban hydrodynamic flood models typically rely on a surveyed terrain model, an explicit pipe drainage network, and rain gauge measurements, none of which were available for the inundation following Typhoon Matmo in My Dinh and Tay Mo, Hanoi, on 7 October 2025. The present study addresses this issue by documenting the construction and calibration of a 32.8 km^2 3Di subgrid model under severe data constraints, demonstrating how unmonitored catchments can be simulated using openly accessible sources. Specifically, a 1 m digital elevation model was systematically repaired for river and lake bathymetry, unsurveyed water bodies, road underpasses, and an excavation pit to re-establish essential overland flow paths. In addition, assigned infiltration rates across land-cover classes were utilized to stand in for the unrecorded subsurface sewer system, while half-hourly satellite precipitation from the IMERG Late product provided rainfall forcing for a closed two-dimensional domain. Model calibration was conducted against eight crowdsourced depth observations. The simulation results demonstrated that six observation points retained surface water and were closely aligned with the reported values within 2.2 cm. However, two peripheral locations along Tay Mo Road and Road 70 remained completely dry in the model. Because all eight points were utilized during parameter adjustment and no independent validation dataset was withheld, this correspondence reflects a calibration fit rather than an unconstrained predictive test.

papers.title: Isolating a Language Model's Judgment with a Label-Free Subspace
papers.abstract: Language models are often asked to make judgments: whether a proposed answer is correct, whether one statement follows logically from another, or whether a response is safe. Yet changing the instructions that specify how the judgment should be expressed can make the final answer less reliable, even for the same input. We ask whether this reflects a change in internal judgment or a failure to express it. Comparing hidden-state vectors for the same input under different instructions, we find that their differences concentrate in a low-dimensional expression subspace. We identify this subspace without benchmark labels and remove its contribution from a linear predictor to obtain an isolated judgment. Across correctness, entailment, and safety, the isolated judgment remains reliable under instructions not used to identify the subspace, even when the model's final answer and the original predictor degrade. When the judgment question is negated, isolation raises the predictor's AUROC from 0.504 to 0.825 for entailment and from 0.480 to 0.891 for safety. We also find that judgment is readable in earlier layers, before the expression subspace begins to disrupt the predictor. Together, these results provide a way to separate judgment from expression and recover internal judgments even when the model's final answers are unreliable.

authors.name: Dongman Lee
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense
papers.abstract: To improve task performance while encouraging desirable response properties, LLM post-training often combines a primary reward (e.g., correctness) with auxiliary rewards (e.g., brevity or efficiency). However, how these rewards are aggregated can critically affect training outcomes. We show that symmetric aggregation, which treats reward channels equally, can induce a failure where aggregate reward improves while primary-task performance degrades, even when individual rewards are meaningful. We investigate this aggregation-induced failure through a one-step multi-reward decision formulation, characterizing when it constitutes multi-reward hacking. We prove that, under symmetric aggregation, deterministic conditional-mean GRPO converges to auxiliary-favoring behavior when auxiliary rewards are more reliably obtained, regardless of initialization. We propose Trust-Anchored Gating (TAG), which first elects an anchor channel based on the policy drift induced by optimizing each channel alone, then gates auxiliary credit on anchor satisfaction. Unlike calibration-sensitive static reweighting, TAG structurally eliminates credit for auxiliary-only outcomes while preserving additional credit for joint success. In the same analytical setting, TAG provably reverses this selection, converging to the primary-favoring action from any initialization when the primary channel is anchored. Experiments across Qwen and Llama models on mathematics and program synthesis reveal substantial degradation under symmetric, constrained, and normalized aggregation, whereas TAG mitigates this failure. On Qwen3-4B with a brevity reward, TAG achieves 0.581 pass@4 versus 0.220 for additive aggregation, while shortening responses by 44% relative to correctness-only training.

papers.title: Universal Dynamic Scaling for Sub-Yield Aging and Over-Yield Rejuvenation in A Cyclically Driven Metallic Glass
papers.abstract: Whether sub-yield aging and over-yield rejuvenation in cyclically deformed amorphous solids share a common physical origin or arise from distinct microscopic mechanisms remains a fundamental yet unresolved debate. Using molecular dynamics simulations of a metallic glass, we resolve this duality by uncovering a unified dynamic clock that dictates energy landscape navigation across both regimes. We show that the transition between regimes reflects a fundamental shift in energy injection pathways: (i) In the over-yield regime, rejuvenation is driven as a first-order response to macroscopic plastic shear work derived from Herschel-Bulkley non-linear rheological scaling. (ii) In contrast, this macroscopic work scaling fails in the sub-yield regime, where early-stage energy landscape elevation and subsequent cyclic aging are instead governed by second-order localized elastic stress fluctuations acting as a mechanical catalyst and noise source, respectively. Intense high-rate agitation increases the escape probability from deeper potential energy minima, thereby suppressing the retention efficiency of structural relaxation. By identifying these localized fluctuations as the primary origin of rate-attenuated sub-yield relaxation, we establish an exact scaling identity relating the relaxation attenuation exponent to the stress fluctuation exponent. This work directly bridges non-linear rheology with stress fluctuation dynamics, providing a unified framework to predict and manipulate structural evolution in amorphous solids.

authors.name: Rui Wan
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Limin Wang
authors.institution: Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University

papers.title: Seeing Both the Forest and the Trees: Reusing Holistic 3D Priors for Part-Decomposed Generation
papers.abstract: Generating 3D assets with explicit parts requires two properties at once: geometric detail inside each part and structural coherence across the whole object. Recent image-conditioned 3D generation models adopt a structured 3D representation that anchors tokens to explicit spatial positions, capturing both properties, but their output remains a single fused mesh. We ask how a part-decomposed generation model can inherit both properties of these holistic priors, and answer with STRUCTPARTS, a framework whose core technical contribution is a dual-frame coordinate interleaving mechanism: each shape latent is interpreted under both a part-local and an object-global reference frame, and processed through a global-local inter-leaved transformer that simultaneously reuses the prior's geometric detail at the part scale and its structural coherence at the whole-object scale. As its structural input, STRUCTPARTS uses a segmented mesh scaffold, a coarse mesh paired with a face-level segmentation mask kept entirely within the prior's native 3D representation. With only lightweight finetuning, both intra-part detail and inter-part coherence emerge from the same pretrained weights. On PartObjaverse-Tiny, STRUCTPARTS matches or surpasses prior part-decomposed models at a fraction of their training cost, while naturally supporting part-mesh refinement and part-level editing.

authors.name: Binbin Huang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Shenghua Gao
authors.institution: Chinese Center For Disease Control and Prevention

papers.title: Defense Filters for Robust Learning of Partially Observed Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: Robust estimation of unknown system dynamics from partial observations under attack is a core challenge in learning for control, increasingly critical in multi-agent networks subject to adversarial data poisoning. Existing methods either require highly restrictive assumptions on the adversary or yield weak error bounds. In this paper, we consider identifying partially observed linear dynamical systems subject to adversarial attacks with an attack probability $p < 0.5$ at each time. We propose a defense-filtering framework leveraging knowledge of the observation matrix to construct a defense filter satisfying full column rank and subspace separability conditions, which enables the evaluation of a single-attack scenario against observed data. Using this framework, we analyze the constrained $\ell_2$-norm estimator and establish finite-sample error bounds for recovering the Markov parameter matrix up to a linear transformation. This is the first approach to provide provable system identification guarantees via a defense filter for partially observed systems subject to harsh environments where the attack probability approaches $0.5$.

papers.title: PW-Pruning: Phase-Aware Expert Selection for Speech-Centric Omni-Modal Models
papers.abstract: Sparse routing reduces per-token computation but leaves the full expert bank resident in memory. We study expert pruning for speech-centric omni-modal models, where pooling calibration statistics can obscure the different expert demands of acoustic-input processing and text-answer generation. We propose PW-Pruning, a phase-aware extension of DO-ACP that constructs separate importance-weighted kernels for acoustic-prefill and teacher-forced answer tokens, then combines phase-weighted log-determinant marginal gains to select one static expert bank. On Qwen3-Omni, retaining 32 of 128 experts per layer improves MMAU-mini and MMSU accuracy over matched pooled selection by 3.20 and 4.38 percentage points, respectively, after supervised fine-tuning, averaged over three runs. Single-phase and shuffled-label controls on this public backbone suggest that semantic phase information contributes to these gains. Experiments on a non-public Qwen3.5-Omni backbone and English-only zero-shot evaluation of Nemotron provide complementary evidence. Across the tested Qwen budgets, AU gains are larger under stronger pruning, without inference-time mask switching.

authors.name: Xuanfan Ni
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

papers.title: Disentangling Multi-epoch Single-lined Binary Star Spectra to Reveal Interstellar Medium Features via MCMC
papers.abstract: Diffuse Interstellar Bands (DIBs) are interstellar absorption features with unidentified carriers in the optical and near-infrared spectra. When observed in cool star spectra, they are heavily contaminated by stellar lines. Traditional methods rely on template matching to remove the stellar component, but their accuracy is fundamentally limited by template quality. We present a template-independent algorithm that separates stellar and interstellar features in binary star spectra by exploiting orbital motion: stellar lines shift with changing radial velocity (RV), whereas DIBs remain stationary in the rest frame. The MCMC-RVSD algorithm, implemented as an RV-based Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo framework, fits both components simultaneously. We validated our approach by applying it to mock spectra simulating LAMOST medium-resolution observations. The method precisely recovers the parameters of DIB $λ$6614. It performs reliably for spectra with $R=3000$-$7500$. We applied the method to 434 real binary sources from the LAMOST medium-resolution survey and introduced the MCMC autocorrelation time ($τ_{\mathrm{DIB}}$) to assess the fit quality. Our analysis shows that an RV span $>20$ km s$^{-1}$ is the primary driver of successful line separation. Denser orbital sampling provides further improvement, and the algorithm remains robust against typical observational noise at SNR $>50$ and RV errors $<5$ km s$^{-1}$. Under ideal conditions, our approach yields significantly smaller parameter uncertainties than traditional template matching. Additionally, the MCMC-RVSD algorithm can also handle multi-stellar line contamination, non-Gaussian DIBs and other DIBs by adjusting model and prior settings. This algorithm provides a reliable, general-purpose tool for precise measurement of interstellar features in time-domain spectroscopic surveys.

authors.name: Ji-Wei Shi
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Selection-Safe Conformal Early Exit: Distribution-Free Coverage under Adaptive Depth
papers.abstract: Calibrating a conformal prediction set at each early exit does not preserve coverage once a data-dependent exit is selected. We construct one terminal path score from prefix maxima, calibrate a single split-conformal quantile, and return nested prefix sets that all contain the valid terminal set. The guarantee is selection-safe without an alpha/L correction and holds simultaneously for every post-calibration label-free stopping policy that preserves terminal-set containment. We also bound the efficiency cost of the path maximum by the empirical tail of the early-over-terminal score excess. Across eight encoder task-backbone cells, pathwise selection attains macro coverage 0.901 versus 0.814 for naive layerwise selection, with average set size 1.41 and latency fraction 0.71. On CIFAR-100 with a 24-exit ViT-L/16 (n_cal=500), first-eligible stopping at budget b=4 attains coverage 0.902, set size 2.76, and latency fraction 0.57, and the same calibration supports deployment-time budget changes without refitting. In a joint exit-count/calibration-size sweep at n=100, pathwise set size moves only from 3.02 to 3.11 as exits increase from 4 to 24, while Bonferroni degenerates to the full label space for 12 or more exits. Paired comparison against MinSE valid selection at (n,L)=(100,24) gives a set-size difference of 0.80 [0.47, 1.13]. Full-vocabulary decoder experiments remain a negative boundary, with sets of 7,162-9,620 tokens. Pathwise calibration is most useful when candidate exits are many relative to calibration size, when budgets change after calibration, and when shallow heads return actionable sets.

papers.title: Learning Intrinsic Dynamics in Latent World Models
papers.abstract: Learning intrinsic dynamics---the relationship between actions and their consequences---is essential for world models. However, visual variations unrelated to the underlying control process can obscure this relationship in learned representations. We investigate the connection between action predictability, defined as the ability to reconstruct an action from consecutive latent states, and the preservation of intrinsic dynamics. Our central hypothesis is that encouraging action predictability discourages representations from discarding the distinctions between different actions and their consequences. We provide two complementary forms of evidence for this connection. Theoretically, we derive a positive lower bound on squared inverse prediction error when the encoder merges distinguishable outcomes of different actions from the same state and appearance, and show that forward prediction can still be exact on those transitions. Empirically, controlled appearance-diversity comparisons, supervision interventions, and latent probes support the role of action prediction in preserving control-relevant transition information. We instantiate action predictability with Concat IDM, which predicts actions from concatenated latent states and updates the shared encoder using action labels already available in offline trajectories, without changing the test-time planner. Across three independent training runs on Push-T with 24 appearances, Concat IDM increases planning success from 9.1% to 77.2%; its paired improvement is 52.9 percentage points larger than that observed with a single appearance. Together, these findings support action predictability as an inductive bias toward intrinsic dynamics and demonstrate the practical benefits of Concat IDM for latent planning under visual diversity.

authors.name: Yuanhong Zhang
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Policy-Gradient Transfer under a Shared State Estimator
papers.abstract: This paper considers the problem of policy-gradient transfer from a simulator to a physical plant when both are controlled through the same fixed state estimator. The plant and the simulator are partially observed nonlinear systems with additive Gaussian noise of common known covariance whose dynamics and observation models differ, and the controller is a squashed Gaussian policy with uniformly bounded latent mean and first two parameter derivatives. We derive a bound on the difference between the plant and simulator policy gradients that is linear in the noise-weighted model error and requires no estimator-accuracy guarantee, because the shared estimator is a common post-processing of the measurements and the data-processing inequality compares the trajectory laws without an estimation-error term. Based on this bound, we derive an occupancy-weighted refinement, a sufficient condition for the simulator gradient to be an ascent direction for the plant, and a bound on the expected squared plant gradient at a random iterate of a finite simulator-training run with optimization, truncation and model-error terms. Simulation results on a scalar system and a pendulum are presented to validate the theoretical results.

papers.title: In-Context Preference-Conditioned Pareto Set Learning from Limited Offline Data
papers.abstract: Multi-objective optimization involves diverse preferences over conflicting objectives. Rather than returning a finite set of trade-off solutions, preference-conditioned Pareto set learning seeks to map a specified preference directly to a corresponding Pareto optimal solution. Yet in many real-world scenarios, optimization must proceed offline without further objective evaluations, leaving only a limited static dataset that sparsely covers the decision and objective spaces. Existing methods either optimize separately for each preference or train a problem-specific Pareto solution model, requiring repeated search across preferences or repeated training across problems. We introduce in-context preference-conditioned Pareto set learning (ICPSL), a framework that amortizes both preference-wise solution search and problem-specific model construction. ICPSL pretrains a foundation-style hypernetwork on a large and diverse set of synthetic prior data. Given the offline observations of an unseen problem, the pretrained hypernetwork learns to generate a problem-specific, preference-conditioned Pareto solution model in a single forward pass. The generated model can then be reused to predict solutions for arbitrary preferences without problem-specific training or preference-wise search. Experiments on synthetic and real-world problems show that ICPSL produces high-quality Pareto solutions while providing substantial speedups in problem-specific solution-model construction.

papers.title: Interlocked Vortex Order in the Frustrated $A_3$V$_9$Te$_{13}$ Lattice ($A$=Cs,Rb)
papers.abstract: Recently synthesized $A_3$V$_9$Te$_{13}$ ($A$ = Cs, Rb) provides a unique platform for exploring the interplay between geometric frustration, magnetism, and correlated electronic states beyond conventional kagome systems. Based on first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that the frustrated V sublattice naturally stabilizes a robust vortex or anti-vortex antiferromagnetic ground state, whose total energy is substantially lower than all other configurations. In addition, the Heisenberg model analysis show strong constraints on the ground state magnetic configuration, such that fixing spin configuration of 1 triangle propagates and fixes all others. The vortex or anti-vortex phase hosts electronic structures reminiscent of kagome metals, including Dirac-like band crossings, van Hove singularities, and flat bands near the Fermi level. Owing to the noncollinear spin texture and quasi-two-dimensional magnetic character, the Néel temperature exhibits an extremely weak dependence on both the magnitude and direction of external magnetic fields, consistent with experimental observations. For Cs-based compound, the ground state band structure is metallic with 6 Weyl points in the BZ; while for the Rb-based compound, spin--orbit coupling opens an approximately 27-meV gap at ambient pressure due to the lifted C$_3$ symmetry. Our results establish $A_3$V$_9$Te$_{13}$ as a promising platform for studying frustration-driven chiral magnetism and its interplay with topological electronic states.

authors.name: H. -Q. Yuan
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology

papers.title: Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Continuous diffusion language models (CDLMs) offer an alternative approach to parallel language generation; however, most existing studies directly use transformer architectures from either causal large language models (LLMs) or Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) for image generation, which were not optimized for CDLMs. In this paper, we conduct a systematic study on Transformer architectures for CDLMs and introduce Language Diffusion Transformer (LangDiT), combining feature and query-key normalization, wider noise conditioning, likelihood-shortcut gradient routing and calibration, and confidence-gated training self-conditioning. LangDiT significantly reduces generation perplexity in matched LangFlow comparisons, establishing a new state of the art in continuous language generation across different model formulations. Using LangFlow as a representative CDLM, LangDiT as a plug-and-play backbone leads to a new state-of-the-art model with a generation perplexity (GenPPL) of 21.72 using 1024 NFEs and 44.72 GenPPL using 128 NFEs on the unconditional generation of 1024-token sequences on the OpenWebText dataset. When adapted to Plaid-style CDLM formulations, LangDiT results in a new leading GenPPL of 11.33 using 1024 denoising NFEs, and 27.51 GenPPL using 128 denoising NFEs. These gains are achieved while retaining each model's underlying representation, training objective, and inference sampler, isolating transformer architecture as a fundamental source of improvement. Our study identifies architectural design as an important source of improvement in continuous diffusion language models.

papers.title: Visual Sanad: Auditing Vision-Language Models for False Acceptance of Qur'anic Citations
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used to interpret religious, educational, and culturally sensitive visual content, yet their reliability on citation verification remains underexplored. We introduce Visual Sanad, a controlled benchmark for testing whether VLMs falsely accept incorrect Qur'anic verse attributions when the same quote-reference pair is rendered under different visual framings. The benchmark contains 2,400 rendered images built from 100 English Qur'an verses, four factual states per verse, and six visual conditions ranging from plain text to decorative and authority-framed layouts. All quote-reference pairs were source-checked and human-audited before rendering. Across 24 full model-prompt runs, we observe a sharp capability split. Proprietary API-served VLMs range from near-perfect citation verification to moderate false acceptance, whereas recent open-weight VLMs often show weak discrimination and default to VALID on most images. De-biased prompting can reduce false acceptance, but often by shifting the decision threshold toward INVALID rather than by producing strong citation discrimination. Visual Sanad therefore exposes a culturally grounded multimodal factuality failure: fluent VLMs may treat displayed religious citations as self-authenticating unless they have strong citation-verification ability.

papers.title: When Models Misread Ink: Auditing VLMs for Arabic Calligraphy Recognition
papers.abstract: Arabic calligraphy is a high-stakes cultural visual domain for Muslim communities, yet VLM evaluations rarely test its fine-grained script traditions. We audit 12 VLMs on a cleaned 1,195-image six-way benchmark using numeric, visual-cue, and Diwani-first prompts. In this closed-set setting, the best numeric-prompt accuracy is 60.9% for closed/API models and 47.2% for open-weight models. The main failure is default-label collapse: every numeric run is dominated by a single label taking 33-63% of predictions, against an 18.8% majority-class baseline. For 8 of 12 models the default is Thuluth; GPT-4o labels 52.9% of all images as Thuluth although it is only 18.1% of the set. Prompting helps unevenly: visual cues move accuracy by more than 10 points for some models but hurt others, and foregrounding Diwani often relocates the default rather than removing it. Arabic calligraphy recognition is therefore a compact, culturally grounded stress test for VLM robustness and for measuring which visual traditions become legible to automated systems.

papers.title: Characterizations in terms of Generalized Inverses
papers.abstract: Using simply outer inverse and their differences, we characterize many known classes of rings including von Neumann regular, unit-regular, exchange, clean, and strongly clean rings.

papers.title: Radon measures in the Berkovich space and generically stable measures in ACVF
papers.abstract: In this paper we study Keisler measures in models of ACVF. We give analogue definitions for a Keisler measure to be orthogonal to the value group and stably dominated using unique extensions, in the spirit of invariant types. Our first theorem shows that a global $M$-invariant Keisler measure is generically stable if and only if it is orthogonal to the value group if and only if it is stably dominated. This theorem is later applied to prove that for a projective variety $X$ defined over a spherically complete model $M$ of ACVF whose value group is $\mathbb R$, there is a one-to-one correspondance between the generically stable measures centered on $X$ and the Radon measures on its Berkovich analyfication of $X$. Such theorem is a measure-theoretic extension of the celebrated work of Hrushovski-Loeser, which establishes a correspondence between generically stable types with the points of the Berkovich analyfication $X^{an}$ of a projective variety$X$. As an application, normalized Chambert-Loir measures associated with semipositive continuous metrics naturally give rise examples of generically stable Keisler measures.

papers.title: Disentangling geometry & growth in cosmic neutrino mass constraints: a more physical split and diagnostic
papers.abstract: Recent cosmological data hint at a neutrino mass sum below the minimum value allowed by the neutrino mass oscillation experiments, with a preference for the opposite of massive neutrinos ("negative" neutrino masses). Since massive neutrinos impact the expansion history of the Universe, which in turn modifies the growth of structure, we ask whether such a preference originates from the observed geometry or structure growth, and whether the two agree. In this paper, we introduce a more physical split of $\sum m_ν$ into parameters $\sum m_ν^{geo}$ and $\sum m_ν^{growth}$ based on their physical effects, with extension to negative values. We split the expansion rate at the Boltzmann-code level: $\sum m_ν^{geo}$ sets $H(z)$ for distance computation, and $\sum m_ν^{growth}$ sets $H(z)$ for perturbation evolution. Combining Planck primary CMB, Planck+ACT+SPT CMB lensing and DESI BAO data, we find similar sensitivity and "negative" preference from geometry and growth with $\sum m_ν^{geo} = -0.07\pm0.10$ eV (68% C.L.) and $\sum m_ν^{growth} = -0.13^{+0.10}_{-0.12}$ eV (68% C.L.). The difference of the two is a null test of the $Λ$CDM model, passed by current data at $0.4σ$ level. Forecasts on Advanced SO CMB and DESI DR3 BAO show that $0.058$ eV would be rejected at $3.0σ$ from the geometry channel alone, if the negative mean of $\sum m_ν^{geo} = -0.07$ eV persists. The two channels can also provide a powerful new diagnostic between possible origins of the neutrino mass tension. With future CMB and BAO data, our Fisher forecasts show that an incorrect dark energy model displaces $\sum m_ν^{geo}$ from $0.058$ eV by $3.1$-$4.2σ$ and $\sum m_ν^{growth}$ by $1.1$-$1.3σ$, while an underestimated reionization optical depth reverses the pattern, $2.7$-$3.6σ$ in $\sum m_ν^{growth}$ against at most $0.23σ$ in $\sum m_ν^{geo}$. (Abridged)

authors.name: Hanyue Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Semisimplicity and Rigidity of the Kontsevich--Zorich Cocycle for Products of Strata
papers.abstract: We study the Kontsevich--Zorich cocycle, its fixed tensor constructions, and their finite direct sums over products of strata of Abelian differentials. The acting groups are closed subgroups $G\subset(\mathrm{SL}_2\mathbb R)^n$ that, up to factor permutations and coordinatewise conjugation by rotations, are products of diagonal $\mathrm{SL}_2\mathbb R$ blocks and a finite central group. For ergodic invariant probability measures, we prove Deligne-type semisimplicity: the bundles admit Hodge-compatible decompositions into $G$-invariant pieces $V_i\otimes_{A_i}W_i$, where $A_i$ are division algebras, $V_i$ carry pure variations of Hodge structure, and the multiplicity spaces $W_i$ carry finite direct sums of pure Hodge structures. Every invariant subbundle arises from $A_i$-submodules of the $W_i$. If block marginal measures have smooth local supports and are locally equivalent to smooth volume, Hodge-orthogonal projections onto invariant subbundles are locally polynomial in period coordinates on the normalized support. The proof obtains a local product-of-quadrics model and joint polynomiality from polynomiality along stable and unstable leaves. On the cone obtained by scaling each diagonal block together, projection coefficients admit homogeneous degree-zero expressions with integral powers of reciprocal block areas. For the full product group $(\mathrm{SL}_2\mathbb R)^n$, single-stratum measure classification supplies the support hypothesis, yielding rigidity for every ergodic invariant probability measure. Under the transported support hypothesis, arbitrary coordinatewise $\mathrm{SL}_2\mathbb R$-conjugates also admit polynomial equivariant projectors, though not necessarily Hodge-orthogonal. Genus-two examples show that nonrotational conjugation can destroy Deligne-torus invariance, and independent factor scalings can require square roots of area functions.

papers.title: DPA-MoE: A Runtime Precision Control Framework for MoE Inference
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models reduce computation by routing each token to a small set of experts, but each selected expert is still used at a fixed precision. We present DPA-MoE, a runtime precision control framework that makes routed experts any-precision. DPA-MoE encodes expert feed-forward weights as prefix-decodable chunks using SharedScale AnyBCQ, profiles per-expert reconstruction residuals offline, and allocates chunks at inference time using live router gate scores. This post-routing allocation lets a single encoded MoE checkpoint operate at multiple effective weight budgets without retraining or re-encoding. Experiments on Qwen3-30B-A3B and DeepSeekMoE-16B show that DPA-MoE improves KL divergence and downstream accuracy over uniform chunk allocation at matched budgets, with modest steady-state throughput overhead in our prototype.

papers.title: Directed impulsive molecular dynamics reveal energy-routing pathways of bond cleavage in TATB
papers.abstract: Responses of energetic materials to external stimuli involve more than uniform thermalization. Understanding directional energy redistribution is essential for structural and ignition design. Here, we use TATB as an example to construct a vibrationally faithful machine-learning potential from only 4,630 configurations. To resolve the elusive nonequilibrium energy flow, we develop directed impulsive molecular dynamics, a statistically controlled protocol that repeatedly deposits equal kinetic energy along selected vibrational modes. By amplifying mode-specific responses while tracking the ensuing nonequilibrium evolution, this approach turns energy redistribution into a directly traceable routing process. We find that initial bond cleavage depends strongly on the initially excited mode, rather than being determined by bond-cleavage barriers alone. Specifically, modes that readily trigger reaction efficiently channel energy towards a bond cleavage coordinate, whereas modes that are less effective at inducing break divert energy into soft-like modes or trap it in modes from which energy flow is inefficient.

papers.title: RAG-RST: Retrieved Exemplars as In-Context Discourse Schema for RST Parsing
papers.abstract: In Rhetorical Structure Theory (RST), each edge of a discourse tree carries a nuclearity label, marking which span holds the central content, and a relation drawn from a closed inventory of functional categories. Neither label is a surface property: the same two clauses can be Elaboration or Background depending on rhetorical intent, and the boundary between them is fixed by annotation convention rather than by lexical cues. Predicting these labels therefore requires a formal discourse schema, and exposure to discourse-rich pretraining text does not supply it: given only a target EDU pair, a strong LLM recovers nuclearity at 0.794 F1 and relation at 0.738 F1. We propose RAG-RST, a retrieval-augmented framework that supplies this schema as in-context demonstration rather than through parameter updates, raising nuclearity to 0.846 F1 and relation to 0.788 F1 with no training. Two configurations are compared: a precomputed strategy that labels all EDU pairs before parsing, and a dynamic strategy that retrieves at each reduce step, so that the exemplars reaching the generator depend on the reductions the parser has already committed to. Both outperform existing RST parsers across span, nuclearity, relation, and full tree metrics, with the dynamic variant consistently strongest. Two properties of the retrieved schema emerge: its utility is bounded in number, saturating and then declining beyond fifty exemplars, and it depends on structural position. Both indicate that a formal linguistic schema can be supplied to a foundation model as a demonstration rather than trained into its parameters.

papers.title: Double covers of tori for p=2 and genuine functions
papers.abstract: In his work on $L$-embeddings and double covers of tori over local fields, Kaletha associates to a maximal torus $S$ in a connected reductive group a canonical double cover $S(F)_{\pm}$ and introduces a genuine sign function $a_S$ associated to a genuine character of $S(F)_{\pm}$. We give two constructions of this genuine sign function over a non-archimedean local field, including residual characteristic $2$. The first uses rootwise lifts to the double cover; the second, in characteristic zero, uses the exponential map. Under explicit ramification conditions, both constructions yield genuine sign functions which, in odd residual characteristic, agree with his construction. We also illustrate the case of $\mathrm{PGL}_2$. A brief announcement of the first construction appears in Appendix D of that work.

papers.title: Private Retrieval Augmented Generation via Random Projection
papers.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances the capabilities of large language models (LLMs) by querying external structured knowledge. However, it can also introduce privacy risks by leaking sensitive information from the retrieval datastore. We propose a simple method to preserve datastore privacy in RAG systems via random projection. By applying the same projection to both datastore embeddings and query embeddings, our method provably preserves semantic similarity between queries and retrieved items while substantially mitigating data extraction attacks. Across multiple RAG architectures and datasets, we show that this lightweight approach achieves superior retrieval and generation performance compared to prior methods which leverage formal differential privacy (DP) guarantees, while exhibiting comparable empirical privacy under strong attack models. Our results for the first time suggest that random projection can serve as a competitive and practical baseline for privacy-preserving RAG systems.

papers.title: CoTranslator: Reverse to Forward Chain-of-Thought Translator for Reasoning Distillation
papers.abstract: Reasoning distillation requires chain-of-thought (CoT) data with correct answers, but obtaining such data efficiently remains challenging. Forward CoT generation (FCG) followed by rejection sampling (RS) produces verified, question-only responses, yet may require many teacher calls for difficult problems. Reverse CoT generation (RCG) is cheaper because it conditions on the known answer, but access to this answer can lead to post-hoc rationalization and a mismatch with the student's answer-free inference setting. We propose CoTranslator, which learns to translate reverse CoT responses toward the distribution of verified forward responses. Trained on a small set of paired reverse and rejection-sampled forward responses, it supports large-scale generation and verification of student training data. Across six student models evaluated on six mathematics benchmarks, CoTranslator improves average accuracy over semantic suppression by up to $5.82$ percentage points. For two 4B students, it retains $95.0\%$ of rejection sampling's average accuracy while using $35.9\%$ of its estimated compute. Without retraining, the same translator transfers to a new mathematics dataset, a different teacher, and STEM problems, improving average STEM accuracy by $4.88$ and $4.31$ percentage points for 4B and 8B students, respectively. These results show that CoTranslator offers an efficient and transferable approach to reasoning distillation.

papers.title: Tokenized Joint Source-Network Coding for Loss-Resilient Video Streaming
papers.abstract: For decades, conventional video streaming systems have relied on packet-level forward error correction (FEC) codes and retransmissions to ensure reliable video delivery. However, in real-time communications, FEC is inherently inefficient under unknown and time-varying packet-loss conditions, while retransmission can incur excessive latency and fail to meet stringent playout deadlines. Emerging deep joint source-channel coding (DeepJSCC) provides an alternative by learning channel-noise-resilient representations, yet its tight coupling with the physical layer makes it difficult to integrate into today's layered network architectures and protocols. In this paper, we propose TokJSNC, a simple-but-effective tokenized joint source-network coding paradigm for packet-loss-resilient video streaming. Rather than first compressing video into a compact bitstream and then protecting it with packet-level FEC, TokJSNC directly encodes video into variable-length discrete token-stream, whose transmission rate is jointly adapted to video content complexity and network conditions. By exploiting the spatiotemporal correlations among learned video tokens, TokJSNC enables robust video reconstruction over a wide range of packet-loss rates without explicit FEC or retransmissions. Consequently, TokJSNC brings the JSCC-like graceful degradation property to the network layer while remaining compatible with existing network architectures and transport protocols. Experimental results show that TokJSNC maintains an average playback frame rate above 22 fps even at a 70% packet-loss rate, whereas the best-performing baseline drops below 12 fps. Overall, TokJSNC establishes a practical pathway for repurposing modern generative video tokenizers for loss-resilient streaming, while providing a fundamental framework for video token communications.

papers.title: Can Visual Generation Expand What Unified Multimodal Models Know?
papers.abstract: Unified multimodal models (UMMs) receive image-generation supervision that exposes them to visual information not fully documented in text. Can learning to generate images expand what pretrained models know? We introduce Knowledge Transfer Probing (KTP), a controlled protocol that supplies new knowledge through image-generation training and tests its accessibility through text-only question answering. Across seven knowledge categories and three UMMs, we observe direct but uneven transfer from visual supervision to language. Motivated by these observations, we successively introduce Textual Alignment and Interleaved Image--Text Alignment, which connect generation and answering through shared knowledge and interleaved responses, respectively. Guidance on selected entities can improve knowledge access on other entities without QA supervision, with additional gains from interleaved alignment. Further analysis shows that knowledge correctly reproduced in images is often more accessible through text, although substantial gaps remain between the two forms of access. These findings support visual generation as a source of knowledge beyond textual supervision, and motivate joint investigation of training data design and model architecture to make this knowledge more broadly accessible.

papers.title: On the Complexity of Finding Stationary Points in Stochastic $(L_0, L_1)$-Smooth Nonconvex Optimization
papers.abstract: We study the stochastic first-order oracle (SFO) complexity of finding $ε$-stationary points of $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth nonconvex functions. Under bounded-variance noise, existing analyses of normalized and clipped stochastic gradient descent (SGD) establish optimal dependence on $ε$ and $L_0$, but the jointly optimal dependence on $L_0$, $L_1$, and $ε$ remains unclear. We resolve this question for an unbiased SFO whose gradient noise has a $p$th central moment bounded by $σ^p$ for some $σ\geq 0$, where $p\in(1,2]$.Specifically, we establish an SFO lower bound of $Ω\big(\big(σ^{\frac{p}{p-1}}ε^{-\frac{p}{p-1}}+1\big) (L_0 Δε^{-2}+L_1Δε^{-1})\big)$, where $Δ>0$ is the initial optimality gap.This bound identifies an unavoidable contribution proportional to $L_1ε^{-1}Δ$. We also prove that mini-batch (smoothed) normalized SGD can attain a matching upper bound, thereby establishing the optimal SFO complexity.

authors.name: Luo Luo
authors.institution: East China University of Science and Technology

papers.title: The Dormant Spiking Neuron: A State-Driven Mechanism for Efficient Spiking Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) offer a compelling pathway toward energy-efficient artificial intelligence, fundamentally anchored in presynaptic input-driven sparsity. However, a substantial yet chronically overlooked source of computational overhead persists: the continuous subthreshold dynamics of postsynaptic neurons. Quantitative analysis reveals that up to 44% of neurons in an ImageNet-trained ResNet-18 model reside in a deeply inhibited state, imposing a persistent computational burden despite having a negligible probability of firing. To address this inefficiency, the Dormant Spiking Neuron (DSN) model is introduced. By incorporating a state-driven dynamic gate, the DSN allows a neuron to enter a dormant state when its membrane potential falls below a predefined negative threshold, dynamically pruning redundant computations at the instance level. Crucially, this dormancy mechanism is directly integrated into the neuronal dynamics and trained end-to-end via backpropagation through time using surrogate gradients, enabling the network to actively learn a robust dormancy policy that adaptively preserves critical information flow. Extensive experiments across static and neuromorphic datasets demonstrate that the DSN framework consistently reduces computational energy by 40% to over 70%. Notably, on the large-scale ImageNet dataset, the DSN outperforms state-of-the-art static pruning techniques at comparable reported cost reductions and simultaneously improves the corresponding baseline SNN accuracy by 1.34%. By establishing a trainable, state-driven sparsity paradigm orthogonal to conventional input-driven methods, the DSN unlocks synergistic efficiency gains, presenting an effective approach for advancing neuromorphic computing.

papers.title: Coverage-Preserving Self-Healing in Partially Observable 3D UAV Swarm Networks via an Advection-Diffusion Graph Transformer
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the resilience and self-healing of unmanned aerial vehicle swarm communication networks under severe network partitioning in complex and adversarial environments. To address limited global observability after damage, we develop a damage-state inference mechanism that enables the ground control station (GCS) to infer global failures from sparse local reports without transmitting location-sensitive coordinates. To recover multi-cluster partitioned topologies, we then propose AdDiff-GT, a physics-inspired graph Transformer that incorporates advection-diffusion dynamics into a node-supernode hybrid graph. Local message propagation captures intra-cluster structural relationships, while global attention models inter-cluster interactions. A weighted composite loss jointly considers connectivity restoration, maneuvering cost, motion consistency, inter-cluster coordination, and spatial preservation during model training. We further develop a meta-learning strategy for transferable initialization across damage patterns and swarm scales, enabling efficient online GCS adaptation and distributed airborne inference. Simulations on 8,000 partitioned scenarios, including 5,000 large-scale cases, show that AdDiff-GT achieves effective topology recovery and spatial preservation over six representative baselines. Meta-learning reduces online planning overhead with a minor increase in recovery steps, balancing prior knowledge transfer and online adaptation.

papers.title: GNN-Guided Local Refinement for Efficient Layout Decomposition with DSA-MP
papers.abstract: Multiple patterning lithography (MPL) has been widely used to improve lithography resolution in advanced nodes, but it faces cost limits as feature sizes shrink. Directed self-assembly (DSA) offers a cost-effective complement, extending the resolution of optical lithography to sub-10 nm and beyond. Integrating DSA into MPL (DSA-MP) further enhances the resolution of contact/via patterning. Nevertheless, growing design complexity exposes the limits of existing decomposition methods, which struggle to balance solution quality and runtime, and neglect edge-to-edge spacing constraints of DSA templates, compromising manufacturability. To address these issues, we introduce a new conflict graph model capturing the previously overlooked constraints and develop a local refinement strategy powered by the graph neural network, enabling efficient and scalable layout decomposition. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves higher solution quality with faster convergence than state-of-the-art methods, while maintaining robustness across layout scales, design styles, technology nodes, and varying mask counts.

papers.title: Noise-Space Reward Alignment for Few-Step Generative Models
papers.abstract: Few-step generative models produce high-quality samples in one or a few evaluations. However, steering them toward desired properties remains difficult, especially when only black-box reward evaluations are available. While one could apply approaches developed for iterative diffusion and flow-based models, such as direct RL fine-tuning or test-time scaling, we find that neither transfers well to the few-step regime: direct fine-tuning suffers from severe reward over-optimization, and test-time scaling sacrifices the efficiency advantage of few-step generation. We propose Noise Policy Optimization (NPO), which explicitly targets the alignment problem for few-step generative models. The key idea is to learn an amortized flow policy over the initial noise space of the generator. The trained policy transports Gaussian noise to a reward-tilted noise distribution, whose pushforward distribution through the frozen generator is exactly the reward-tilted output distribution. By keeping the generator frozen, we can effectively utilize the knowledge encoded in the pretrained model, yielding a better reward-quality trade-off than direct fine-tuning. The amortized policy moves the search cost into training, so inference adds only a lightweight noise sampling step on top of the pretrained model. To improve sample efficiency during training, we use ELBO-based likelihood estimation that requires only sampled endpoints rather than simulated trajectories. Across image, language, and protein structure generation, NPO consistently achieves a better reward-quality trade-off than direct fine-tuning, and matches test-time search methods with 16 to 549 times lower inference cost.

papers.title: Extracting the Central Sound Speed of Neutron Stars through Intrinsic Stellar Structure Scaling with Reduced Equation-of-State Model Dependence
papers.abstract: Inferring neutron star (NS) core properties remains sensitive to the assumed equation of state (EOS). Using a nonlinear Walecka model with generalized $ω$-meson self-interactions, we construct six EOS families, each containing $10^3$ samples subject to identical nuclear and astrophysical constraints. Despite satisfying these constraints, the families predict markedly different high-density behavior and core properties; higher-order $ω$ interactions can also generate interior sound-speed peaks within purely nucleonic matter. To reduce this model dependence, we use the intrinsic and perturbative analysis of the dimensionless Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equations (IPAD-TOV) to derive an EOS-independent estimator $Θ(\rm{X},Ψ)$ of the central squared sound speed $s_{\rm c}^2$, where $\rm{X}=P_{\rm c}/\varepsilon_{\rm c}$ is the central EOS-parameter and $Ψ$ characterizes the stellar-mass response to central energy density. For canonical $1.4\,M_\odot$ NSs, $Θ$ correlates linearly with $s_{\rm c}^2$ across the families ($R^2\approx0.94$-$0.99$). The family-dependent relations converge toward a common optimum: minimizing their dispersion yields $s_{\rm c}^2\approx 0.523\pm0.044$ and $\rm{X}\approx 0.173^{+0.020}_{-0.018}$ for all six families, or $s_{\rm c}^2\approx 0.496\pm0.092$ and $\rm{X}\approx 0.167^{+0.030}_{-0.029}$ when the family without $ω$ self-interaction is excluded. The corresponding radii are $11.73^{+1.08}_{-0.92}$ and $11.92^{+1.76}_{-1.28}\,\rm km$, respectively, with $95\%$ confidence intervals. A unified scaling fitted to all EOS samples supports both extractions. These results show how common stellar-structure relations can constrain NS core properties with reduced EOS-model dependence, even when existing observations cannot distinguish among the underlying EOS descriptions.

papers.title: How Much Screening Buys a Second? Speed, Selection, and the Maker's Spread
papers.abstract: We study the spread a liquidity provider needs to break even against counterparties that can exploit a stale quote, and we place two defenses on a single scale: repricing sooner and screening informed flow. A break-even condition pins down the exact screening rate at which a slower maker matches a faster unscreened venue: the selection that buys back the extra staleness. The result requires only an integrable price innovation and therefore holds under jumps, atoms, and infinite variance. Predictable drift is a centering problem: it widens a spot-centered quote, but its cost vanishes once the quote is recentered on the expected reference. In four USDC-WETH pools benchmarked against Binance ETH-USDT from June to August 2026, the one-second benchmark innovation is sharply non-Gaussian: 73% of seconds show no price change. Cutting cadence from twelve seconds to one sheds 84.5% of the expected shock, so a twelve-second maker must screen at least 84.5% of informed flow to match a one-second venue, far above the 71.1% that a Gaussian model implies. In trending markets, the stale pool is picked off at execution: with-trend fills obtain an effective spread 11.1 bps lower than against-trend fills, with the same sign in all four pools.

papers.title: BiShield-TEE: On the (In-)Security of Unilateral Weight Obfuscation in On-Device TEE-Shielded LLM Partition
papers.abstract: On-device deployment of large language models (LLMs) is increasingly adopted due to latency and privacy requirements, but exposes proprietary models to reverse engineering and intellectual property theft. Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) provide hardware-enforced isolation for on-device inference, yet most TEE-based parameter obfuscation relies on unilateral matrix transformations that obfuscate only the output side. We identify a vulnerability in this design, termed the Solution Determinacy Property (SDP): the obfuscation secret is uniquely determined, exposing the structure of the true key and enabling attackers to break the protection. Under our attacks, representative methods GroupCover and ArrowCloak are reduced to negligible protection, with attack accuracy reaching over 2.4 times the full-shielding black-box baseline and recovering near-complete model functionality. To address this vulnerability, we propose BiShield-TEE, a bilateral framework that induces Ambiguous Solutions through joint obfuscation of input and output dimensions, hiding the true key among many equally valid candidates. Experiments across diverse models and datasets show that BiShield-TEE confines attack accuracy to the full-shielding black-box baseline, while achieving higher inference efficiency than prior methods on real hardware. Our code is available at https://github.com/laduiw/BiShield-TEE.

papers.title: Electrical Power Grid Reliability Assessment Exposed to Straight Line Winds
papers.abstract: Maintaining the resilience and reliability of electrical power grids under weather driven disturbances is a critical challenge for modern power system planning and operation. Among weather driven hazards, tornadoes and hurricanes are mostly considered for research purpose overlooking straight line winds despite its significant contribution to transmission line outages and cascading effects. Accurate modeling of these events is essential for operational decision making, and long term infrastructure planning and investment. This research explores the probabilistic risk assessment of transmission lines under straight line winds and their impacts on system level performance. The approach examines the probability of transmission towers failure, transmission lines outages, cascading effects, and identify critical transmission lines. The IEEE 118 bus system was utilized to validate the proposed approach and to demonstrate how wind induced component failures propagate throughout the network, affecting power grid reliability.

authors.institution: Shahjalal University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Mem4Act: Learning Effective Latent Memory for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Long-horizon robotic manipulation fundamentally requires memory: agents must retain task-relevant information from past observations and interactions and use it to guide future actions. Existing approaches typically preserve raw historical observations, compressed visual tokens, or language summaries, but these representations either expose the action policy to increasingly long histories or risk discarding task-relevant temporal, semantic, and perceptual information. We introduce Mem4Act, a framework for learning effective latent memory as a fixed-size representation explicitly optimized for long-horizon robotic control. Mem4Act addresses three coupled challenges: how to efficiently cover long histories, what information memory should retain, and how to ensure the policy actually relies on memory. To this end, it organizes history via multi-granularity temporal aggregation, preserves complementary semantic and perceptual information through question-answering supervision and key-frame DINO feature reconstruction, and employs memory-first two-stage training to encourage greater use of memory by the action policy. The resulting memory captures both high-level task state and fine-grained perceptual evidence while providing a bounded interface to the action policy. Across RoboMME, RMBench, and four real-world manipulation tasks, Mem4Act achieves state-of-the-art performance on memory-dependent control, with success rates of 49.88%, 61.0%, and 81.5%, respectively. Extensive ablations further demonstrate the importance of temporal aggregation, complementary memory supervision, and memory-first training.
