In particular, one bit is used for a two-level tolerance miscorrection check to validate the bounded distance decoding (BDD) result, while the other identifies bits to be randomly flipped upon BDD failure and miscorrection. List decoding is incorporated to further facilitate the error performance. Density evolution is performed for the design of the quantization thresholds. Compared to iterative BDD, the proposed scheme requires only moderate increases in memory and computational overhead. Simulation results verify that our scheme outperforms several unquantized soft-aided decoders, while maintaining small memory costs and low BDD attempts.

authors.name: Yueying Zhan
authors.institution: Technology and Engineering Center for Space Utilization

papers.title: A 2D Image Feedback-Based Autonomous Endovascular Navigation Method: A Perception and Control Framework
papers.abstract: In endovascular interventions, physicians rely on planar DSA and X-ray fluoroscopy to interpret vessel anatomy and device motion, yet converting these images into feedback for autonomous navigation remains difficult. A perception and control method is formulated for two-dimensional image feedback. Vessel masks are converted into a labeled centerline graph, and device-tip estimates are projected onto a planned path to obtain progress, deviation, and direction. A rule-based controller uses these quantities for delivery, branch selection, probing, rollback, and recovery. The method was evaluated on a physical dual-device robotic platform in 65 closed-loop runs using simulator-rendered planar images across three paths. All runs reached at least 0.95 maximum observed guidewire progress; two runs (3.1%) met the prespecified failure rule of three or more autonomous stop events. The results establish route-level performance on the tested platform; clinical image sequences and broader anatomy remain to be evaluated.

authors.name: Chunying Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: CausalEvo: Causal Skill Self-Evolution for Health LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents for health can accumulate reusable textual skills from task feedback, such as calculation criteria, measurement time points, and formula units. Deciding which skills to retain is consequential: useful rules improve later answers, while faulty generalizations propagate errors. We propose CausalEvo, a method for causal skill self-evolution that estimates the relative effects of deliberately changed skill sets while holding the model weights, feedback cases, and rule count fixed. At each evolution step, a frozen LLM proposes candidate rules, which are pooled with the incumbent skills so that the current skill set remains a feasible choice. Paired skill replacements against shared background rules are scored on the same feedback cases; least squares converts the score differences into relative skill values, and the top-ranked rules are retained, favoring incumbents on ties. A decision-loss bound separates candidate support, approximation, and estimation errors. On six MedCalc-Bench-Verified tasks with 120 held-out cases, CausalEvo achieves 60.00% accuracy, compared with 55.83% for SkillOpt and 51.67% without skills. Across the recorded training configurations, which use different optimization budgets, it consumes 55.6% fewer training tokens than SkillOpt. Gains concentrate in particular calculations alongside regressions on others, and paired accuracy intervals include zero. CausalEvo turns task feedback into controlled decisions about skill retention and replacement. Project repository: https://github.com/txbrook/CausalEvo

authors.name: Yuchen Zhang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology

papers.title: Sparse Attention for Video Generation Acceleration via Growing Sparsity and Reduced Search
papers.abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) dominate video generation but suffer from high inference cost due to the quadratic complexity of self-attention. Sparse attention mitigates this by skipping unnecessary computation in the attention matrix, but existing methods apply a fixed sparsity ratio throughout denoising and struggle to accurately determine which computations to skip. To address these limitations, we analyze attention dynamics through attention entropy and mean attention distance, and find that attention becomes increasingly concentrated across denoising steps. We further observe that blocks selected early continue to capture a large fraction of the total attention weight at later steps. These findings suggest two acceleration opportunities: the sparsity ratio should grow as denoising progresses, and earlier search results can be reused to reduce the search space. Based on these findings, we propose Growing Sparsity and Reduced Search (GSRS), a training-free framework that retains more computation early and progressively reduces it later, while restricting subsequent searches to an early candidate set to reduce search overhead. GSRS adopts Top-p selection for adaptive sparsity control, supported by a precise evaluation scheme that computes exact attention weights within the FlashAttention computation at negligible overhead. Experiments on HunyuanVideo and Wan 2.1 validate that GSRS achieves 1.55$\times$--2.21$\times$ speedup while maintaining generation quality comparable to full attention.

authors.name: Cen Chen
authors.institution: State Grid Henan Electric Power Company (China)

papers.title: VisualTrust: Video Reasoning under On-Screen Claim Framing
papers.abstract: On-screen text can describe what a video shows, or it can frame what the video is supposed to mean. Current benchmarks treat both alike, testing whether a model can read the text rather than whether it should trust it. We study claim deference, multimodal large language models' tendency to let an on-screen claim override conflicting visual evidence. We introduce VisualTrust, a counterfactual benchmark with 5,063 cases across 14 claim-fact classes. Each case pairs a question with three versions of the same video: one with no claim, one with an accurate claim, and one with a misleading claim that alters a single grounded fact. The option the misleading claim supports is the trap answer. Across seven open-weight and four proprietary models, mean accuracy falls from 90.1% without a claim to 51.9% with a misleading claim. Among initially correct responses, 42.8% flip to the trap answer and only 0.6% become other errors. Strong no-claim accuracy does not ensure resistance. We also introduce DEAR (Decoupled Evidence Arbitration and Reading), a training-free agent for video question answering that separates evidence arbitration from reading. An independent check reports conflicting evidence, a selector weighs it without a fixed modality priority and blinds what it withholds, and the reader answers from the resulting video in a fresh context. On 500 videos across three proprietary models, DEAR raises accuracy under misleading claims from 47.2--64.0% to 81.8--85.2% and reduces trap-answer selection from 34.4--50.8% to 11.6--15.0%, while preserving no-claim accuracy.

authors.name: Huachao Zhu
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University

authors.name: Junjielong Xu
authors.institution: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

authors.name: Pinjia He
authors.institution: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen

papers.title: DLOSAC: Joint Spatial-Geometric Image Estimation via Delaunay-Guided Local Optimization RANSAC
papers.abstract: Reliable image geometric estimation from noisy matching points is typically addressed using RANSAC, often combined with local optimization to refine inliers and model parameters. However, existing paradigms are predominantly residual-centric; even heuristic attempts to enforce spatial uniformity suffer from a sequential, two-stage nature that inherently decouples distribution optimization from geometric refinement, preventing an effective trade-off. In this paper, we propose DLOSAC, a local optimization framework that jointly incorporates both geometric consistency and spatial distribution information. We begin by constructing a Delaunay triangulation over candidate inliers to explicitly encode neighborhood topology. The geometric module introduces an edge-based consistency metric to evaluate geometric errors, while the spatial module derives distribution descriptors from triangle areas and edge attributes to quantify the clustering of inliers. Finally, we combine edge-based geometric constraints, spatial distribution regularization, and traditional point-level geometric constraints to improve the quality of geometric parameters. Extensive experiments on six publicly available real-world datasets, covering three types of geometric estimation tasks, achieve state-of-the-art performance.

authors.name: Guanyuan Feng
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: RecSoup: Efficient Model Merging Approach for Controllable Multi-Objective Recommendation
papers.abstract: Recommender systems often need to balance multiple conflicting objectives. Controllable Multi-Objective Recommendation (CMOR) enables dynamic adjustment of objective trade-offs at inference time without retraining, adapting to shifting user or system requirements. Existing CMOR approaches typically rely on output-level reranking or parameter-generating modules, which either limit the scope of feasible trade-offs or incur substantial training and inference cost. Model merging provides a promising alternative by reusing multiple objective-specific models via parameter combination. However, its direct application to recommender systems is challenging due to the lack of a shared linear regime and cross-objective interference. To address these issues, we propose RecSoup, a lightweight two-stage approach for effective CMOR via specialized model merging. RecSoup first mitigates parameter interference across objectives through a pruning strategy that jointly considers objective-specific importance and cross-objective relevance. It then performs adaptive parameter merging via a learnable preference-to-coefficient mapping, allowing dynamic trade-off control at inference time without joint retraining or additional generative modules. Theoretically, we prove that RecSoup outperforms the parameter generation paradigm in effectiveness and efficiency, as it can fully navigate the Pareto front without smoothness constraints. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that RecSoup achieves improved Pareto front quality and effective controllability while delivers 165--228x faster inference-time latency than parameter generation approaches. Code is available at https://github.com/35798642/RECSOUP.git.

papers.title: Rethinking Learning from Label Proportions via Moment Matching
papers.abstract: Learning from label proportions (LLP) is a weakly supervised setting where training data are grouped into bags with only bag-level label proportions observed, and the goal is to learn a classifier that predicts labels for individual instances. Recently, a large body of methods has emerged; however, most of them rely on the assumption that instance-label pairs are sampled i.i.d. and randomly assembled into bags, an assumption often violated in real-world scenarios. Our experimental results indicate that these methods perform suboptimally under non-random settings. In this work, we adopt a more realistic assumption: bags are sampled i.i.d., and instance labels are conditionally independent given the instances. Under this setting, we show that the label counts follow a Poisson multinomial distribution. Motivated by this observation, we propose LLP via moment matching (LLP-MM), a simple yet effective approach which leverages multi-order factorial moments as training objectives, encouraging the classifier predictions to match these moments and thereby more fully exploit the underlying statistical structure of the data. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets under various bag construction strategies demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach while maintaining high computational efficiency. Our code is available at https://github.com/TianhaoMa5/LLP-MM.

authors.name: Dong-Dong Wu
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: DocPilot: Interactive Agent Orchestration and Training for Long Visual Document Understanding
papers.abstract: Multimodal long-document question answering requires models to seek sparse evidence across pages and modalities, understand heterogeneous document content, and reason over the collected evidence. Even advanced vision-language models (VLMs) can overlook sparse evidence and struggle with cross-modal reasoning in a single pass. Existing document agents further introduce multi-step interaction, but some still rely on predefined workflows or coarse-grained actions, limiting the flexibility and granularity of document reasoning. We introduce DocPilot, an agentic document framework that supports expressive orchestration and makes complex document solving learnable by small language models (SLMs). DocPilot orchestrates evidence seeking through page-level navigation and fine-grained evidence localization, and integrates local visual inspection, code-based numerical reasoning, and cross-modal reasoning for multimodal understanding. To transfer these capabilities to small models, we propose curriculum-based agentic training that progresses from single-ability learning to adaptive orchestration through supervision from data-grounded reasoning traces and executable interaction trajectories. Across MMLongBench-Doc, DocBench, FinRAGBench-V, and MADQA, DocPilot achieves strong gains with frontier VLM backbones, while DocPilot-4B delivers competitive performance against substantially larger models, demonstrating strong effectiveness and generalization across diverse long-document reasoning settings. The code is available at https://github.com/HKUSTDial/DocPilot.

authors.name: Yuyu Luo
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

authors.name: Nan Tang
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

papers.title: LTM: Latent Transition Based In-Context Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Robotic manipulation often requires remembering interactions that are no longer visible. We introduce Latent Transition Memory (LTM), which stores history as compact latent transitions between consecutive observations. Instantiated on $π_{0.5}$ as LTM-$π$, our method uses a frozen latent action encoder, a lightweight adapter, and causal KV caching for incremental inference without memory-specific semantic annotations or external reasoning-model calls. With DreamDojo transitions, LTM-$π$ achieves 58.54% success on RoboMME and 80.5% on LIBERO-Mem, performing best among baselines without external reasoning models or memory-specific annotations. Ablations support the contribution of transition content beyond temporal cues and the efficiency of delayed memory admission. Scaling RoboMME demonstrations tenfold improves success from 57.67% to 87.50%, while a Cup Swap diagnostic highlights the role of process supervision in temporal composition. Under a 200-token memory budget, success remains 84.00%, versus 87.50% without compression. Finally, real-robot counting success improves from 11.25% to 82.50%. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness, scalability, and efficiency of latent transition memory, highlighting its capacity for complex temporal information, bounded-context operation, and real-world robotic control.

authors.name: Zhongyuan Wang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Ehrhart positivity for paving positroids
papers.abstract: A central conjecture of Ferroni, Jochemko, and Schröter posits that every positroid is Ehrhart positive. While Ehrhart positivity has recently been verified for notable classes such as lattice path matroids and series-parallel matroids, the general conjecture remains open. In this paper, we prove that the base polytope of any paving positroid has positive Ehrhart coefficients. This establishes a new class of Ehrhart positive positroids and provides substantial evidence supporting this conjecture.

papers.title: Task-Phase-Conditioned Expert Routing Is Not a Reliable Proxy for Quantization Sensitivity in MoE FFN Tensors
papers.abstract: We investigate whether per-layer, per-task-phase (prompt/reasoning/response) expert-routing statistics in a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model can guide layer-wise mixed-precision quantization of routed-expert FFN tensors (down/gate and up). To attain layerwise routing statistics, we build a routing-capture and profiling pipeline for Qwen-3.6-35B-A3B in ik_llama.cpp, derive a composite sensitivity score from routing entropy/decisiveness, coefficient of variation (CV), Jaccard/phase-fragility, and top-1 expert strength, and use coordinate descent to tune a layer allocation that respects a fixed average bits-per-weight budget. Notably, the profiling pipeline is applicable to standard top-k MoE architectures. Across independent experimental conditions (about 4.0 bpw flat, about 2.7 bpw steep, and about 2.7 bpw random allocation as a control), reallocation fails to outperform the uniform baseline within each quality tier. In the flat regime, reallocation is statistically neutral (z about 0.9). For the steep tier, the random reallocation performs within 1 SE of the routing-guided reallocation at the same tier, indicating a structural loss at this quality rung caused by mandatory downgrades and Kullback-Leibler Divergence (KLD) tail injection. This aggressive-budget condition shows a decisive loss (z greater than 4 SE) replicated across three independent weight vectors. We argue that the deeper issue is that routing-behavior statistics are an unvalidated proxy for true per-layer quantization cost.

papers.title: Beyond Match Results: Bayesian Mediation of Ability, Performance, and Winning in Professional Tennis
papers.abstract: Match results measure competitive ability, but they do not explain how ability is expressed during play. Match statistics offer a natural mediator, however performance is usually measured over the same match as the outcome: a full-match statistic uses events that help determine the winner, while a first-set statistic is earlier but rests on fewer service points and still contributes to the result. Comparing the two therefore mixes timing and precision. We develop a Bayesian mediation framework for this problem. Dynamic abilities on hard, clay, and grass courts are estimated from previous seasons only and are linked to both players' service performance, and a Bradley--Terry model relates ability and performance to the match result. A control mediator samples the first set's number of service points from the full match, separating the measurement window from the point count. In 3,820 men's matches, the hard-court mediated share rises from 0.52 with a first-set mediator to 0.95 with a full-match mediator; the point-count contrast accounts for 0.30 of this gap and the window contrast for 0.13. The pattern replicates on the women's tour. Simulations and sensitivity analyzes examine the decomposition and assumptions needed for a causal interpretation.

papers.title: Fourier decay and endpoint estimates for lacunary maximal operators
papers.abstract: We study endpoint estimates for lacunary maximal operators associated with compactly supported measures. For every $d\geq1$, we construct a compactly supported, absolutely continuous probability measure on $\mathbb R^d$ with polynomial Fourier decay whose associated lacunary maximal operator fails to map $H^1(\mathbb R^d)$ boundedly into $L^{1,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$. In particular, it fails to be of weak type $(1,1)$. This gives a negative answer to the weak type $(1,1)$ question posed by Seeger and Wright in 2011 and to Open Problems 14 and 15, contributed by Wright at the 2016 Conference in Harmonic Analysis, held at the University of Wisconsin--Madison in honor of Professor Michael Christ.

authors.name: Xiaojing Zhou
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering
papers.abstract: Agentic knowledge graph question answering(KGQA) relies on sequences of executable operations, but trajectory-level rewards obscure their individual contributions. Successful trajectories may contain ineffective operations, while failed trajectories may contain useful ones. To assess individual operations, we propose OpCredit, an operationaware policy-learning framework that combines downstream outcome credit with immediate transition credit: Branch Outcome Credit (BOC) reuses ordinary rollouts to compare terminal task rewards observed after different operations under matched navigation contexts; Frontier Transition Credit (FTC) measures operation-induced changes in answer-conditioned frontier potential. The two complementary signals jointly supervise the corresponding decision spans during training, while inference uses only the learned policy and standard KG interface. Experiments on ComplexWebQuestions, WebQSP, and GrailQA across three backbones demonstrate consistent improvements in KGQA performance.

authors.name: Yucheng Li
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Self-Guided LLM Reasoning for Error Diagnosis in Vehicle Routing Problems
papers.abstract: Vehicle Routing Problems (VRPs) are fundamental to many real-world applications. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have spurred progress in solving these NP-hard problems. However, most existing approaches assume that input instances are error-free, neglecting the presence of faults commonly encountered in real-world data. In this work, we systematically investigate the capability of LLMs to detect (and correct) errors in VRP instances, and identify key limitations, particularly in handling complex instances or errors that substantially increase the LLM's reasoning burden. To overcome these challenges, we propose a self-guided reasoning framework in which LLMs autonomously generate code that provides structured insights to aid in error diagnosis. Experiments across diverse problem settings and LLMs demonstrate that our framework significantly improves error detection performance, achieving near-perfect accuracy.

authors.name: Jianan Zhou
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Kernel-Based Heterogeneous Mean Field Games on a Continuum Type Space
papers.abstract: This paper studies a class of heterogeneous mean field games on a continuum type space, in which interactions are generated by a Hilbert-Schmidt kernel operator acting on the type-indexed mean state profile. The control set is allowed to be a general closed convex subset of a Euclidean space, and the optimal feedback is characterized through the unique maximizer of the Hamiltonian. For a prescribed mean-field path, the stochastic maximum principle leads to a family of fully coupled forward-backward stochastic differential equations (FBSDEs) indexed by the agent type. Under Lipschitz conditions and a monotonicity assumption on the reduced coefficients, the frozen FBSDE is globally well posed. We then formulate the consistency problem as a fixed-point problem for the kernel mean-field path. When the operator norm of the interaction kernel is sufficiently small, the resulting map has an invariant ball and is continuous and compact, so that Schauder's theorem yields existence of a mean field Nash equilibrium. Uniqueness follows under an aggregate monotonicity condition adapted to the kernel coupling. A linear-quadratic example illustrates how finite-rank interactions and heterogeneous risk preferences produce coupled collective modes, and yields a spectral smallness condition for existence and an explicit sufficient condition for uniqueness.

papers.title: From Interference to Diversity: Mode Coloring and Two-Dimensional Modal-Time Rake Combining for Multipath OAM Communications
papers.abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams provide a spatial-multiplexing dimension for wireless communications, but multipath scattering broadens their mode spectrum, so that energy leaks across modes as inter-mode interference (IMI), which conventional OAM demultiplexing discards. This paper treats the leaked modal energy not as interference but as a structured, harvestable resource: it attains up to $LK$-fold asymptotic diversity under independent-branch fading and yields harvested energy under the rank-limited per-tap fading of the operating channel. Each active OAM mode is colored with a distinct time-domain orthogonal spreading code, and a two-dimensional (2D) receiver grid spanning the OAM modes and the resolvable multipath delays jointly combines the despread outputs. The design builds on the Bessel order-difference coupling law of tilted OAM beams, summarized by a Gaussian mode-diffusion model with a mode-coherence metric that quantifies the surviving orthogonality, and on an effective diversity metric that separates the combining gain available at finite signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) from the asymptotic diversity order. At 28~GHz, with a four-mode eight-element uniform circular array (UCA) and four resolvable multipath taps, the proposed 2D modal-time Rake lowers the bit-error rate (BER) by one to three orders of magnitude and saves roughly 10--15~dB of required SNR over mode-wise detection and mode-domain zero-forcing (ZF) and minimum mean-square error (MMSE) detection, and it also outperforms an uncolored modal-time MMSE equalizer; the advantage survives the spectral-efficiency cost of spreading as well as channel-estimation and timing imperfections.

papers.title: To Think or Not to Think: Pre-Decisional Reasoning Budgets for Referring Audio-Visual Segmentation
papers.abstract: Multimodal reasoning systems increasingly assume that longer chain-of-thought (CoT) uniformly improves downstream grounding. We show that this assumption fails in referring audio-visual segmentation (Ref-AVS): simple queries can be harmed by excessive reasoning, creating an "overthinking trap" associated with phrase and localization drift, while genuinely ambiguous queries still benefit from multi-step reasoning. To systematically study this, we construct counterfactual reasoning-budget labels under a five-fold out-of-fold evaluation protocol. Our results recast adaptive Ref-AVS reasoning as a pre-decisional representation problem: before the first generated token, the generation-onset state contains linearly decodable information predictive of whether additional reasoning will improve segmentation. A linear probe predicts binary reasoning need with 70.1% accuracy, substantially outperforming text-only features and uncertainty-based proxy signals. As a router, the onset-state controller improves over downstream confidence routing and closely matches Short-then-Decide while using far fewer tokens. Proxy comparisons show that the onset representation contains predictive information not fully recovered by the evaluated hand-crafted features. Reusing this onset state for lightweight, single forward-pass routing reduces autoregressive token consumption by 60% while retaining about 96% of always-long performance. It further provides a cost-quality trade-off on $R^2$-AVSBench without target-label tuning, rather than an accuracy improvement over always-long. Error analysis links harmful long reasoning to phrase and localization drift, illustrating the benefit of bypassing unnecessary reasoning on simple queries. Ultimately, our results support efficient adaptive reasoning in Ref-AVS through pre-decisional internal representations.

authors.name: Haojie Hu
authors.institution: PLA Rocket Force University of Engineering

papers.title: Projection-Based Parareal for Nonlinear Initial-Value Problems
papers.abstract: Parareal is a parallel-in-time method for initial-value problems that has found extensive applications and given rise to many variants. Krylov-enhanced parareal is a variant of parareal that uses projection techniques to accelerate convergence substantially for linear problems. In this paper, we study a projection-based parareal algorithm for nonlinear initial-value problems with a modified iteration scheme and an arbitrary orthogonal projection. For a general nonlinear problem, we prove a convergence estimate for each iteration step on a fixed time grid. We analyze the errors of the modified scheme and the scheme of Krylov-enhanced parareal relative to the old error as the coarse grid is refined. For a coarse solver of order $p$ and step size $h$, we prove error bounds of $O(h^{p+1})$ for the modified scheme and $O(h)$ for that of Krylov-enhanced parareal at the first potentially inexact time point under mild assumptions. Numerical experiments on two nonlinear problems are consistent with the theoretical analysis.

authors.name: Yehao Zhang
authors.institution: China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences

papers.title: A proof of the interlacing conjecture for the singular values of Sylvester-Kac matrices
papers.abstract: Boros and Rózsa (Linear Algebra Appl. 421 (2007) 407--416) reduced the singular value problem for the odd-order Sylvester--Kac matrix $P\in\mathbb{R}^{(2m+1)\times(2m+1)}$ to those for $Q^{(m)}\in\mathbb{R}^{(m+1)\times m}$ and $S^{(m)}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times(m+1)}$ via a permutation similarity transformation. They noted that $(Q^{(m)})^{T}Q^{(m)}-S^{(m)}(S^{(m)})^{T}$ is positive definite, and also conjectured that $σ_i(S^{(m)})\geσ_{i+1}(Q^{(m)})$ for $1\le i\le m-1$ and $m\ge2$. In this paper, we prove that these inequalities are strict and establish the strict interlacing relation \begin{equation*} σ_1(Q^{(m)})>σ_1(S^{(m)})> \cdots>σ_m(Q^{(m)})> σ_m(S^{(m)})>0 \end{equation*} for all $m\ge1$. Here, $σ_i(\cdot)$ denotes the $i$-th largest singular value of a matrix.

papers.title: Optimizers for the finite-rank fractional Lieb--Thirring inequality
papers.abstract: The finite-rank fractional Lieb--Thirring inequality provides an estimate on the Riesz sum of the first $N$ negative eigenvalues of the fractional Schrödinger operator $(-Δ)^s-V$ in terms of the $L^{γ+\frac{d}{2s}}(\mathbb R^d)$ norm of the potential $V$, where the Riesz exponent $γ>\max\left\{0,1-d/(2s)\right\}$. We prove the existence of optimizers for every finite rank by establishing a result on the spectrum in the case of dichotomy. We further characterize the spectral gap and qualitative properties of optimizers, including the Euler--Lagrange equation, regularity, and asymptotic behavior at infinity. In particular, under the condition $γ+{d}/{(2s)}\geq 3+{4s}/{d}$, we show that all normalized maximizing sequences are precompact modulo translations. Moreover, we derive a strict binding inequality for the optimal constants in the finite-rank setting, which implies that the optimal fractional Lieb--Thirring constant, if it exists, cannot be attained by a potential with finitely many negative eigenvalues.

papers.title: Resolutions of compact balanced spaces
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a compact reduced balanced complex space of pure dimension $n\geq2$. We prove that every resolution of singularities of $X$ is a balanced manifold; in particular, $X$ belongs to the class $\mathscr{B}$. This removes the additional cohomological assumptions appearing in earlier results of Fu-Meng-Xia. The main new ingredient is the linear independence of the Aeppli classes of the exceptional prime divisors of a projective bimeromorphic morphism onto a normal complex space. This follows from the vanishing of curve degrees for Aeppli-trivial divisors and the relative negativity lemma. For non-normal spaces, strict positivity is used to eliminate divisors mapping onto codimension-one subsets before passing to the normalization. We also recall a classical surface example of Grauert showing that the inclusion of compact balanced spaces in $\mathscr{B}$ is strict.

papers.title: Moment Propagation for the Vlasov--Poisson System with Gyroscopic Forces, Velocity Diffusion, and Specular Reflection
papers.abstract: This paper studies the three-dimensional Vlasov--Poisson system with gyroscopic forces and velocity diffusion. For the Cauchy problem in $\mathbb R^3$ and the specular--Dirichlet problem in bounded domains, we prove the propagation of velocity moments of order $k>2$ for weak solutions with bounded $L^1\cap L^{\infty}$ norms and kinetic energy. The proof applies Serre's compensated integrability to weighted mass--momentum tensors to derive density estimates. A finite iteration alternating moment propagation with improved density integrability then closes the estimates. These estimates provide a simplified approach to moment propagation and yield global continuation of classical solutions.

authors.name: Jingpeng Wu
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Electrical Insulation and Power Equipment

papers.title: DeciCAD: Harness-Grounded Learning of Action Policies for CAD Agents
papers.abstract: Large Language Model agents operate through closed-loop action policies whose decision space is defined by an agent harness. We investigate how this operating space shapes agent behavior and policy learning in computer-aided design (CAD), a professional domain characterized by persistent state, geometric constraints, and long-horizon procedures. We instantiate this perspective in DeciCAD, a domain-native harness that exposes semantic CAD actions, decision-oriented observations, environment feedback, and persistent state transitions. Building on this harness, we develop a learning pipeline that extracts causal decision supervision from interaction trajectories and improves the policy through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and geometry-grounded online reinforcement learning (RL). Across four CAD benchmarks, DeciCAD achieves the best F1 and intersection over union (IoU) while reducing model-output tokens by 45--88% relative to a general-purpose coding harness. Under matched supervision, its SFT policy improves F1 from 0.6883 to 0.7437 and outperforms the coding policy; subsequent online RL further raises geometry availability from 66.5% to 73.5% and F1 to 0.7880. These results demonstrate that the decision space induced by a harness materially affects both agent execution and policy learning in CAD.

papers.title: A family of algebras that connects positroids, the Theta conjecture, the Delta conjecture, and Eulerian quasisymmetric functions
papers.abstract: We define a family of algebras $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,a,b}$ whose Hilbert series, when $n\le a+b\le n+2$, $a>0$, and $0<b<n$, enumerate certain positroid cells by codimension. Equivalently, these series enumerate certain affine permutations by length. We determine the graded $\mathfrak{S}_n$-module structure of these algebras by using exact sequences to derive an invertible recursion for their graded Frobenius characteristics when $a+b\ge n$ and then passing to the limit $a\rightarrow\infty$. In particular, the graded Frobenius characteristic $\mathrm{grFrob}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_{a+b-1}]/I_{a+b-1,a,b};q)=\operatorname{rev}_q(ω((Θ_{e_{a-1}}Θ_{e_{b-1}}\nabla e_1)\mid_{t=0}))$, where $\operatorname{rev}_q$ reverses the $q$-coefficients and the specialization $(Θ_{e_{a-1}}Θ_{e_{b-1}}\nabla e_1)\mid_{t=0}$ appears in the Theta conjecture. For $a,b\ge1$, we also show that $e_a^\perp\mathrm{grFrob}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_{a+b}]/I_{a+b,a,b};q)=q^{\binom{a}{2}}\operatorname{rev}_q(ω((Δ_{e_{a-1}}^\prime e_b)\mid_{t=0}))$, where $Δ_{e_{k-1}}^\prime e_n$ occurs in the Delta conjecture. In the three cases $a+b-n=0,1,2$, the ungraded Frobenius characteristics agree with three families of Eulerian quasisymmetric functions, respectively. We also construct an open subvariety of $(\mathbb{P}^{k-1})^n$ whose rational Chow ring is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,k,n-k}$. This variety admits a stratification induced by certain positroids. Its strata need not be affine, and their codimension generating function equals $\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,k,n-k};q)$.

authors.name: Hai Zhu
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Mod 3 Congruence Families for twisted signatures of string manifolds in dimensions up to twenty-eight
papers.abstract: In the paper, we establish congruences for twisted Dirac indices and signatures on closed string manifolds by specializing the two-parameter modular forms of Liu and Wang to the tangent bundle. Fourier coefficient comparisons yield uniform congruences modulo $3$ in dimensions $4k$, $1\leq k\leq7$. Suitable parameter choices give explicit formulas involving only genuine twisting bundles in dimensions $8,12,16,20,24,$ and $28$, and recover the comparisons of Chen and Han in dimension $24$. The level-one Witten genus further strengthens selected Dirac congruences to moduli $729,27,27,$ and $9$ in dimensions $16,20,24,$ and $28$, respectively. The proofs use Fourier expansions in reduced $K$-theory and integer identities obtained by clearing powers of two from the denominators before reduction modulo $3$. We also construct non-string spin counterexamples in each of the six listed dimensions and identify the additional coefficient that obstructs extending the uniform argument to dimension $32$ without further information.

papers.title: P2TPO: Structure-Aligned Page-to-Token Credit Assignment for Full-Page Document Parsing
papers.abstract: End-to-end full-page document parsing must preserve the content and structure of heterogeneous elements, yet otherwise accurate outputs can contain local errors and omissions. A single page-level advantage does not explicitly identify which elements differ in quality across sampled outputs or where their errors occur. We introduce Page-to-Token Policy Optimization (P2TPO), a structure-aligned credit-assignment framework that operates on full-page policy trajectories. Reference-element alignment first associates block-level quality contrasts with generated spans. Unified Anchor Pricing (UAP) incorporates matched and missing element outcomes and provides feedback relative to a fixed quality ceiling when sampled outputs receive identical but imperfect scores for a reference element. Within matched blocks, Span Credit Redistribution (SCR) redistributes existing block credit according to aligned correct and erroneous spans, using boundary proxies for within-block omissions while preserving the total block-derived advantage across its tokens. Under a fixed-weight additive page utility, we show that element-indexed contrasts retain local quality differences that page-level aggregation can cancel out. In the main experimental comparison, P2TPO outperforms all evaluated policy optimization baselines in seed-averaged scores on each of the six document parsing benchmarks. Additional experiments demonstrate gains across model scales and initializations.

authors.name: Ziqiang Dong
authors.institution: Suzhou University of Science and Technology

papers.title: When Reasoning Is Not Enough: Proactive Inquiry for Cross-Modal Safety in Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can act unsafely when individually benign images and texts are interpreted jointly. Beyond implicit reasoning risk, where reasoning drifts toward harm, we identify intent-level risk, where cross-modal ambiguity silently commits the model to a hazardous premise that path-level optimization alone cannot correct. We propose SAFE-PRO, which uses a Risk-Conditioned Uncertainty (RCU) signal, combining predictive entropy with a learned cross-modal risk score, to decide when to ask safety-grounded clarifying questions and where to apply path optimization, under a reward that prioritizes safety and penalizes over-refusal. We also build SSUI-Dialog, a multimodal multi-turn dataset with dual-intent supervision, and theoretically analyze gradient variance and unsafe-completion risk under RCU. Across seven benchmarks and two base MLLMs, SAFE-PRO consistently improves safety over SRPO, roughly halves its over-refusal, and surpasses GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet in average single-turn safety.

authors.name: Wei Cai
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: EMO: A Closed-Loop Test-Time Computation Framework via Alternating Context Optimization and Logits Steering
papers.abstract: Test-time context optimization adapts frozen language models through textual feedback, but ordinary conditional generation provides no separate control over how strongly to reinforce the distributional changes induced by a context update. We introduce EMO, a training-free framework inspired by expectation--maximization that alternates question-specific context estimation (E-step) and distribution refinement (M-step). The E-step revises a system context using textual gradients from an external judge without access to gold answers. The M-step contrasts next-token distributions under the revised and preceding contexts at a shared prefix to construct a confidence-constrained logit correction. Feedback on the steered response drives the next context update, coupling adaptation across rounds with intervention within each generation. Theoretically, we connect parameter and context optimization through a shared target-KL objective and additive logit representations, and derive the steering vector from context-induced logit displacements. Under context-improvement and faithful-steering assumptions, we prove a one-round decrease in target KL divergence for sufficiently small steering strength. Under greedy decoding across eight models and six benchmarks, EMO improves the zero-shot baseline in 39 of 40 aggregated settings, averaging $+9.10$ percentage points. With the same judge, it adds $+1.53$ points on average over context-only optimization (TextGrad), with consistent MMLU-Pro gains across models. At matched target-model generation budgets, accuracy advantages over best-of-$N$ are strongest on Llama, while oracle coverage is higher in most comparisons despite fewer candidates. The coverage--selection gap motivates allocating test-time computation jointly to candidate generation and verification.

papers.title: A quadratic ancestor inequality for spanning trees
papers.abstract: We introduce a quadratic ancestor inequality for weighted spanning trees on finite undirected graphs and give two applications. First, for every finite $n$-vertex transitive graph, the expected distance in its uniform spanning tree (UST) between two independent uniform vertices is at least $\sqrt{n}-1$, resolving a conjecture in [Benjamini--Kozma, Comm. Math. Phys. 259 (2005), 257--286]. Second, we prove that the growth exponent of three-dimensional loop-erased random walk (LERW) is at least 3/2.

papers.title: Generalization Guarantees of Randomized Block Coordinate Descent for Nonconvex Learning
papers.abstract: Randomized block coordinate descent (RBCD) is a popular optimization algorithm for many large-scale machine learning problems. The existing theoretical analysis of RBCD mainly focuses on its convergence behavior from an optimization perspective, while its generalization behavior remains less understood for nonconvex problems. In this paper, we establish high-probability generalization guarantees for RBCD with nonconvex objectives. In the general nonconvex setting, we derive bounds on the gradients of both empirical and population risks, requiring only standard smoothness assumptions. With polynomially decaying step sizes, we tune the iteration number to balance optimization and generalization, thereby quantifying how early stopping leads to the optimal convergence rate for the population gradients. In the gradient-dominated setting, we provide bounds in terms of functional suboptimality, which nearly match the optimistic rates in convex and low-noise settings. Finally, we develop dimension-independent bounds for loss functions of a specific structure, making the generalization guarantees applicable to high-dimensional problems.

papers.title: From Observation to Intervention: Distilling Self-Generated In-Context Demonstrations via Executable Causal Intervention
papers.abstract: Self-generated In-Context Learning (ICL) enables LLMs to synthesize their own few-shot demonstrations, often outperforming manual prompts. However, existing methods filter demonstrations by observation, assuming a rationale is high-quality if it leads to the correct output. We show such filtering suffers from \textit{observational equivalence}, whereby both faithful causal rationales and spurious post-hoc rationales can yield same outputs and are statistically indistinguishable from observation alone. Inspired by independent causal mechanisms, we argue that faithful rationales imply \textit{transfer invariance}, in which causal rationales should remain effective across logically similar samples. We instantiate this criterion as \textbf{E}xecutable \textbf{C}ausal \textbf{I}ntervention for \textbf{D}emonstrations \textbf{D}istillation (ECI2D), which abstracts language rationales into executable programs and applies the causal interventions ($do$-operator) on logically similar samples, retaining only those demonstrations that imply transfer invariance. Experiments on math, logical and commonsense reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that ECI2D consistently outperforms observation-based ICL while retaining far fewer demonstrations, with gains exceeding 7 points as the test distribution shifts.

papers.title: How Little Red Dots Turn Blue: Evolution of Kelvin-Helmholtz Contracting Black Hole Envelopes and Observational Diagnostics
papers.abstract: James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations have revealed compact, red-colored, broad-line emitters known as little red dots (LRDs), while a bluer counterpart population has been referred to as little blue dots (LBDs). Their physical connection remains unclear: they may represent different evolutionary stages of the same phenomenon, distinct populations, or different phases of the broader evolution of early galaxies and their black holes (BHs). We propose a model in which a rapidly growing BH is embedded in a geometrically thick gaseous envelope accompanied by concurrent nuclear star formation. The model reproduces the observed spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of LRDs and LBDs, and naturally connects the two phases through Kelvin-Helmholtz contraction of the envelope and exposure of the nuclear accretion disk, as the gas supply declines due to external stellar activity or feedback. We predict the corresponding evolutionary tracks in the UV-optical slope ($β_{\rm UV}$-$β_{\rm opt}$) plane which bridge the apparent gap between LRDs and LBDs. These evolutionary tracks start from the LRD regime and consistently exhibit a red excursion that extends toward $(β_{\rm UV},β_{\rm opt})\sim(2,-1)$ before turning toward the LBD regime. This feature is largely insensitive to variations in the model parameters that govern the envelope structure, providing a robust signature of the transitional population. The transition lasts $\sim5$-$50\,\mathrm{Myr}$, depending primarily on the BH feedback efficiency and the gas-retention efficiency of the envelope. The abundance ratio of transitional systems to LRDs therefore provides a constraint on BH feedback and gas retention during the rapid growth of early supermassive BHs.

authors.name: Zihao Wang
authors.institution: Key Laboratory of Symbolic Computation and Knowledge Engineering of Ministry of Education, Jilin University

papers.title: The Blume-Capel Model as a $φ^6$ Field Theory: A Monte Carlo and Flow Model Study
papers.abstract: We report Monte Carlo simulations of a continuous spin variant of the Blume-Capel model. We compute the phase diagrams in the crystal-field-temperature plane, as a function of the softness of the spins. We show that normalizing flows, a class of generative models capable of direct sampling without autocorrelation, are effective samplers across the phase diagram, including in the first-order transition region and in the vicinity of the tricritical point. Finite-size scaling analyses of flow samples locate the first- and second-order transitions as well as the tricritical point with accuracy comparable to canonical and extended-ensemble Monte Carlo.

authors.name: Ryan Larson
authors.institution: United States Naval Medical Research Unit SOUTH

papers.title: On the Last-Iterate Convergence of Clipped Gradient Methods
papers.abstract: In stochastic (strongly) convex optimization, establishing last-iterate convergence guarantees for first-order methods has recently garnered increasing attention, as this not only deepens the theoretical understanding of these algorithms but also aligns more closely with practice. Notably, people have demonstrated that one of the most famous, simple, and popular methods, Stochastic Gradient Descent ($\mathtt{SGD}$), provably achieves last-iterate convergence. However, the existing results may have limited applicability, since they typically rely on strong conditions on the gradient noise (e.g., an exponentially decaying tail) rather than the more realistic heavy-tailed noise. Unfortunately, when faced with heavy-tailed noise, $\mathtt{SGD}$ is known to exhibit undesirable behavior or even fail to converge. To address the challenge of heavy-tailed noise, people have proposed $\mathtt{Clipped}\text{-}\mathtt{SGD}$, an algorithm that combines $\mathtt{SGD}$ with a simple mechanism, gradient clipping. Although $\mathtt{Clipped}\text{-}\mathtt{SGD}$ performs well in practice, its last-iterate convergence property remains highly underexplored. In this work, we prove the first optimal last-iterate rates in high probability for $\mathtt{Clipped}\text{-}\mathtt{SGD}$ under heavy-tailed noise, thereby closing a gap in the literature.

papers.title: Bellman-Consistent Trajectory RL for LLM Arithmetic Reasoning
papers.abstract: To address sparse terminal rewards in LLM arithmetic reasoning, we propose a Bellman-consistent trajectory RL method. Our framework introduces Trajectory Bellman Residual Minimization (TBRM) to transform sparse rewards into dense token-level signals. We integrate a Reinforce Leave-One-Out (RLOO) group strategy to reduce gradient variance of Bellman residuals and use hindsight goal relabeling to accelerate intermediate learning. Evaluated on the Countdown task, our method alleviates optimization bottlenecks and stabilizes gradient variance significantly better than GRPO. The TBRM-RLOO framework boosts Pass@1 to 0.55--0.64 and achieves a state-of-the-art Pass@16 accuracy of 76.0--84.0\%, outperforming the SFT, IPO/DPO, and RLOO baselines. Our approach demonstrates exceptional single-sample efficiency and successfully circumvents standard performance plateaus via test-time scaling.

papers.title: RoPE-Flow: Monocular Vision-based Robot Pose Estimation via 2D Graph-Conditioned 3D Flow Matching
papers.abstract: Camera-to-robot pose estimation from a monocular image is significant for vision-based robot navigation and control. However, recovering 3D structural features from 2D observations remains a challenging task. Existing camera-to-robot pose estimation methods either rely on time-consuming iterative rendering or involve sophisticated 2D-3D registration which suffers from projection ambiguity, accumulated errors for distal joints and imbalanced learning for different joints. In this work, we propose RoPE-Flow, an end-to-end flow matching-based framework for camera-to-robot pose estimation. From the predicted 2D heatmaps, we propose a Keypoint-centered Feature Extractor to obtain positional features along with contextual representations from keypoints-centered multi-scale patches. Moreover, we introduce Graph-guided Condition Generator, which embeds a learnable adjacency map to generate condition for flow matching based on correlation among keypoints. Besides, we introduce Bone Length Loss and Ray-Depth Loss for topological consistency and scale stability, with joint-wise weighting to mitigate varied prediction difficulty across joints. The proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods for pose estimation across different types of robots with mutiple cameras. Besides, we establish a novel cross-scene benchmark to demonstrate the outstanding performance of RoPE-Flow on zero-shot cross-scene robot pose estimation. Meanwhile, animated visualizations are shown on the website: ropeflow.netlify.app

authors.name: Wanhao Liu
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Rulin Zhou
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Quantum Color Newton Rings
papers.abstract: We study integral Newton rings attached to symmetric quantum colors. We show that their boundary values at a deleted node are exactly the elements of Habiro's cyclotomic completion, and we describe their quantum neighborhoods at $q=1$ uniformly in the rank. The symmetric-color $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ invariants of a knot are the values of an element of such a ring. In its expansion at $q=1$, the coefficient of $(q-1)^m$ has denominator dividing the $(n-1+2m)$th power of the Alexander polynomial, with integral numerator, and this exponent is sharp. For $5_2$ and $6_1$ at $q=i$, the period matrices of the rank-two coefficient recurrences have spectral modules of exact order three in the Picard group of an affine elliptic curve.

papers.title: A Quantitative Hydrodynamic Limit for the Vlasov-Fokker-Planck/Navier-Stokes System in the Fine Particle Regime
papers.abstract: We justify the hydrodynamic limit of the Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equation coupled with the incompressible Navier--Stokes equation in the fine regime with a quantitative convergence rate. In this regime, the limiting dynamics is described by the inhomogeneous incompressible Navier-Stokes system for the fluid-particle mixture. In contrast with the existing relative entropy approaches, the present work extends to a pointwise convergence of the hydrodynamic limits with an explicit rate on any given time interval [0,T]. The proof is based on a Macro-Micro decomposition around the moving local Maxwellian, together with an $\varepsilon$-weighted energy-dissipation structure adapted to the fine particle relaxation scales. Furthermore, we remove the classical small background restriction inherent in high-order energy methods, allowing the limiting profile to be possibly large. This is accomplished by exploiting a hidden Kelvin-Voigt type damped wave equation structure within the macroscopic velocity error system, yielding the critical extra dissipation required to close the uniform estimates.

authors.name: Zhendong Fang
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University

authors.name: Jian Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Formation of Trapped Surfaces for the Einstein-Euler System
papers.abstract: We prove the formation of trapped surfaces for the Einstein--Euler system in 3+1 dimensions beyond spherical symmetry. We consider smooth characteristic initial data in a short-pulse regime with rapid fluid injection. Starting from initial data containing no trapped surfaces, we obtain two sufficient criteria for trapped surface formation, corresponding to the shear and fluid contributions, respectively. In particular, for the fluid-driven criterion, we impose no positive lower bound on the shear flux. To handle the multiple propagation speeds associated with gravitational waves, sound waves, and fluid transport, our analysis combines three ingredients: a coercive fluid energy current whose null fluxes reflect the unequal velocity components, curvature renormalizations adapted to the matter terms, and weighted geometric estimates controlling derivatives in all spacetime directions. To ensure that fluid injection alone can lead to trapped surface formation, we use particle-number conservation in a designed spacetime region to control the focusing process and obtain the desired sphere-integrated fluxes.

authors.name: Xinliang An
authors.institution: Chinese Research Academy of Environmental Sciences

papers.title: From Long Context to Selective Memory:A Survey of Memory-Centric Compression for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Long-context capability has become essential for large language models (LLMs) to handle complex tasks, yet continuously expanding the context window does not remove the computational, storage, and information-selection pressures incurred at inference time. Existing work on prompt compression, KV-cache management, efficient serving, retrieval augmentation, and agent memory is usually discussed in isolation, leaving the flow of information between storage and computation insufficiently understood. This survey reframes long-context compression as a memory-management problem for allocating inference-time resources. We distinguish compute-active memory, which directly participates in model computation, from compute-inactive memory, which lies outside the computation path but can be stored, retrieved, updated, or forgotten, and we characterize offloaded KV caches, persistent prefix caches, and precomputed KV states as intermediate states on the activation path. On this basis, we formulate writing, offloading, recall, retrieval-and-injection, materialization, eviction, consolidation, and forgetting as state transitions within an information lifecycle, and introduce a budgeted cost model that places these operations in a single cost account. The resulting framework unifies short-term context compression, long-term memory management, and the transitions between them, and shows that the central challenge is not merely reducing information volume but deciding which information should participate in costly inference, when, and in what form. We further summarize evaluation dimensions, benchmark gaps, and open challenges, and argue that future research should move from static, pointwise compression toward dynamic, governable, lifecycle-aware memory management.

authors.name: Chaogui Gou
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

papers.title: Dark Matter Particle Explorer: Ten-Year On-Orbit Performance and Scientific Outcomes
papers.abstract: The Dark Matter Particle Explorer (DAMPE, also known as ``Wukong'') is the first scientific space mission within the framework of the Strategic Pioneer Program on Space Science of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. The main scientific objectives of DAMPE include indirect detection of dark matter, cosmic-ray physics, and high energy gamma-ray astronomy. Thanks to its large geometrical factor and thick imaging calorimeter, DAMPE could effectively detect cosmic-ray electrons (including positrons) and gamma-rays up to 10~TeV, and nuclei up to PeV. Since launched on 17 December 2015 into a Sun-synchronous orbit, DAMPE has been smoothly operating on orbit for more than ten years. Here we present an overview of instrument, on-orbit status, and highlight scientific results of DAMPE, including the measurements of the all-electron energy spectrum and the spectra of protons and other nuclei, and high energy gamma-ray line search.

papers.title: Conditional limit laws for open intermittent dynamics
papers.abstract: We obtain conditional limit theorems for open intermittent Liverani-Saussol-Vaienti (LSV) maps. Unlike the results of closed systems (e.g. some uniformly expanding maps), we obtain a new limit distribution, which is different from the Gaussian law or the stable law, for both "regular" and singular observables.

authors.name: Can Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Beyond Retrieval Failure: Understanding Why LLMs Miss Evidence in Multi-Hop RAG
papers.abstract: Multi-hop retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) requires an agent to retrieve evidence for a sequence of dependent sub-questions. When a wrong answer lacks a required passage, the passage may be inaccessible to the retriever, or the agent may have failed to issue a query that would retrieve it. Standard retrieval evaluations conflate these two causes. We study how much apparent retrieval failure is instead caused by search drift: the search no longer tracks an unanswered sub-question. Holding the retriever, corpus, and generation model fixed, we introduce ExecutionRAG, a training-free requirement register that records open sub-questions and their supporting evidence. The register changes search guidance but not evidence access, so each gold passage it recovers certifies that the passage was reachable by the original retriever. On 1,000 MuSiQue questions, the number of wrong answers with unretrieved required evidence falls from 382 to 234 with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and from 383 to 274 with Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B. These counts correspond to 69% to 44% and 66% to 48% of each system's wrong answers, respectively. Crucially, evidence recovery does not produce a proportional reduction in total error: premature resolutions and abstentions increase as missing-evidence failures decrease. The central finding is therefore a shift in the remaining bottleneck, from guiding search toward required evidence to verifying that the retrieved evidence is sufficient.

authors.name: Jiaqi Wei
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Learning and Forecasting Multiscale Spatiotemporal Epidemic Dynamics with Lagrangian-Eulerian Graph Neural ODEs
papers.abstract: Accurate medium- to long-range epidemic forecasting requires extrapolating high-dimensional, heterogeneous and nonstationary dynamics from partial observations. Yet hybrid models often leave implicit which observations inform which epidemic processes and how learned graph interactions modify system state. We introduce LE-EpiGNODE, which replaces generic message passing with process-specific, mechanism-guided neural operators: age-contact information drives Lagrangian infection generation, whereas mobility drives conservative Eulerian population transport within a structure-preserving universal differential equation. We evaluated LE-EpiGNODE across 14 controlled synthetic mechanisms spanning time-modulated, state-dependent, nonlinear and coupled dynamics, three complementary COVID-19 settings, 21 comparator models and five targeted ablations. Forecasting gains tended to become more pronounced at longer horizons; at the longest horizon, LE-EpiGNODE achieved the lowest WMAPE in all three real-world datasets, reducing error by 17.7-40.0% relative to the best baseline. Controlled ablations linked these gains to the Lagrangian-Eulerian decomposition and process-aligned priors, while synthetic ground truth showed that learned operators and induced state fluxes track known generating dynamics. These results support mechanism-organized graph neural dynamics as a route to reliable long-horizon extrapolation with directly testable, process-level mechanistic interpretation beyond trajectory accuracy.

papers.title: FGSS-BO: Feedback-Guided Hypothesis Management for LLM-Based Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-guided Bayesian optimization (BO) uses past observations to guide search, but proposed directions and their revision can remain implicit. We propose Feedback-Guided Search State (FGSS), a structured hypothesis-management interface connecting language-based guidance to observed evidence, executable parameter interventions, and comparative support updates. An LLM reflector proposes and revises hypotheses; a deterministic curator validates them and maintains identities and test records. The evolving state guides candidate construction and priorities. Instantiated on LLAMBO, FGSS-BO retains its surrogate and default expected improvement selection, with a bounded testing policy. On two retrospective protocol/media tasks with nearest-neighbor response oracles, it attains higher sample mean final best and search AUC than the matched LLAMBO baseline and evaluated non-LLM baselines. Prose-reflection and EI-only controls show mixed component effects. Six direct-training hyperparameter-optimization tasks show task-dependent transfer, strongest on diabetes SVM; exact-grid and reaction controls examine other settings. FGSS exposes hypotheses, their execution, and cross-round revisions for inspection while supporting search gains in selected settings.

authors.name: Ronald X. Xu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Mingzhai Sun
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: A refinement of the strange duality conjecture on K3 surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $v,w$ be primitive Mukai vectors of positive rank on a polarized K3 surface with $χ(v\otimes w)=0$. Marian and Oprea conjectured that the strange duality map $H^0(M(v),Θ_w)^\vee\to H^0(M(w),Θ_v)$ is either zero or an isomorphism. We give three families of counterexamples to this conjecture. In each of them the map is nonzero but fails to be an isomorphism: in the first (a quartic surface) it is not surjective; in the second (Picard rank one, including very general polarized K3 surfaces) the source has strictly larger dimension than the target; and in the third (an elliptic surface) source and target both have dimension six, yet the map has rank five. The three examples share a common mechanism: one of the moduli spaces carries an effective divisor of square $-2$ on which a theta line bundle has negative degree, so that this theta line bundle is not nef and has nonvanishing higher cohomology, and the theta sections produced by the strange duality map vanish to excess order along this divisor. We therefore propose a refined conjecture, in which both theta line bundles are assumed to be big and nef, for instance ample.

authors.name: Yu Zhao
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Unique Charge-density-wave Order and Fluctuation-induced Phonon Softening in the Optimally-doped Trilayer Cuprate Bi$_2$Sr$_2$Ca$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{10+δ}$
papers.abstract: Charge-density-wave (CDW) order is a ubiquitous feature of cuprate superconductors that competes with superconductivity. However, its behavior remains poorly understood in trilayer compounds, which contain the optimal number of CuO$_2$ layers for superconductivity. Here, we report Cu $L_3$- and O $K$-edge resonant inelastic x-ray scattering (RIXS) measurements of optimally-doped Bi$_{2}$Sr$_{2}$Ca$_{2}$Cu$_{3}$O$_{10+δ}$ (Bi2223), the trilayer cuprate with the highest superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$) among Bi-based cuprates. We observe CDW order with a single in-plane wavevector of ${\bm q}_{\text{CDW}} = (0.25, 0)$, demonstrating that a coherent CDW order is formed across the trilayers. We also resolve CDW fluctuations emanating from the static order, whose profiles differ between the Cu $L_3$ and O $K$ edges. The phonon softening occurs where these CDW fluctuations interact with the phonon branch, indicating that the RIXS phonon anomaly is driven by the coupling between CDW fluctuations and the phonon branch.

authors.name: K. Yamamoto
authors.institution: RIKEN Center for Integrative Medical Sciences

authors.name: H. Eisaki
authors.institution: National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology

authors.name: D. J. Huang
authors.institution: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University

papers.title: Causal Mediation Analysis for Panel Data with Double/Debiased Machine Learning
papers.abstract: We develop a double/debiased machine learning framework for causal mediation analysis in panel data with two-way fixed effects. Binary, multivalued, or continuous treatments and continuous mediators affect outcomes via histories. We formulate partially linear models for potential outcomes and mediators, define history-specific direct, indirect, and total effects, and identify them under a sequential conditional independence assumption given unit effects, allowing arbitrary time-invariant confounding. Estimation combines first-differencing, cross-fitting sample splitting that removes period effects, and machine-learned confounding functions within a GMM framework whose score is Neyman orthogonal in all nuisance components. We establish asymptotic normality of the estimators for the structural parameters and causal estimands and provide consistent variance estimators. Simulations show small bias and near-nominal coverage under nonlinear confounding, whereas a DML-free benchmark fails severely for indirect effects. An application to U.S. county data illustrates that a stable total effect can conceal substantial sensitivity in its direct-indirect decomposition.

papers.title: Functions of bounded variation are not dense in the Strong BD Norm
papers.abstract: We prove that functions of bounded variation are not dense in the space of functions of bounded deformation with respect to the strong BD norm. Using alternating Riesz products and directional slicing, we construct on every nonempty open subset of $\R^n$ ($n\ge2$) a continuous, compactly supported BD function that is at positive distance from BV.

papers.title: RDL-Bench: A Benchmark for Task-Aware Question Answering over Relational Databases
papers.abstract: Relational databases (RDBs) remain the primary infrastructure for storing and managing structured data across enterprise and scientific domains. Natural-language (NL) interfaces to RDBs aim to let users ask questions without writing SQL, but real user needs go beyond SQL-style lookup: some questions require reasoning over the observable database state, while others require predictive inference from historical relational records under temporal constraints. Existing benchmarks address these goals in isolation. To address this gap, we introduce RDL-Bench, a benchmark for task-aware question answering (QA) over real RDBs. RDL-Bench organizes diverse user questions into reasoning-oriented questions, whose answers are determined by the current database state, and prediction-oriented questions, whose answers depend on future outcomes under temporal constraints. Each instance contains an NL question, task metadata, schema information, temporal context, either executable evidence or target-construction logic, and denotation-level ground truth. RDL-Bench supports two evaluation settings: native solvers under their intended capabilities, and task-aware modular systems where a router dispatches each question to an appropriate execution module.

papers.title: Nonreciprocal Control of Spatiotemporal Floquet Dynamics in Levitated Optomechanical Arrays
papers.abstract: Periodically driven photonic and optomechanical systems provide a versatile setting for realizing collective Floquet dynamics, yet the relation between temporal locking and continuous rotation of the finite-$q$ pattern remains poorly understood. We show that a nonreciprocal ring of parametrically driven optically levitated particles allows the spatial phase to be controlled while collective temporal locking is preserved. Nonreciprocity polarizes the counterpropagating finite-wave-vector modes and drives a transition from the pinned state to persistent directional spatial-phase drift. The normalized spatial-phase drift velocity is independently encoded in the splitting of the two dominant spectral branches, and its direction reverses with the coupling asymmetry. The pinned regime exhibits a laboratory frame period-two time-crystalline response, whereas the rotating regime forms a distinct temporally locked spatiotemporally ordered state. The same correspondence between spatial-phase drift and spectral splitting persists down to few-particle rings, indicating that the effect does not require a large array. These results establish nonreciprocity as a route to independently control spatial-phase drift and temporal synchronization in driven levitated optomechanical systems.

papers.title: X-Fly: Learning to Reach and Stop in Full-Chunk Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
papers.abstract: Aerial vision-language navigation (VLN) agents built on large vision-language models are expensive to query. Executing a complete predicted action chunk before replanning amortizes this cost, reducing model inference from 195 to 42 ms per executed waypoint for our policy. It also moves the states at which the policy is queried away from expert demonstrations, which supervise neither recovery from these states nor termination at the learner's own arrival. On OpenFly test-seen, no-stop failures account for 47.78% of full-chunk behavior cloning (BC) outcomes. We present X-Fly, a staged training framework for full-chunk aerial VLN. Recovery DAgger labels learner-visited decision states with smooth chunks that reconnect to future expert segments and with STOP at the first in-region state. Flow-GRPO then jointly refines the chunked flow controller and a Bernoulli STOP policy from same-task closed-loop outcomes, supplemented by outcome-verified stopping supervision. With eight controls per decision, X-Fly reaches 74.18% SR on test-seen and 51.73% on test-unseen, compared with 16.45% and 18.43% for full-chunk BC and 32.04% and 29.46% for DreamFly.

papers.title: Curvature-Distortion Numbers of Graphs: Prescribed Lin--Lu--Yau Curvature Lower Bounds
papers.abstract: We study an optimization problem for weighted Lin--Lu--Yau curvature. Given a graph $G=(V,E)$ and a prescribed lower curvature bound $k\ge0$, we ask for the smallest multiplicative distortion \[ \Dist(w):=\frac{\sup_{e\in E}w_e}{\inf_{e\in E}w_e} \] of the edge weights needed to make every edge have curvature at least $k$. This leads to the family \[ \DN_{\LLY}^{k}(G) := \inf\bigl\{ \Dist(w): κ_{\LLY}^{w}(e)\ge k \text{ for every }e\in E(G) \bigr\}, \] which extends the nonnegative-curvature invariant introduced in our preceding paper \cite{Xia2026InvariantI}. The edge weights change the transition probabilities, while the combinatorial graph distance remains fixed. Positive prescribed curvature leads to a fundamental distinction from the case $k=0$. If $G$ is a connected locally finite infinite graph and $k>0$, then \[ \DN_{\LLY}^{k}(G)=\infty. \] Thus no finite multiplicative distortion of the edge weights can impose a uniform positive curvature lower bound on such a graph. For a finite tree $T$ with $m$ edges, such weights exist exactly when $k\le2/m$. We prove that the minimum distortion is attained by a weight unique up to scaling, and that the normalized minimizer and its distortion depend continuously and nondecreasingly on $k$. We then extend the finite-tree theory to general connected graphs. As an application, we characterize the graphs of girth at least six for which finite $k$-distortion is possible.

papers.title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks: Curse of Dimensionality and Structural Bias
papers.abstract: Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KANs) have a dimension-independent approximation exponent when the target admits a sufficiently smooth representation by univariate edge functions. We ask whether this favorable scaling belongs to the architecture or to the assumed target class. For arbitrary-depth standard spline-KANs, we prove a worst-case lower bound on isotropic Sobolev balls: below a dimension-independent accuracy threshold, the required number of spline coefficients grows at least exponentially with input dimension. Existing composition-matched MLP results, by contrast, show that favorable exponents on low-arity targets are not exclusive to KANs. We also revisit empirical comparisons. On four scaling-law targets, spline-KAN approximants constructed from known decompositions transfer exactly to MLPs with the cubic ReLU activation $σ(x)=(\max\{0,x\})^3$, although their full dense parameter counts are larger. In controlled ridge-profile scans, KANs have a strong advantage when each nonlinear component depends on one input coordinate. When a component couples multiple input coordinates, this advantage may narrow sharply. At tight budgets, interacting targets often favor MLPs. In the random-label test on MNIST, ReLU-MLPs fit the randomized training labels more efficiently than spline-only KANs. Together, these results locate favorable scaling in target structure and a compatible inductive bias, not a general KAN-specific escape from the curse of dimensionality.

papers.title: Smoothness of Shortest Isogenies to Frobenius Conjugates
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be chosen uniformly from the geometric isomorphism classes of supersingular elliptic curves over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ and $δ_E$ be the minimum degree of isogenies from $E$ to its Frobenius conjugate $E^{(p)}$. We establish bounds for the smoothness probability of $δ_E$ and hence affirm Wesolowski's $p^{1/3+o(1)}$ attack on the supersingular endomorphism ring problem is unconditional. We also establish a uniform asymptotic formula, with a main term expressed in terms of Dirichlet $L$ values, for the probability that a connection isogeny of degree $n$ exists between $E$ and $E^{(p)}$.

papers.title: Activation-Adjacent Layer Normalization: Effects on Approximation Power
papers.abstract: Layer normalization (LN) and root mean square normalization (RMSNorm) depend on their inputs and remain nonlinear at inference. Inserting either next to an activation may therefore change the function a network represents. We study when shallow activation-normalized (AN) and preactivation-normalized (PN) networks can approximate a prescribed width-$N$ one-hidden-layer MLP. Viewing RMSNorm as input-dependent scaling, we use width augmentation to locally linearize normalization on compact feature sets. For AN networks, an unbounded activation range allows width $N+1$, while every continuous nonconstant activation admits width $N+r$ with error $O_f(r^{-1})$. For PN networks, affine parameters or, without them, degree-one positive homogeneity recover width $N+1$; general continuous activations admit width $N+r$ with error tending to zero. The corresponding LN constructions use centered coordinate pairs, yielding widths $N+2$ and $N+2r$, respectively. We prove that $N+1$ for RMSNorm and $N+2$ for LN are also the worst-case bound for approximations, and show that applicable universal-approximation theorems for ordinary MLPs transfer to these normalized architectures. Numerical experiments recover the predicted approximation rates for both normalizations across all five settings and illustrate the shifted-ReLU finite-width obstruction.
