papers.title: Two-Stage Score Estimation for Group-Specific Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: Generative modeling across related distributions raises a question: how can shared structure support accurate generation for a target distribution with limited observations? We develop a statistical framework for diffusion transfer that analyzes a shared pooled score together with a target-specific offset. Under Besov regularity of the pooled density and a stable hierarchical composition model for the offset, we derive convergence rates that separate the costs of learning these components and identify when a simpler offset yields a faster risk-bound rate than separate fitting. Under suitable boundary and regularity assumptions, we prove that the offset remains bounded and jointly regular as diffusion time approaches zero. These results allow the lower time cutoff to vanish polynomially and provide total-variation guarantees for diffusion models as density estimators. Synthetic simulations and image benchmarks provide a proof of concept for the framework.

papers.title: On the dimension conjecture for global Galois deformation rings in characteristic two
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field, and let $S$ be a finite set of primes of $K$ containing all primes above $2$ and all archimedean primes. Let $G_{K,S}$ be the Galois group of the maximal algebraic extension of $K$ unramified outside $S$. We prove two refined lower bounds for the Krull dimension of unrestricted global Galois deformation rings of continuous absolutely irreducible representations of $G_{K,S}$ over finite fields of characteristic $2$. As applications, we construct the first counterexamples to the dimension conjecture in every dimension $n\geq 2$ over every number field with a real prime. Over every totally real number field, these constructions also yield the first examples of such universal deformation rings that fail to be complete intersections. Furthermore, we propose a modified dimension conjecture over arbitrary number fields and in every dimension.

papers.title: Non-simply connected Poincaré surgery
papers.abstract: We give homotopy-theoretic proofs of the principal results of non-simply connected Poincaré surgery. These include the Fundamental Theorem of Poincaré surgery, the Poincaré transversality exact sequence, and the construction of Poincaré handle structures. All results apply in dimensions~$\ge 8$.

authors.name: John R. Klein
authors.institution: The University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston

papers.title: Sharp and Stable Label-Free Calibration Certificates from Logical Coherence
papers.abstract: Query-conditioned probabilistic predictors answer logically related questions one at a time, and labels to check their calibration are often missing. For each restriction on what a bettor's stakes may use, a minimax theorem identifies, for finitely supported laws of the answers, the sharp label-free lower bound on the corresponding calibration residual. On bundles of different events its mean, marginal and joint stages can separate strictly, and a bundle's bound cannot be attributed to one question without assumptions on the others. The sharp marginal bound is discontinuous in the answers, and no label-free lower bound continuous in the Wasserstein distance stays within a constant factor of it. Lipschitz stakes give a stable bound, sharp for a smooth calibration residual and, for every positive Lipschitz constant, positive exactly when the sharp marginal bound is. On i.i.d. streams, projected online gradient ascent at fixed nodes gives fixed-horizon certificates whose shortfall is bounded by grid, learning and statistical terms, and predictable betting gives anytime-valid ones. In a preregistered study of four predictors on two data sets, all seven confirmatory certificates were positive (the eighth pair did not pass the pilot). A certificate shows only that calibration is at least this bad; zero means "not refuted".

papers.title: Linear bounds for rich-neighbor edge-colorings
papers.abstract: An edge in a proper edge-coloring is rich if all edges adjacent to it receive pairwise distinct colors. A rich-neighbor edge-coloring is a proper edge-coloring in which every non-isolated edge is adjacent to a rich edge. The rich-neighbor chromatic index $\rn(G)$ is the minimum number of colors in such a coloring. We prove that every loopless multigraph $G$ satisfies $\rn(G)\le3χ'(G)$, where $χ'(G)$ is the chromatic index. Exact values are also determined for complete bipartite graphs and complete graphs. For all positive integers $m,n$, $\rn(K_{m,n})=m+n-1$, except that $\rn(K_{2,2})=4$. For $n\ge3$, $\rn(K_n)=2n-3$, except that $\rn(K_4)=6$ and $\rn(K_6)=10$. Moreover, for $n\ge7$, the rich edges in every optimal rich-neighbor edge-coloring of $K_n$ form a star forest.

papers.title: An Alternating Minimization Algorithm for Federated Sparse Orthogonal Nonnegative Matrix Factorization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop an alternating minimization algorithm for federated sparse orthogonal nonnegative matrix factorization (ONMF) with emphases on controlling client drift. To reduce communication frequency, clients perform multiple local updates between communication rounds, biasing updates toward their respective local objectives and giving rise to client drift, particularly under data heterogeneity. In federated sparse ONMF, global nonsmooth regularization further complicates drift control, as proximal mappings generally do not commute with averaging. To address these challenges, we develop an effective optimization algorithm that introduces variable splitting to decouple proximal operator evaluation from communication, allowing clients to handle joint sparsity regularization locally. In addition, the algorithm incorporates a correction term into the local gradients to adjust the update directions and mitigate client drift. We theoretically establish that the proposed algorithm achieves sublinear convergence to a bounded residual error under some mild conditions. Numerical experiments demonstrate favorable convergence behavior on a synthetic dataset and competitive clustering performance on real-world multi-view datasets.

papers.title: Modularity criteria for multiple Eisenstein series
papers.abstract: We give two criteria for a linear combination of multiple Eisenstein series of fixed weight to be a modular form, one in terms of its Fourier coefficients and one in terms of its $L$-function. The first criterion follows from an exact transformation formula under $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$, which describes the modular defect of multiple Eisenstein series explicitly. The second criterion is a Hecke converse theorem for multiple Eisenstein series, which shows that the functional equation of the $L$-function alone already implies modularity.

papers.title: What Does History Add? Calendar Controls and Information-Timing Audits for University Trajectory Forecasting
papers.abstract: We audit the predictive value of historical summaries in a rule-based university trajectory simulator. Seventeen ridge specifications and persistence separate current plans, past-state and past-plan summaries, and calendar-only history-length indicators. Across training, validation and two family-held-out evaluations, we reconstruct 16,750 routes and 804,000 monthly records. On the original 40-family set, six-month history lowers six-step normalized RMSE from 0.159234 to 0.151522, but its difference from a length-only control is -0.000895 (descriptive paired 95% interval [-0.001957,0.000248]). Fixed weights on 30 families unused in identified prior tasks reproduce this pattern: 0.156480 to 0.150074 versus current-state prediction, but -0.000558 [-0.001783,0.000728] versus the length control. These uncertain comparisons do not generalize to all-history summaries, which improve on their own calendar control. Exploratory decomposition finds clearer preparation-index and funds benefits, whereas fatigue dominates the six-month model's loss and has an uncertain length-controlled benefit. Moreover, 28.20% of its six-step fatigue predictions violate the simulator's [5,90] support. We document family dependence, prior exposure, strict temporal indexing, matched recursive references and independent numerical replay. The task conditions on recorded future plans; it does not evaluate real-student forecasts, causal action effects, autonomous planning or language-model memory. This is an evaluation audit, not a new memory architecture.

papers.title: ConStore: Search-Overlapped Prefetch and Co-Retrieval-Aware Content Storage for Disk-Based ANNS
papers.abstract: Disk-based approximate nearest-neighbor search (ANNS) supports retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), search, recommendation, and advertising over corpora that exceed memory capacity. Existing ANNS research often focuses on vector search at small top-K, whereas industrial-scale applications require larger retrieval sets. Fetching the corresponding content from storage remains comparatively underexplored. Our profiling across million- to billion-vector corpora shows that, at large K, content fetch latency can match or exceed vector-search latency and cannot be ignored in end-to-end retrieval. We present ConStore, a content storage engine combining two complementary techniques to reduce end-to-end retrieval latency. Speculative Inline Content Prefetch (SICP) commonly abstracts graph-based and cluster-based ANNS as progressive SSD I/O that refines an in-flight candidate queue. It prefetches content for stable leading candidates under a bounded I/O budget, overlapping content reads with search without changing the final top-K results. Co-Retrieval-Pattern-Aware Grouping (RPAG) uses query logs to place frequently co-retrieved documents in contiguous segments. Workload-Adaptive Segment Reorganization (WASR) adapts this layout to workload shifts by selectively regrouping segments under a bounded rewrite budget. Group Content Fetch (GCF) exploits this layout to coalesce per-document random reads into batched, page-aware I/O requests. SICP works independently of the content layout, while RPAG and GCF reduce fetch cost even without prefetching. Across three multi-hop QA workloads with K from 10 to 1600, ConStore reduces end-to-end retrieval latency over the best per-document-read baseline by up to 48% on DiskANN and 25% on SPANN. Separate experiments on 100M- and billion-vector indexes demonstrate SICP's applicability at larger scales.

papers.title: Ranking and Unranking Permutations in Heap's Order
papers.abstract: Heap's algorithm is a permutation generation method with very low constant overhead. Its element-interchanging mechanism, however, prevents the standard factorial-base Lehmer code from being applied directly, and to our knowledge no explicit Rank/Unrank algorithm for the Heap order has been published. This paper describes the block structure of Heap's algorithm in terms of rearrangement operators: the net effect of a block-internal traversal is a tail-preserving operator and the block-boundary swap is a top-level swap operator, and together they yield a closed-form recurrence for the block transitions. On this basis a bottom-up Unrank algorithm and a top-down Rank algorithm are built from one and the same closed-form in-block mapping; both run in $O(n^2)$ time and $O(n)$ space and require no factorial-scale precomputed table. The supporting proofs use a synchronized strong induction on the dimension to establish the bijectivity of the trailing-element mapping, closed forms for the final arrangement and for the trailing sequence, the dichotomy of its cycle structure, and the reciprocity of Rank and Unrank. The Heap order is in fact the colex order of the mixed-radix code.

papers.title: Missing Light, Misleading Confidence: Optical-Module Readout Loss and Signal Reliability in Neutrino Telescopes
papers.abstract: Optical neutrino telescopes reduce the photomultiplier signals of an optical module or string segment to compact multichannel summaries, and readout loss can make these summaries unreliable. We asked whether availability-based quality gates, which accept a summary when enough of the readout was live, can certify a summary of inter-channel statistical consistency (called coherence here; not optical coherence) under readout loss, and where they fail. We used public IceCube pulses (9,484 string records) and the released hits of KM3NeT event KM3-230213A with controlled readout loss, together with a replay of real KM3NeT readout flags. In a two-by-two design we compared a published recursive support state with direct mask support, and calibrated every threshold on development records. The support state is a function of the mask and added no information. On IceCube the support-gated rule retained 0.16 percentage points more usable summaries, an effect of the window at which support was read that reversed sign at a looser tolerance; on KM3NeT it accepted nothing. The gates accepted only records with nearly intact masks, including records whose charge had been depleted by signal-dependent loss that the mask does not record. Pulse loss during live acquisition and timing jitter passed every availability gate, which then accepted summaries of which up to 66% were unreliable. Availability flags are therefore necessary but not sufficient, and signal-based checks are needed. This work uses public data and is not an IceCube or KM3NeT Collaboration result.

authors.name: Pittaya Pannil
authors.institution: King Mongkut's Institute of Technology Ladkrabang

papers.title: Single-stage joint diffusion of sky images and clear-sky index for ultra-short-term irradiance forecasting: what the frame-to-irradiance stage discards
papers.abstract: Sky-image irradiance forecasting is dominated by a two-stage design: a video-prediction model forecasts future sky frames, and a separately trained regressor maps those frames to irradiance. We propose a single-stage alternative that co-denoises the future sky-image and clear-sky-index sequences in one diffusion process, with an irradiance head that reads a denoised preview of the future sky rather than the noised diffusion state. The forecaster needs no regression stage and runs from sky images and deterministic covariates alone, with no measured irradiance at its input --- the situation at a site with a camera but no pyranometer. On 2023 SIRTA data the model reaches a pooled RMSE of $104.1$~W\,m$^{-2}$ and a skill score of $+0.34$ on the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) against smart persistence, higher than any of twelve baseline configurations, and retains that skill when retrained on 2021--2022. On the model's own generated frames, a separately trained regressor reaches $150.6$~W\,m$^{-2}$ against the joint head's $104.1$: roughly $46$~W\,m$^{-2}$ that joint training recovers and a cascade discards. Point accuracy is competitive but not best: a deterministic network that also reads measured irradiance attains $97.6$~W\,m$^{-2}$. The model's CRPS skill leads that network's in every sky-condition tertile, by $0.26$ to $0.30$.

papers.title: Confidence-Calibrated Inference Expansion for Evaluator-Guided Test-Time Reasoning
papers.abstract: Evaluator-guided reasoning presents a local control problem at every step: trust the current answer, return a fallback, or spend more inference. We formulate this choice as a compute-aware three-action controller, scoring terminal actions by predicted answer success and expansion by a rollout-based continuation-success surrogate, with compute cost priced explicitly. A local action-gap analysis characterizes when score errors can change a decision, while an expected regret bound accounts for errors along the realized expansion path. Guided by this analysis, we learn and calibrate action-specific confidence estimates, with local uncertainty penalties for ambiguous decisions. On held-out width expansion and revision tasks, the controller improves observed utility over calibration-selected fixed policies while reducing normalized online compute by about 30% and 16%, respectively. Across four Qwen3-8B seeds, compute is lower than fitted Q in both settings, while utility differences are small and mixed. The results frame evaluator-guided reasoning as resource allocation under uncertainty, rather than a uniformly stronger reasoner.

papers.title: Exact Makespan Bounds and the GPipe Homogeneity Bias for Heterogeneous LLM Inference Pipelines
papers.abstract: We give an exact critical-path characterization of the makespan of micro-batch pipelines serving LLMs on heterogeneous GPU clusters, quantifying how the classic homogeneous GPipe formula errs. In the pure-forward, communication-free, infinite-buffer setting, T(M) = (M-1)tau_max + Sum_j tau_j, where tau_j is stage j's per-micro-batch service time and M the micro-batch count (Theorem 1). Under asynchronous communication -- modern NCCL-based serving -- it extends to T(M) = Sum_j tau_j + Sum_j d_j + (M-1)tau_max, with Sum_j d_j a purely additive constant (Theorem 2); under blocking communication, T(M) = (M-1)sigma_max + Sum_s sigma_s with sigma_s = tau_s + d_s, so communication enters the steady-state slope iff some d_s > tau_max - tau_s (Theorem 3). These results quantify the GPipe overestimate, decompose the bias into a homogeneity term Sum_j (tau_max - tau_j) and a communication-ignoring term Sum_j d_j, and imply that balancing per-stage compute dominates communication reduction for steady-state throughput. A real system with partial overlap is sandwiched between Theorems 2 and 3, with a closed-form bound on the overlap throughput gain. All claims are validated pointwise (error < 10^-9) on eleven configurations and a 1.6x10^5-point fuzz, including a mixed RTX 5090/3090/GTX 1070 partition. We situate the results in flow-shop scheduling and list open extensions: bandwidth-limited communication, bounded buffers, prefill-decode interleaving.

papers.title: Discontinuous-Property Mechanical Metamaterials: A Framework for Discontinuous Lattice Dynamics
papers.abstract: Discontinuity, as the extreme limit of nonlinearity, is common in macroscopic continuum systems. This work introduces discontinuous-property mechanical metamaterials (DPMMs) as a prototype for establishing a geometric-mechanics framework for discontinuous lattice systems. We extend band theory to systems with complementary constraints through geometric regularization and analyze modal discontinuities. By analyzing its static, modal, and transient responses, we validated discontinuous stiffness and Poisson's ratio, alongside intense nonlinear wave mixing and mode conversion. A proof-of-concept experiment demonstrates the practical feasibility of implementing DPMMs. This work characterizes discontinuous lattice systems through the intuitive DPMM concept and provides a practical framework to harness sharp transitions in mechanical metamaterials for nonlinear wave manipulation.

papers.title: Classification of bipartite observables III: simplicity, mixtures and quantum error correction
papers.abstract: This is the third paper in a series that reads the dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory as properties of bipartite quantum observables. Here we study simplicity through two countable structures with simple unstable theories: the Rado graph, and the symplectic space of labels of Pauli strings of finite support, in which addition records the products of the strings and the symplectic form records their commutation. In the second structure, forking characterizes the logical errors of stabilizer codes: an error undetectable by the checks of a code is logical exactly when its type over the stabilizer labels and a complete set of logical-operator labels forks over the stabilizer labels, and the independence theorem becomes a rule for gluing syndromes. A two-valued relation between countable sets of labels defines a diagonal bipartite observable, whose real-valued theory describes Alice's probability mixtures of labels and their expected responses at Bob's probes. Mixing changes the classification: if the relation has the independence property, this theory has the tree property of the second kind. For the observable of the symplectic form, actual mixtures of checks witness this property for the response itself; for the observable of the Rado graph, every array that witnesses it for a quantifier-free formula in Bob's probe contains idealized preparations, which lie outside the original structure.

authors.name: Eduardo Dueñez
authors.institution: The University of Texas at San Antonio

authors.name: José Iovino
authors.institution: The University of Texas at San Antonio

papers.title: Smale's mean value constant and admissible univalent Blaschke pairs
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be the class of polynomials $P$ of degree at least $2$ with $P(0)=0$, $P'(0)=1$, let $S(P)=\min_{P'(c)=0}|P(c)/c|$ and let $\mathcal{M}=\sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}}S(P)$ be Smale's mean value constant. Smale proved that $\mathcal{M}\le4$, observed that $\mathbb{M}\ge 1$, and asked whether $\mathcal{M}=1$. We show that $\mathcal{M}$ coincides with $$ \mathcal{B}=\sup\frac1{B(0)}, $$ the supremum running over pairs $(W,B)$ in which $W$ is a normalised univalent map of the standard unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ and $B$ is a finite Blaschke product with $B(0)>0$ such that $WB$ is locally univalent in $\mathbb{D}$. Smale's question is therefore a problem in univalent function theory. We also introduce the degree-restricted constants $\mathcal{B}_d$ for $B$ with $\mathrm{deg} B \le d$ and show that $$1.1018586788\ldots=\sqrt{\frac{8081}{6656}} \le \mathcal{B}_1 < \sqrt{\frac{7}{5}}=1.1832159566\ldots$$ This implies that $\mathcal{M}>1.1018$ and we also show that there are polynomials of arbitrarily large degree with $S(P)>1.1018$. The polynomial construction behind these results also settles Problems 1A and 1B of Smale's 1981 paper. For $P\in\mathcal P$ and an integer $k\ge2$ let $S_k(P)=\min_{P'(c)=0}|P^{(k)}(0)/k!|^{1/(k-1)}|P(c)|$. Smale proved, by Löwner's coefficient estimate for inverses of univalent functions, that $\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}S_k(P)\le C_k^{1/(k-1)}<4$, where $C_k$ is the $k$-th Catalan number and he asked whether the constant $4$ (Problem 1A), or the constant $2=C_2$ for $k=2$ (Problem 1B), can be reduced. We prove that $\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}S_k(P)=C_k^{1/(k-1)}$ for every $k\ge2$. Hence the constants $4$ and $2$ cannot be reduced and the answers to both problems are negative.

papers.title: LLM-Based Weak Annotation for Cybersecurity Tweet Classification: A Teacher-Student Framework
papers.abstract: Cyber threat intelligence (CTI) relies on the timely identification of emerging threats, enabling organizations and security analysts to support situational awareness and decision-making. Social media platforms such as X (formerly Twitter) have become valuable CTI sources because vulnerabilities and attack activities are often discussed there before appearing in formal reports. However, the rapid growth of cybersecurity discussions on social media has created more content than domain experts can realistically review and annotate, making labeled data a major bottleneck for developing supervised learning approaches. While large language models (LLMs) have shown promise as weak annotators in other domains, their effectiveness for cybersecurity tweet classification and downstream training of domain-specific pre-trained language models (PLMs) remains underexplored. To address this challenge, we propose a Teacher-Student weak supervision framework in which a selected LLM serves as a Teacher to generate weak labels for unlabeled cybersecurity tweets, enabling the training of cybersecurity-specific PLMs without large-scale manual annotation. Experimental results show that PLMs trained solely on LLM-generated labels consistently achieve F1 scores above 0.92, remaining within 3 percentage points of fully human-supervised models across all evaluated architectures. These findings suggest that LLM-based weak annotation offers a practical alternative for constructing cybersecurity-specific training data when expert annotation resources are limited.

papers.title: Trigger Value Selection in Clean-Label Malware Backdoors: An Effectiveness-Detectability Analysis
papers.abstract: Clean-label backdoor poisoning is a threat to machine learning-based malware classifiers because poisoned samples can be inserted into training data without changing their labels. Previous explanation-guided attacks mainly focus on selecting important trigger features, but the values assigned to these features can also affect the attack behavior. In this paper, we study trigger value selection as an independent design factor in clean-label backdoor attacks against feature-based malware classifiers. We evaluate several value-selection strategies on EMBER 2018 and a Win64 PE subset of EMBER 2024 using LightGBM classifiers. We compare rare-value, SHAP-based, frequency-bounded, co-occurrence-aware, and quantile-based selectors under random and distribution-based malware-similar benign sampling. The results show that aggressive selectors such as MinPopulation and CountAbsSHAP can achieve high attack success rate, especially under distribution-based sampling, but they are also easier to detect by sanitization methods such as Isolation Forest. In contrast, selectors such as CorrCountAbsSHAP and Quantile95 can reduce poison recall while keeping useful attack effectiveness. These findings show that trigger value selection is not merely an implementation detail, but an important design choice that shapes the effectiveness and detectability profile of clean-label malware backdoor attacks.

papers.title: Multivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures of generalized Johnson association schemes
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak X$ be a commutative association scheme of class $d$ on $X$. We construct the generalized Johnson association scheme $\mathfrak J_{n,h}(\mathfrak X)$ on partial maps from $[n]$ to $X$ with domains of size $h$. For $1\le h\le n-1$, we prove that $\mathfrak J_{n,h}(\mathfrak X)$ has $(d+1)$-variate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures. In particular, its multivariate $Q$-polynomial property answers affirmatively a problem posed for generalized Johnson association schemes arising from finite Gelfand pairs. We also determine the primitive idempotents and the two eigenmatrices, expressing the first eigenmatrix as a product of an Eberlein polynomial and a multivariate Krawtchouk polynomial, and the second eigenmatrix as a product of a Hahn polynomial and a multivariate Krawtchouk polynomial. For the multivariate factors, we use Mizukawa--Tanaka $(d+1,2d+2)$-hypergeometric functions. In an appendix, we identify the normalized columns of the second eigenmatrix with the known spherical functions in the finite Gelfand pair case. We also discuss the orthogonality relations and the imprimitivity arising from partial maps with the same domain, and explicitly describe the multivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures inherited by the blocks and the quotient.

papers.title: A sharp criterion for well-posedness of semilinear Schrödinger equations on the real line
papers.abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for semilinear Schrödinger equations on the real line. We establish a sharp necessary and sufficient condition on the nonlinearity for local well-posedness in Sobolev spaces of regularity greater than five halves. This criterion is formulated in terms of the Mizohata condition and is equivalent to explicit algebraic conditions on the nonlinearity. To prove sufficiency, we combine energy estimates with a gauge transformation adapted to the bounded primitive arising from the Mizohata condition. To prove necessity, we show that the failure of the condition yields a dense set of initial data for which no solution exists on any positive time interval.

papers.title: Local wave-packet spectroscopy of the Drude weight in Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids
papers.abstract: We investigate wave packets generated by a local pulse electric field in a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) with a U(1) charge $q$. Bosonization shows that a local pulse field creates two counterpropagating packets with opposite accumulated charges $\pm qK$ and velocity $v$, where $K$ and $v$ are the TLL parameter and velocity. The packet motion produces a linearly growing charge polarization $P(t)=2 qDt$ in the conducting TLL at non-equilibrium, allowing the Drude weight $D=vK$ to be extracted from real-time local dynamics. We test this local-packet description by time-dependent variational principle simulations of the spin-1/2 XXZ chain. The simulations visualize the density, current, energy, and entanglement profiles in the space-time plane and confirm the predicted packet charge and propagation velocity. We also show that excess energy and entanglement remaining near the pulse region are suppressed in the weak-pulse limit. Finally, the Drude weight obtained from the packet-induced polarization agrees with the exact Bethe-ansatz result, demonstrating local-packet spectroscopy of intrinsic transport in a TLL.

papers.title: Imaginary quadratic fields of class number at most 2000
papers.abstract: We determine all imaginary quadratic fields with class number at most 2000, unconditionally: there are 16,453,493 of them, and the largest $|d_K|$ among them is 1,062,350,083. To our knowledge, such a list was previously known only for class number at most 100. We make explicit a recent argument, released by OpenAI and not refereed, that excludes Landau-Siegel zeros: every real zero $β$ of $L(s,χ)$, for a primitive real character $χ$ of conductor $q\ge3$, satisfies $(1-β)\log q\ge5.8\cdot10^{-4}$. An elementary lower bound for $L(1,χ)$ then shows that a field with class number at most 2000 has $|d_K|<1.61\cdot10^{15}$. The fields with $6\cdot2^{28}\le|d_K|\le1.65\cdot10^{15}$ are excluded by Watkins' sieve, and those below are read from the class group tables of Mosunov and Jacobson. As a consequence, the lists of Cremona and Sutherland of imaginary quadratic orders with class number at most 1000, and the counts of Holmin, Jones, Kurlberg, McLeman and Petersen for odd class numbers up to 1999, previously known under the generalized Riemann hypothesis, hold unconditionally. The two steps, the bound for $β$ and the bound for $|d_K|$, are proved in Lean, building on the existing formalization of that argument, and the proofs are checked by two independent kernels. The contributions of AI systems to this work are stated in the paper.

papers.title: Good stratifications of non-degenerate locally tame complete intersection varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that non-degenerate locally tame complete intersection varieties admit good stratifications. As an application, we study variation of the Milnor fibrations in pencils associated with non-degenerate hypersurface singularities.

papers.title: Wavelet covariances under fixed finite observations: dilation symmetry breaking and distinct endpoint limits
papers.abstract: For a centered homogeneous generalized Gaussian field with spectral weight $C|ω|^{-γ}$, we prove two-endpoint recovery of normalized posterior wavelet covariances under fixed finite admissible observations. Global dilation symmetry holds if and only if all observation functions vanish. The nonzero wavelet and the observation functions are real Schwartz functions with $M\geq1$ vanishing moments, with $C>0$ and $γ<2M+1$. Noise is Gaussian and field-independent, and total observation covariance is positive definite. Under simultaneous dilation of target scales and positions, multiplication by $λ^{-γ}$ recovers the prior covariance as $λ\downarrow0$ and $λ\uparrow\infty$, uniformly on every fixed compact target set. If a nonzero observation function exists, additional finite first nonzero Fourier orders $m_ψ,m_i$ at zero of the wavelet and nonzero observation functions yield compact-uniform recovery bounds $O(λ^{2m_ψ+1-γ})$ and $O(λ^{-(2\min_i m_i+1-γ)})$, with leading coefficients and cancellation-dependent improvements. The bounds are exact leading orders when their coefficients are nonzero. For the Matérn-type spectrum $S(ω)=C(κ^2+ω^2)^{-p}$, $κ>0$, $1/2<p<M+1/2$, fixed finite noisy point observations yield distinct compact-uniform limits: the homogeneous $C|ω|^{-2p}$ kernel after multiplication by $λ^{-2p}$ at small scales, and the constant-spectrum $S(0)$ kernel without normalization at large scales. A projection-norm criterion treats fixed closed observation subspaces; Mexican-hat formulas illustrate the finite-observation results.

papers.title: Development of a Long-Term Stable Three-Axis Single-Beam Vector Optically Pumped Magnetometer Using a Buffer-Gas-Free Rubidium Vapor Cell and Direct Absorption Frequency Locking for Unshielded Geomagnetic Monitoring
papers.abstract: Optically pumped magnetometers (OPMs) achieve ultra-high sensitivity, yet sustaining long-term stability in unshielded, dynamic geomagnetic environments remains challenging. Here, we present the design and unshielded validation of a three-axis vector OPM achieving sub-nanotesla accuracy using an off-the-shelf rubidium (Rb) ampoule and a vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL). Unlike conventional sensors, this system operates without high-pressure buffer gases, mitigating wall-collision relaxation via a single-beam geometry combined with active zero-field nulling and adiabatic 70 kHz AC heating. To suppress VCSEL thermal wavelength drift without sub-Doppler optics, active frequency stabilization based on direct absorption spectroscopy (DAS) was implemented across a wide capture range. Continuous evaluation in an unshielded laboratory in Okayama against synthetic geomagnetic records from the Kakioka and Kanoya observatories demonstrated exceptional horizontal tracking fidelity. Concurrently, the vertical transfer matrix resolved the regional geomagnetic coast effect, extracting Parkinson induction vectors reflecting regional conductivity contrast, with high robustness against DC electric railway interference. Spectral characterization showed an intrinsic white noise floor of 10-20 pT above 1 Hz, enhanced by digital oversampling beyond the 12-bit DAC quantization limit, while residual overlapped Allan deviation revealed a 0.1 nT bias instability at 100-200 s integration times. These results prove that a compact, low-cost OPM platform based on commercial components can suppress long-term drift and serve as a reliable instrument for geophysical surveys and unshielded magnetic sensing.

papers.title: Strong Lefschetz property of the Kirchhoff algebra of the complete tripartite graph $K_{1,1,n}$
papers.abstract: By Whitney's 2-isomorphism theorem, the cycle matroids of two graphs are isomorphic if and only if one graph can be transformed into the other by finitely many applications of two operations: separation or identification at a cut-vertex, and twisting. The complete tripartite graph whose vertex set is the disjoint union of two singletons and an $n$-element set is invariant, up to isomorphism, under these operations. In this paper we prove that the Macaulay inverse system (the Kirchhoff algebra) determined by the basis generating polynomial of the cycle matroid of such a graph has the strong Lefschetz property over a field of characteristic $0$. The proof reduces the non-degeneracy of the higher Hessians to the ranks of disjointness matrices of families of subsets (the Gottlieb--Wilson theorem) and to the representation theory of the symmetric group in relation to the Johnson scheme.

papers.title: Polarization Properties of Thomson-Scattering Triaxial Ellipsoids
papers.abstract: Polarimetry is a powerful tool for constraining the geometry of distant astrophysical objects. Continuum polarization induced by Thomson scattering can probe the photospheric geometry of transients and provide insight into their explosion mechanisms. We systematically study continuum polarization from spheroids over a broader range of deformations and viewing angles than considered previously, and generalize the calculation to triaxial ellipsoids. We find that strongly deformed spheroids exhibit a non-monotonic dependence of polarization on viewing angle, a behavior overlooked in previous studies. Triaxial ellipsoids show more diverse polarization signatures, but their qualitative behavior can be understood from the area of surface elements viewed nearly edge-on, where the local polarization is strongest. Our results provide a simple physical understanding of the dependence of polarization on photospheric geometry and help constrain the geometry of astrophysical transients through polarimetric observations. The computational results of this study will be made publicly available for use in future research.

authors.name: Tomonori Totani
authors.institution: Research Center for the Early Universe

papers.title: A Proof of the Jung-Kim Conjecture on the Centers of Walled Brauer Algebras
papers.abstract: We give a unified account of the five families of Khovanov arc algebras $K_n^m$, $K_n^{-\infty}$, $K_n^{+\infty}$, $K_n^\infty$ and $K_\infty^\infty$ in the framework of level-two tensor product categorifications, making explicit a perspective familiar to specialists. Our main application is a proof of the Jung--Kim conjecture: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the centre of every walled Brauer algebra is generated by supersymmetric polynomials in its Jucys--Murphy elements. We also give a homogeneous basis of the centre in terms of arc diagrams, for the grading induced by $K_\infty^\infty$. The proof combines a calculation of the arc-algebra centre with an explicit comparison of central actions under the Brundan--Stroppel Morita equivalence and Brundan-Kleshchev isomorphism. Along the way, we explain the relation between $K_n^{-\infty}$ and classical super duality, and identify $K_n^{-\infty}$ and $K_n^{+\infty}$ as Ringel duals. We also revisit mixed Schur--Weyl duality for general linear Lie superalgebras within the same framework.

papers.title: Higher-order necessary conditions for nonscattering
papers.abstract: We study the scattering of incident waves by a class of planar analytic inhomogeneities with constant refractive index, governed by the Helmholtz equation. We derive an infinite hierarchy of necessary conditions for nonscattering: any complex analytic nonscattering incident wave must satisfy infinitely many differential constraints at a specific point determined by the geometry of the inhomogeneity. As an application, we show that for any noncircular elliptical inhomogeneity, every single separated (Mathieu) mode necessarily scatters. This is in stark contrast to the circular case, where single separated (Bessel) modes are nonscattering at infinitely many wavenumbers.

authors.name: Narek Hovsepyan
authors.institution: The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley

papers.title: Cayley graphs of abelian groups, circular colorings and discrete fundamental groups
papers.abstract: For each integer $k \ge 2$, we prove that an abelian group $Γ$ satisfies $\exp(Γ) \in \{1,\dots,k\} \cup \{2,4,\dots,2k\}$ if and only if it admits no non-bipartite Cayley graph whose circular chromatic number is strictly less than $2 + \frac{2}{k-1}$. This refines the algebraic characterization by Krebs and Sankar of abelian groups that admit $3$-chromatic Cayley graphs.

papers.title: Optimal Reduced Representatives of Quadratic APN Permutations in Odd Dimension
papers.abstract: The formal derivative of the reduced polynomial representative of a map on a binary finite field depends on the coordinates, although its differential uniformity does not. This matters for lifting permutations to Galois rings: a polynomial over a Galois ring of characteristic a power of two greater than two permutes the ring exactly when its reduction permutes the residue field and the derivative of the reduction has no zero there. We prove that for every odd $n\ge5$, every quadratic almost perfect nonlinear permutation $Q$ of $\mathbb{F}_{2^n}$ admits invertible binary-linear maps $L$ and $A$ such that the derivative of the reduced representative of $L\circ Q\circ A$ has no zero and each of its nonempty fibres has exactly two elements. The range is exact: this fails for $n=3$, as computed earlier, and for even $n$ there are no such permutations. For $n\ge9$, a linearization and a projectively injective cofactor map reduce the problem to counting binary matrices: more than 5% of the invertible inputs $A$ succeed, more than half for $n\ge15$, without any classification. For $n=5,7$ we use two independent classifications and finite certificates. Consequently every such permutation is linearly equivalent to a counterexample to the reduced critical-point conjecture of Bartoli and Stănică that lifts to permutation polynomials of optimal differential uniformity over every Galois ring with this residue field. For odd $n\ge9$ the existence proof is checked in the Lean 4 proof assistant.

papers.title: Coefficient choice in Galois-ring lifts of APN permutations: sharp unit-direction spectra and one-term optimal lifts
papers.abstract: Permutation polynomials over the Galois ring $\mathrm{GR}(2^k,m)$ are nonlinear components for symmetric primitives that add keys in the ring, as in secure computation modulo $2^k$. Rønjom and Sandrib showed that their differential uniformity is at least $2q^{k-1}$, where $q=2^m$. For the class studied here it is attained on top-layer differences, while almost all differences are units. We ask how small the difference table can be on unit differences when the residue permutation is fixed and only higher coefficient digits of its lift are chosen. Let $m\ge5$ be odd, $k\ge3$, and let $p$ be a reduced quadratic almost perfect nonlinear (APN) permutation of $\mathbb{F}_q$ whose derivative is nowhere zero and two-to-one. Over all lifts of $p$, the least possible maximum on unit differences is $q$ or $2q$, decided by two invariants of $p$ and the level $k$. We describe every lift attaining it and show that the coefficients modulo $8$ decide optimality at every level. For every odd $m\ge5$, residue permutations with at most $16$ monomials attain $q$ after one $2$-adic digit of one coefficient of the natural lift is changed. For an explicit infinite family, one added monomial lowers the maximum on unit differences from $4q$, or from at least $q^2$, to $2q$ at every level without raising the degree. Under a uniform starting state and independent uniform round keys, valuation preservation yields layerwise bounds for characteristics and two-round differentials that distinguish lifts with the same global uniformity. Core results are formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: Content associations with answer selection and engagement in supply chain community question answering
papers.abstract: Community question-answering platforms are important ecosystems for knowledge sharing, yet research on what makes an answer best or a question engaging has often focused on either individual lexical features or broad topics. This exploratory study examines both levels in Yahoo! Chiebukuro, asking which nouns and semantic noun clusters are associated with best-answer selection and question engagement. We analyze a large corpus of questions and answer-tier posts collected under the keyword logistics, using an offline machine-translation pipeline with manually validated noun-level fidelity. Best-answer selection is modeled with conditional logistic regression within question threads, controlling for answer length, order, and question-answer noun overlap. Engagement is modeled in two stages: whether a question receives any response and, conditional on receiving one, how many responses it attracts. Operational logistics nouns such as distribution, warehouse, and center are associated with best-answer selection, whereas broader civic and infrastructure nouns such as car, tax, and shinkansen are associated with higher engagement. At the cluster level, most semantic noun clusters are associated with best-answer selection, while the clusters associated with response likelihood and response volume are largely distinct. These findings reveal differentiated content-outcome profiles across answer and question levels and provide a domain-wide descriptive map of engagement and answer selection in logistics-related cQA discourse.

papers.title: Data-Efficient ConvNeXt Pretraining for High-Resolution Sentinel-1 GRD SAR Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Labeled Sentinel-1 Ground Range Detected (S1GRD) datasets remain scarce, limiting supervised deep learning for land-surface remote sensing, while self-supervised pretraining for this domain has been dominated by Vision Transformer (ViT)-based masked image modeling requiring substantial data and compute. We propose SparK-SAR, a sparse convolutional masked pretraining framework built on SparK and ConvNeXt, designed to exploit convolutional inductive biases for S1GRD imagery under constrained compute. SparK-SAR makes three core technical contributions: (i) ConvNeXt-RS, a domain-adapted encoder that halves the stem stride (4x to 2x) to produce 14x14 feature maps at stride 16x, providing 4x more spatial tokens at identical parameter count; (ii) a lightweight ConvNeXt-512 reconstruction decoder with PixelShuffle upsampling that reduces pretraining VRAM by 7.5-8.5% per GPU relative to a UNet-128 baseline while matching its accuracy; and (iii) an empirical characterization of FP16 mixed-precision pretraining instability in the standard SparK UNet-768 decoder on S1GRD data, complemented by a finding that finetuning with layer-wise learning rate decay (LLRD) improves downstream performance of pretrained encoders. On four Copernicus-Bench S1GRD tasks, our finetuned 27.8M-parameter ConvNeXt-RS encoder improves over a non-pretrained baseline by +4.7, +5.0, +5.8, and +1.4 pp on EuroSAT-S1, BigEarthNet-S1, DFC2020-S1, and Flood-S1 respectively, and outperforms the Copernicus-FM ViT (139M parameters, frozen) on three of four tasks at roughly 5x fewer parameters. A pretraining data-scaling study reveals task-dependent data efficiency: classification saturates with as little as 10-25% of the SSL4EO-S12 v1.1 corpus, while dense prediction continues to improve significantly up to 25-50%. The study also includes a CKA representation analysis and a geographic de-collision experiment.

papers.title: Third-moment cancellation and predictable representation in finite-state BSDE approximation
papers.abstract: We study finite-state approximations of Brownian-driven Markovian backward stochastic differential equations when the same one-step increment is used both for weak propagation and for martingale representation. For a centered isotropic state-independent increment with vanishing third moment, we prove first-order convergence of the Markov value field, its spatial gradient, and the predictable $Z$-field under suitable smoothness assumptions. The corresponding orthogonal martingale has maximal $L^2$ size $O(h^{1/2})$. We identify its quadratic representation defect and prove a joint functional limit theorem for the state process and the normalized orthogonal martingale, which in particular yields a mixed-normal terminal limit with path-dependent conditional variance. On the trace-free quadratic sector, the representation defect has the sharp universal operator lower bound $d/[2(d+2)]$; equality holds exactly for normalized laws that are weighted spherical 4-designs. In dimension $d\geq 2$, vanishing third moment is incompatible with exact scalar one-step predictable representation for any finite-state centered isotropic increment. Consequently, every such exact-representation law has a nonzero cubic direction, and a smooth Fourier terminal condition converts this direction into a sharp global $h^{1/2}$ weak error. For the centrally symmetric regular-simplex rule we also identify the leading quadratic GKW component, compute the exact first-order asymptotic of the accumulated orthogonal-martingale variance, and recover it from the general functional limit. Thus the same third-order tensor links weak accuracy and predictable representation, yielding an accuracy-representation tradeoff for finite-state BSDE approximations.

papers.title: Loss-versus-rebalancing with external proportional transaction costs
papers.abstract: We study liquidity provision in automated market makers when trading in the external market incurs proportional transaction costs. We consider both separately collected fees and fees retained in reserves. The benchmark is a self-financing strategy holding the same total risky inventory and trading at the external bid and ask. Under continuous external prices and pure arbitrage, the pool and benchmark have identical liquidation wealth whenever the pool fee or the external spread is positive. Thus loss-versus-rebalancing relative to this transaction-cost benchmark is zero, even without a pool fee if the external spread is positive. We then construct retained-fee utility-indifference pools that implement admissible decreasing inventory schedules, and geometric mean pools that implement feasible constant no-trade boundaries for portfolio weights. These results offer an investment interpretation of liquidity provision: by choosing the pool design, a liquidity provider can specify a trading strategy whose rebalancing is carried out by arbitrageurs.

papers.title: Agentic Dependency Transformations: Lessons from an Exploratory Case Study of Flask
papers.abstract: Modern software relies heavily on third-party libraries, requiring maintainers to balance the benefits of reuse against dependency-related maintenance and risk. We define dependency transformation as an emerging approach in which an AI coding agent alters how a repository handles external dependencies. Local reimplementation is one transformation strategy that recreates required functionality as local code; dependency transformation is broader and may include other strategies. In this emerging-results paper, we report an exploratory case study of Flask to explore dependency transformation strategies. We design experiments that show how available context shapes an agent's dependency discovery and iterative transformation of dependencies. The case yields five preliminary lessons. These lessons and the five-part research agenda position dependency transformation as an emerging research direction and motivate explicit transformation contracts, provenance constraints, preservation requirements, and independent validation criteria.

papers.title: The Role of Agentic Instruction Categories for Code Generation: A Study of Five Python Libraries
papers.abstract: Agentic coding systems increasingly rely on repository-level agent files, such as AGENTS.md, to communicate project knowledge and developer intent. However, it remains unclear which categories of agent instructions enable efficient agent-file generation and accurate code generation. We evaluate five instruction categories: Repository Overview, Function Description, Implementation Detail, Testing, and Reconstruction Steps, across all 31 non-empty combinations using two Large Language Models (LLMs), Gemma 4 and GPT-5.4, and five human-written Python libraries. Our study addresses two research questions, comprising five sub-questions, on agent file generation and code generation. Results show that the number of instructions alone does not determine token usage for agent-file generation, with substantial variation across models and libraries. Although most AI-generated libraries compiled successfully regardless of the instruction combination, functional correctness remained limited. No Gemma 4 variant passed all tests, whereas 12.99% of GPT-5.4 variants did. Function Description achieved Gemma 4's highest partial-pass rate, while Reconstruction Steps achieved GPT-5.4's highest full-pass rate. For structural similarity to human-written code, Reconstruction Steps was most frequently associated with libraries closest to the originals in Lines of File and total Cyclomatic Complexity, while Testing and Reconstruction Steps were jointly most frequent for File Count and Function Count.

papers.title: Fundamental Theorem of Discrete Asset Pricing
papers.abstract: Motivated by discrete price quotes in continuous time, we seek a fundamental theorem based on no arbitrage rather than a condition on limiting trading opportunities. We consider a vector of discounted prices taking values in a locally finite subset of $R^d$ in continuous time. For a locally bounded càdlàg price, we prove that no arbitrage, no free lunch with vanishing risk, no free lunch, and the existence of an equivalent local martingale measure are equivalent. An elementary finite-dimensional reduction of portfolios yields a common pathwise bound on admissible wealth. This bound reduces closedness to convex averaging in a weighted Hilbert space, after which the Kreps-Yan theorem applies. Trading gains are finite Stieltjes sums, and the proof uses no Itô integration.

papers.title: Diffusion Language Models as Open Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Diffusion language models generate text by reversing a classical diffusion process over token sequences. We show that their continuous-time forward and reverse dynamics can be embedded in the framework of open quantum systems, which describes quantum systems interacting with their environment. This connection provides a basis for extending diffusion sampling to superpositions of sentence states and for modifying the underlying generation dynamics. We construct a $τ$-leaping unraveling scheme that simulates stochastic trajectories of these states while updating multiple token positions at each step. This enables generation conditioned on superposed prompts or thoughts, which we call Superposition of Prompts (SoP) and Superposition of Thoughts (SoT). The same formulation yields Quantum-Inspired Remasking (QIR): perturbing the masked-diffusion dynamics produces a confidence-based rule for revising previously generated tokens. Experiments with pretrained diffusion language models show that superposition-based generation can retain information from conditioning components not selected at the final measurement, while QIR improves LLM-assessed text quality when applied at an appropriate stage of generation.

papers.title: Reliability-Aware Refinement of High-Resolution Human Mobility Origin-Destination Tables under Sparsity and Suppression
papers.abstract: High-resolution origin-destination (OD) tables derived from digital mobility traces can preserve fine-scale collective movement structure, but sampling, population expansion, and privacy-motivated low-count suppression create heterogeneous observational support across OD entries and make apparent zeros difficult to interpret. We develop a reliability-aware refinement framework that combines each released OD entry with a time-resolved, data-informed radiation baseline through a closed-form cell-wise Gamma-Poisson update, without smoothing neighboring OD pairs. Applied to a 125 m hourly Tokyo OD product, the method preserves concentrated directional flows while adding lower-intensity, baseline-supported links. The relative contribution of released and model-supported structure varies substantially across OD pairs and departure hours, including among positive-flow entries: released flows are most strongly retained at 7:00, followed by 17:00, whereas the radiation baseline contributes more at 13:00. The inferred characteristic radius broadens the movement range represented by the baseline and exhibits structured variation around major station areas and rail corridors. Tokyo and Fukuoka also show a common increase in data-baseline separation at long distances. Under controlled Poisson thinning, calibrated refinement yields lower realization-averaged mean absolute error than an independently resampled no-refinement table across the tested conditions. This experiment provides internal calibration under imposed degradation, not external validation against true unsuppressed flows. The framework thus provides a transparent way to preserve fine-scale empirical mobility structure while making the cell-wise contribution of structured model support explicit.

papers.title: CM Elliptic Analogue of the Coleman--Ihara Formula
papers.abstract: The Soulé characters are Kummer characters constructed from cyclotomic units and also arising from the Galois action on the pro-$p$ geometric fundamental group of $\mathbb{P}^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$. The Coleman--Ihara formula describes the restrictions of these characters to the local Galois group at $p$ as products of the Coates--Wiles homomorphisms and Kubota--Leopoldt $p$-adic $L$-values at positive odd integers. In this paper, we prove an elliptic analogue of this formula for elliptic curves with complex multiplication by the ring of integers of an imaginary quadratic field $K$. We consider certain Kummer characters associated with elliptic units, which we call elliptic Soulé characters. These characters are elliptic counterparts of the classical Soulé characters and also arise from the Galois action on the pro-$p$ geometric fundamental groups of once-punctured elliptic curves. For suitable pairs of positive integers $(i,j)$, we give an explicit description of their restrictions to the relevant local Galois groups as products of the two-variable Coates--Wiles homomorphisms introduced by Yager and the two-variable $p$-adic $L$-values of $K$.

papers.title: Extinction and the global structure of positive equilibria in a ratio-dependent intraguild predation model
papers.abstract: We study an intraguild predation model with ratio-dependent trophic interactions. We first derive sufficient conditions for consumer extinction, total extinction, and global convergence to biologically relevant boundary equilibria. We then turn to coexistence at equilibrium and introduce a biologically motivated coordinate transformation that reduces the positive-equilibrium problem to an explicitly parameterized one-dimensional curve. This reduction enables us to determine how the positive-equilibrium branch connects to boundary equilibria and to classify all of its admissible global geometries. We also discuss the stability of positive equilibria. Numerical examples suggest the presence of periodic and chaotic coexistence, as well as several forms of multiple attractors.

authors.name: Tzu-Hsuan Chan
authors.institution: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University

authors.name: Chang-Hong Wu

papers.title: Probing Deconfined Quantum Criticality Point on a Digital Quantum Computer
papers.abstract: A deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP) is a continuous transition between ordered phases with unrelated broken symmetries, beyond the Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson paradigm. In one dimension, such a transition between a $z$-polarized ferromagnet (zFM) and a valence-bond solid (VBS) is well established numerically in a frustrated spin-$1/2$ chain. Here we ask whether a superconducting quantum processor can resolve this transition and its signatures despite finite-size effects and device noise. The ground states are prepared by ancilla-projected quantum imaginary-time evolution (QITE), whose exact target states are compressed by tensor-network optimization into shallow depth quantum circuits. The hardware data distinguish the phases through their order parameters, spin and dimer correlations, structure factors, correlation ratios, and snapshot distributions. The crossing of the order parameters locates the transition, and its finite-size extrapolation lies close to the thermodynamic-limit value obtained from large-scale numerics. A noise model based on the device calibration accounts quantitatively for the reduced amplitudes measured on hardware. Our findings demonstrate that a Landau-forbidden transition between competing orders can be resolved on current quantum processors.

papers.title: Synchronization induced by stochastic subsystem resetting in complex networks
papers.abstract: We study synchronization in network-coupled oscillators subject to stochastic resetting of a subset of nodes. We show that resetting can induce collective coherence in oscillators that are never directly reset, through the interplay of network structure, frequency heterogeneity, and the organization of the reset subsystem. In the infinite-resetting-rate limit, the reset nodes become effectively pinned to a reference phase, and linearization near synchronization maps the dynamics of the remaining subsystem onto a grounded-Laplacian problem. This formulation yields an analytical relation between the synchronization level and the reset parameters, providing an estimate of the coupling strength required to achieve a prescribed degree of coherence. Beyond the linear regime, we develop a mean-field description in which the reset subsystem acts as an effective ordering field for the remaining oscillators. Numerical simulations across different network topologies confirm these predictions and show that synchronization is enhanced by increasing both the reset fraction and network connectivity. In heterogeneous networks, the placement of reset nodes can strongly influence the synchronization response. For frequency distributions with nonzero mean, resetting competes with the intrinsic collective rotation and can drive the system from a rotating synchronized state to a phase-locked state. These results establish subsystem resetting as a mechanism for inducing and controlling collective synchronization in complex networks.

papers.title: Per-State Signatures and Mean Time-to-Failure: An Algorithm for Systems With Simultaneous Failures
papers.abstract: We present an algorithm that computes the structural signature and the mean time-to-failure (MTTF) of a monotone binary system at every one of its states, rather than only at the state in which all components work. It makes no assumption on the structure function and evaluates it exactly once per state, as many times as needed for the signature of the complete system alone, so computing the MTTF everywhere costs only a factor polynomial in the number of components over computing it once. As a by-product, it identifies all minimal path sets. We assume exchangeable component failure times whose survivor count is a continuous-time Markov chain. This setting admits simultaneous failures, as in the Lévy-frailty Marshall-Olkin, binomial failure rate and lethal-shock models, where the simplifications available for single failures do not apply. We use the per-state MTTF to define threshold repair policies. We show that the per-state signature is a strictly finer decision criterion than the MTTF: signature dominance at a common failure count implies MTTF dominance, but not conversely. Under the Lévy-frailty Marshall-Olkin model the MTTF is monotone in the state, which yields the long-run cost rate of every threshold policy in a single pass. Experiments on 22 benchmark networks with up to 30 components and 31 failure models show that the best MTTF-threshold policy has a median excess cost of 0.36% over the optimal state-based policy, and that it is never worse than the best policy that repairs after a fixed number of failures.

papers.title: Holomorphy rings and the Nullstellensatz over large fields
papers.abstract: For an infinite field $K$ and an ideal $I\subseteq K[X_1,\dots,X_n]$, let $J(Z_K(I))$ be the ideal of polynomials vanishing on the $K$-rational zero locus of $I$. A Nullstellensatz over $K$ is an algebraic description of this closure operator on ideals. Hilbert's classical theorem provides such a description via the radical of $I$ over any algebraically closed field. In the present article, we introduce a unifying framework for Nullstellensätze over arbitrary rings using the notion of an $A$-radical, for $A$ is a subring of $K(X)$ containing $K[X]$. We show that a single canonical holomorphy ring gives a Nullstellensatz over every infinite field, recovering Hilbert's theorem when $K$ is algebraically closed. In addition, we give a new characterization of large fields (in the sense of Pop) via a particular Nullstellensatz: a perfect field is large exactly when the \emph{rational} holomorphy ring $A_n(K)$--the intersection of all $K$-rational places of residue field exactly $K$--satisfies the corresponding Nullstellensatz. Finally we study the order structure of the class of rings $A$ for which the $A$-radical gives a Nullstellensatz. We show that over non-algebraically closed fields this class has no minimal element, showing there is no optimal Nullstellensatz over such fields.

papers.title: ExecWeave: Cross-Layer Execution Provenance for Observable Agentic Software
papers.abstract: Agentic software invokes tools, launches processes, accesses files, and communicates with local or remote services. Application traces describe logical operations, whereas operating-system telemetry records machine activity without necessarily identifying the responsible agent action. Relating these evidence planes is a reconstruction problem: a plausible but unsupported association can assign an effect to the wrong principal. We present ExecWeave, a local-first system that materializes provider semantics and independently observed runtime events into a typed execution graph. The implementation retains separate source artifacts, distinguishes logical occurrences from repeated evidence, and records attribution, inference, and causal-status metadata. An optional command-to-process correlator emits a non-causal inferred bridge only when its bounded search yields one compatible observed process; uniqueness within this observed candidate set is not a guarantee of causal correctness. OS-observed file and network effects acquire a semantic tool or agent principal only through an observed process plus a justified command-to-process association; session-correlated file-system events do not by themselves provide that principal. Source code is available at https://github.com/Irish-kw/ExecWeave.

papers.title: AutoOnboarder: Autonomously Onboarding LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Agentic large language models have been documented to lose reasoning capability when placed inside a harness, the software that mediates their observations and actions. To reconcile these losses, we introduce AutoOnboarder, an autonomous system that adapts an agent to a task the way a trainer onboards a new employee. It places the agent under the supervision of an intelligent ``Onboarder'' coding agent, which iteratively tailors its foundation model, prompt, and harness source code to simultaneously improve performance and decrease cost. Like a real onboarding process, the Onboarder is only given tens of examples, and all evaluation data is isolated on a separate virtual machine to prevent leakage. We report the lessons learned from building and testing AutoOnboarder on genomic-sequencing prior authorization form submission. Autonomously onboarded agents are able to match or exceed the performance of a Gemini 3.5 Flash baseline at up to 29$\times$ lower costs. However, these agents remain imperfect, and the Onboarding process varies greatly in terms of final performance. We conclude that future Onboarding systems require a robust environment for the Onboarder, including a structured thought interface, (controlled) internet access, and a wide model search space.

papers.title: Regret Lower Bound for Online Learning of Quantum States with Logarithmic Loss, with Applications to Quantum State Tomography and Confidence Sequences for Matrix Means
papers.abstract: We study the problem of online learning of quantum states with logarithmic loss, which is a quantum generalization of online portfolio selection and has applications to quantum state tomography, the task of estimating an unknown quantum state from measurement outcomes. We first establish a regret lower bound, showing that the regret rates of Exponential Weights and the algorithm of Tseng et al. (2025) have optimal polynomial dependence on the dimension. Our analysis leads to two further results. First, our lower-bound proof leads to a quantum state tomography algorithm that is sample optimal up to polylogarithmic factors in the sample size. Second, we develop an algorithm for constructing confidence sequences for the mean of a matrix-valued random variable. A numerical experiment shows that the latter algorithm is competitive with existing methods.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Parallel $M$-Matrix Scaling
papers.abstract: In this paper we consider the problem of computing a positive diagonal scaling of a $d \times d$ symmetric $M$-matrix so that all row and column sums are $1$. We provide a poly-logarithmic iteration algorithm that solves this problem to high accuracy, where the cost of each iteration is dominated by the cost of solving a Laplacian system. This improves upon the recent $\tilde{O}(d^{1/3})$ iteration bound of [Vladu STOC 2025] and yields a randomized algorithm for the problem that runs in near-linear time and poly-logarithmic parallel depth.

papers.title: Measuring the local shape of learning-rate transfer curves
papers.abstract: Understanding the learning-rate (LR) dependence of trained model performance is essential for better optimization of neural networks, but the appropriate size of the LR depends on learning dynamics, architecture, and their hidden biases, and thus our understanding of this complex dependence remains limited. The behavior of the loss curve as a function of the LR has recently been observed in extensive experiments on LR transfer across different settings, such as model sizes, and it is becoming more important to explore methodologies for quantitatively characterizing the shape of this LR curve. In this work, we provide two relational equations that give a good empirical explanation of the gradient of the LR transfer curve, i.e., the LR gradient. One is a theoretical formula that holds at the edge of stability, and the other is an approximate expression obtained by naively treating this gradient as a hyper-parameter gradient. Using these two relational equations in a complementary manner, we show a lower bound on the gradient of the curve and a zero gradient under specific conditions for normalization layers in theory. The approximate expression also applies to a wide range of experimental settings and allows us to decompose the LR gradient into layer-wise components and quantify the strong contribution of specific layers to the curve shape. Thus, this serves as a foundation for better understanding the internal mechanisms of LR dependence.
